\section{Helly projection, guarded no-fill covers and a high-girth obstruction (BH18)}\label{sec:bh18}
The load-bearing obligation remains \ref{obl:progress}. We extend DS18's tree-convex no-fill rule on the actual BD18 pair registry and MS24 deltas, without assuming complete projection-safety recognition. The following are exact typed reductions, not universal coverage.

\begin{lemma}[Exact Helly binary-fill projection]\label{lem:bh18-helly}
In an explicitly acquired binary owner-selector chart with all actual guards absorbed or exactly represented, let $D_i$ be a nonempty live owner domain and $S_i(r)=\{t\in D_i:t\text{ is compatible with exterior row }r\}$. After arc consistency, suppose the family of these supports is Helly: each pairwise intersecting subfamily has a common point. Delete each allowed exterior pair from distinct owners whose supports are disjoint, and remove $i$. The resulting chart is exactly the existential projection of the original chart onto surviving selectors. The hypothesis and the fill are deterministically recognizable in polynomial time in the explicit registry length.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Any original transversal survives. A transversal after fill selects pairwise intersecting, nonempty supports, and therefore has a common row of $D_i$, yielding a lift; the empty selection lifts by any row. Record domain and support maps for reverse reconstruction. At a path-consistency fixed point no new fill is needed. The Berge--Duchet criterion recognizes Helly families: for each three distinct elements $x,y,z\in D_i$, intersect all supports containing at least two of them, and require a nonempty intersection (empty collection intersection $D_i$). These supports meet pairwise, proving necessity. Conversely a minimal pairwise-intersecting family $E_1,\ldots,E_t$ with empty total intersection has $t\ge3$. Choose $x_j$ in all sets except $E_j$, for $j=1,2,3$. The $x_j$ are distinct and every $E_\ell$ contains at least two of them, contradicting the triple criterion. This is a classical Helly recognition argument; see Dourado, Grippo and Safe, \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.12610}{arXiv:2201.12610}. The new integration is binary fill on authenticated owner charts, not a new general Helly theorem. Four supports $\{0,1\},\{1,2\},\{2,3\},\{3,0\}$, together with full supports, satisfy Helly but cannot all induce connected sets on a tree. Any nonempty domain of size at most two is eligible after AC.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Single-pivot guarded Helly no-fill cover]\label{lem:bh18-pivot}
For candidate owner $i$ and another actual owner $j$, for every $a\in D_j$ let $D_a=S_i(a)$. Use the nonempty restricted supports $S_i(r)\cap D_a$ of every row of any other exterior owner compatible with $a$. Require $D_a$ and all these supports nonempty, require intersecting restricted supports for every compatible pair of such rows from distinct owners, and require the family to be Helly. If all pivot rows pass, eliminating $i$ without fill gives the exact existential projection. Failed pair-intersection tests with three live pairwise-compatible rows $a,r,s$ give a certified ternary nogood, not an unconditional deletion of $(r,s)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every surviving exterior transversal selects one actual pivot row $a$. Its other selected rows have pairwise-intersecting restricted supports, hence have a common member of $D_a$. This is the required lift, retaining the actual guard and row IDs. The converse is deletion of an owner from a transversal. If $S_i(a)\cap S_i(r)\cap S_i(s)=\varnothing$, the three rows cannot occur jointly in any original transversal. This forbids $(r,s)$ only within the additional guard selecting $a$ (or symmetrically in either other orientation). A general non-Helly family alone does not prove its offending support sets correspond to compatible rows of distinct owners, much less a globally extendible exterior word.
For strictness over the unconditional Helly test, take $D_i=\{0,1,2\}$ and three exterior Boolean selectors with row-zero supports $\{0,1\},\{1,2\},\{0,2\}$ respectively and full row-one supports. Forbid the first and second exterior zero rows jointly. The full family is non-Helly, but conditioning on the first exterior row satisfies all hypotheses, so the center projects exactly without fill. Restoring the forbidden exterior pair invalidates this center projection. The no-fill condition is sufficient, not a complete safety oracle (cf.\ Lemma~\ref{lem:ds18-nofill}).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Universal raw Helly and single-pivot progress fail]\label{lem:bh18-stall}
Every unpinned linear signed 3-NAE owner registry of minimum variable degree two has non-Helly support families at all owners. If the Berge girth exceeds four, every candidate and distinct pivot fail the single-pivot guarded cover. Both statements continue to hold if one owner admits one additional formerly forbidden word.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For a center owner choose a forbidden word and one neighboring owner for each of its three coordinates, with row matching that coordinate of the forbidden word. The three neighbors are distinct by linearity; their supports are the three coordinate slices of the center domain. Every two intersect because all two-coordinate projections are full, but the total intersection is empty. If girth exceeds four, the three neighboring scopes are disjoint from one another (a shared vertex gives a Berge triangle). When the pivot meets the center, use the pivot as the chosen neighbor of that coordinate. Pick its matching row. The other two neighbor rows are compatible with it and each other, but their restricted supports have empty intersection. When the pivot is disjoint from the center, it meets at most one chosen neighboring scope (otherwise a Berge cycle of length at most four results). Select a pivot row matching that shared coordinate if necessary. The three neighbors are pairwise compatible and compatible with the pivot, but their restricted supports still have empty joint intersection. The required conditions therefore cannot all hold. The same argument uses a remaining forbidden word after the relaxation and full two-coordinate projections. DO01 supplies arbitrarily large critical UNSAT instances and single-budget SAT neighbors in this raw domain. This excludes these particular recognizers even without cap, not scope-changing rewrites, multiple pivots, alternative certificates or unrestricted SAT. In particular the raw statement is not automatically a statement after the BW18 complement quotient.
\end{proof}

\section{Representative row folding and guard-transport firewall (DP19)}\label{sec:dp19}
The target remains Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}. DS18 and BH18 address exact owner projection; BD18 and MS24 provide necessary pair restrictions. We distinguish a decision-preserving representative restriction from a source-support-preserving deduction before combining these operations with DR18's reserve.
\begin{lemma}[Paid single-pivot conditional row replacement]\label{lem:dp19-fold}
In an explicit binary selector registry with all actual guards absorbed or exactly encoded, let $D_i$ be the live owner domains and $N(r)$ the live compatible rows of other owners. For $r\in D_i$, suppose another owner $j$ has the following certificate: for every $a\in D_j\cap N(r)$ there is $s_a\in D_i\setminus\{r\}$ with $a\in N(s_a)$ and
\[
 (N(r)\setminus N(s_a))\cap N(a)=\varnothing.
\]
Deleting $r$ preserves the exact feasible projection onto all owners other than $i$, hence preserves decision. The criterion admits polynomial bit-time discovery and verification in the explicit registry.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every feasible transversal using $r$ selects some compatible $a$ of owner $j$. All other selected rows $t$ belong to $N(r)\cap N(a)$, hence to $N(s_a)$; the pivot row is compatible separately. Replace only $r$ by $s_a$. Every surviving transversal already satisfies the original registry, proving the converse. If there is no compatible pivot row, arc closure already rejects $r$. A completed scan checks all compatible pivot rows, not merely sampled ones. Global neighborhood inclusion is a special case. With $R$ registered rows, enumerate candidate triples $r,s,a$, partitioned by the owner of $a$, using bit-vector containment on $R$ bits; even a naive implementation is polynomial, $O(R^4)$ bit operations per scan with indexed arrays. A cap hit is not a completed certificate. The actual current guard is part of the registry identity.
At fixed declared observation span and original-input cap $B$, the secondary measure $h=$ live rows plus live pair entries strictly decreases; $W=(B+1)(q-1)+h+1$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:dr18-credit} decreases by at least one at unchanged $q$. There are at most $R$ folds, with no reinitialization of the reserve. Apply certified unconditional closure initially, after each accepted move and at stagnation, relative to the actual current chart. Charge all failed scans, certificate verification, pair accesses, retained source and guard maps, and witness replay. A surviving SAT witness is already a pre-fold legal transversal and can use earlier lifts; UNSAT follows by exact projection induction. No count preservation or all-source-model preservation is claimed. With the original polynomial chart cap, serial work, space and cumulative memory are polynomial on this phase; other recursive occurrences must still satisfy the aggregate theorem.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Guard transport and all-shared uniqueness]\label{lem:dp19-firewall}
The fold commutes with every subsequent restriction on exterior rows alone, but does not in general commute with restrictions on the folded owner. Consequently no source impossibility or necessary equation may be exported from a representative chart solely because it holds there. If every coordinate of a raw table owner is observed by another owner, then each feasible exterior selection uniquely fixes its row. A single-owner replacement preserving all exterior rows cannot compress any actually feasible row of that owner.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Exact exterior projection gives the first assertion by intersecting with the exterior restriction. For noncommutation take four owners $X,Y,Z,W$ with domains of sizes $3,2,3,3$, values numbered from zero. Allow $X$--$Y$ when $x=0$ or $x=y+1$; $X$--$Z$ when $z=0$ or $x=z$; $Y$--$Z$ when $z=0$ or $z=y+1$; $Z$--$W$ when $w\ne(z+2)\bmod 3$; other pairs unrestricted. Replace $x=0$ by $x=y+1$. This is certified by the previous lemma, though no global domination exists in the initial registry. There are twelve transversals before and eight after the fold; imposing $x=0$ is satisfiable before and unsatisfiable after. Thus source-wide necessary facts require independent source certificates or a proved transport invariant. The uniqueness assertion follows from equality on the actual overlaps and distinct row words: every coordinate of the owner is already fixed by the exterior. This is why multiowner or scope-changing normalization, not merely row substitutions, is necessary for genuine representative compression in all-shared raw charts.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Raw linear NAE folding obstruction]\label{lem:dp19-stall}
An unpinned linear signed three-uniform NAE registry of minimum variable degree two has no single-pivot folding certificate of Lemma~\ref{lem:dp19-fold} in its raw six-row selector representation.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Fix distinct candidate rows $r,s$ of one owner and a compatible pivot row $a$. Choose a coordinate $v$ where $r,s$ differ and another owner $k$ containing $v$. If $k$ is the pivot owner then $a$ agrees with $r$ at $v$, excluding $s$. Otherwise a row of $k$ may be chosen agreeing with $r$ at $v$ and with $a$ on their at-most-one common coordinate. The at-most-two pins are consistent and extend to signed NAE. By linearity this row belongs to $N(r)\cap N(a)$ but not $N(s)$. Thus no alternative $s$ passes. This proof concerns raw tables, not arbitrary learned pair registries; other certified nonlocal rules may escape the obstruction. It is not an unrestricted lower bound.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Executed comparison and provenance.}
On exactly the five BD18 states and MS24 combined symmetric pair deltas (with original GD24/BS17/S23 lift maps and the three distinct M23 guards), check mask subset and symmetry, then run arc closure before each scan. No new arc deletions. All ten full global-dominance scans found none; all ten single-pivot scans reached the cap of 250000 replacement tests each without a certificate. No peer fold was applied, no independent source-lift replay or post-MS24 path/affine closure rerun. On 100 seeded five-owner ternary binary CSP controls (74 SAT, 26 UNSAT), 227 folds including 58 conditional preserve exact decision by exhaustive reference enumeration; the four-owner example has twelve then eight then five transversals, and the opposite-label pinned control verifies noncommutation. Fano and deletion have zero and ten transversals and no fold. The 4092040 assertions mostly check pair-mask symmetry, not independent proof steps. No formal kernel, complete portfolio, native compiler or physical cumulative memory measurement. \href{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/2cc714cf9bca3ac152eb36b47d27f1d77044b147}{Report}, \href{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/9f4ff3c421300730cff9837610414fd457c001b7}{checker}, \href{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/5f38a442dd8e5d418e1eb80c5ffa7c0114dd63aa}{results and immutable input references}.

\section{Two-alternative exterior cover and block representative normalization (BS18)}\label{sec:bs18}
DP19's pivot-dependent replacement preserves exterior projection but not all original support. The following complementary certificate permits multiple alternative rows or bounded blocks without a designated pivot.
\begin{lemma}[Certified bounded block cover]\label{lem:bs18-block}
In an explicit binary selector CSP with actual guards absorbed or encoded, fix an owner block $H$ of size $h$ and a compatible internal tuple $a$. Let $N(a)$ be the live exterior rows compatible with every row of $a$. For distinct compatible alternatives $b_1,\ldots,b_t$ on $H$, put $B_i=N(a)\setminus N(b_i)$. If no selection of one row from each $B_i$ is mutually compatible (allow the same row to be reused, forbid distinct rows of the same owner), deleting the internal tuple $a$ preserves exact feasible projection onto the exterior owners. For fixed $h,t$ this sufficient certificate admits polynomial discovery and replay in the explicit encoded chart.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
A feasible exterior transversal compatible with $a$ but with none of the alternatives would select a blocker for every alternative, and the selected blockers would be mutually compatible. Thus every exterior word formerly extended by $a$ extends by a surviving alternative. Every retained transversal was previously feasible. Enumerate at most $R^h$ compatible internal tuples, at most $R^{ht}$ ordered alternatives, and at most $R^t$ blocker choices for $R$ registered rows; all pair accesses, membership and guard checks use explicit bit-polynomial work. If $h=1$, deletion removes a row; if $h=2$, it removes a symmetric pair. At fixed declared span and fixed polynomial cap, these are strict DR18/BD18 secondary-credit reductions without reserve reset, with closure after each accepted move. For $h>2$ a paid higher-arity representative registry and its exact consumers are additional obligations; no free translation to pair masks is asserted. A surviving witness needs only the earlier authenticated source lifts. Representative-only restrictions must be versioned separately from necessary deductions, by DP19's firewall. No count preservation is asserted.
\end{proof}
For $h=1,t=2$, blockers $B,C$ have no compatible selection exactly when $C$ is disjoint from $B\cup\bigcup_{z\in B}N(z)$. This bitset test includes single dominance ($B=\varnothing$). For a strict fixed point of global single dominance, use center $A=\{a,b,c\}$, binary $X,Y,Z$: $a$ accepts either $X$ but only $Y=0$; $b$ accepts $X=0$ and either $Y$; $c$ accepts $X=1$ and either $Y$; impose $Y=Z$, other pairs unrestricted. No row has a same-owner support superset. Nevertheless deleting $a$ preserves every feasible exterior word, by the alternatives $b,c$. Exhaustive control: six then four transversals, all four exterior words retained. This is not a claim of strict superiority to DP19's pivot rule.
\begin{lemma}[Unbounded complete cover recognition barrier]\label{lem:bs18-star}
Deciding whether deleting a specified universal center row preserves all exterior words is coNP-complete on explicit binary stars with independent Boolean leaves.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Given a 3-CNF $F$, take one binary leaf per variable, a center row $a$ compatible with every leaf value, and an alternative center row per non-tautological clause, compatible exactly with its falsifying assignments (one allowed bit on each occurring variable, both on absent variables). All leaf pairs are unrestricted. After deletion of $a$, a leaf word extends exactly when it falsifies a clause. Thus preservation of every exterior word is equivalent to UNSAT of $F$. A missing exterior word can be checked against every remaining center row in polynomial time. The star before deletion is trivially SAT, so this is not an unrestricted decision lower bound. Complete coverage acquisition cannot be assumed polynomial in a proof of P=NP.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Raw bounded-cover obstruction]\label{lem:bs18-stall}
Every unpinned linear signed 3-NAE registry of minimum coordinate degree two defeats the $h=1,t\le2$ certificate in its raw six-row selector representation.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For each alternative choose a coordinate on which it differs from the target row. If the chosen coordinates agree, choose one exterior owner containing that coordinate and a row agreeing with the target; it blocks both. If they differ, choose respective exterior owners, distinct by linearity. Each agrees with the target on its sole shared coordinate. If these exterior owners intersect, their at-most-one common coordinate is not either target coordinate, and one can prescribe a common bit on it. Signed NAE has full two-coordinate projections, so both compatible blocking rows exist. The argument with one alternative is immediate. This includes DO01 critical raw cores under the degree hypothesis, not arbitrary post-normalization charts or unrestricted algorithms. More generally, if all coordinates of a block are observed outside it, a feasible exterior transversal uniquely determines its internal tuple, so no actual feasible tuple can be replaced while preserving that exterior. A scope-changing or sufficiently large block must escape this invariant.
\end{proof}

\section{S24: Charged pair-block fusion and an explicit-fusion barrier}\label{sec:s24}
The target is U-PROGRESS (Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}), not a further fixed-scope terminal catalogue. Extend DP19 exterior-preserving replacement and BH18 Helly elimination to an authenticated scope-changing operation on the same BD18/MS24/BH18 charts. All prior guards must already be enforced by the exact selector registry.
\begin{lemma}[Exact pair-block representative fusion]\label{lem:s24-fusion}
In an explicit binary owner-selector registry, merge distinct owners $A,B$ by enumerating their allowed row pairs $(a,b)$. Give each pair the exterior neighborhood $N(a)\cap N(b)$ restricted to other owners. Retain one actual pair per maximal neighborhood under inclusion, leaving all exterior-exterior edges unchanged. The merged chart has exactly the same existential projection onto all exterior rows, and every satisfying merged transversal lifts to an original one.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
An original transversal chooses a compatible pair and exterior rows contained in that pair's neighborhood. The neighborhood is contained in some retained maximal neighborhood, so substituting the retained actual pair preserves all exterior rows. Conversely, each retained row is an actual compatible pair and each exterior edge certifies both old edges, hence expansion is legal. Store the actual original row IDs and concatenate disjoint owner-lift lists. Counts and full internal support are not preserved in general. As in DP19, new guards on removed representatives are not transportable without separate proof; no representative restriction is a source impossibility. Reclose with certified unconditional rules initially, after each accepted deduction/merge and at stagnation.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Fixed-cap growth credit]\label{lem:s24-credit}
Fix a polynomial row cap $C=C(N)$ in original input length before dispatch. For nonempty admitted charts let $B=C+\binom C2$, $h$ be live rows plus undirected live pair edges, and $m$ the live owner count. The integer
\[
\psi=(B+1)(m-1)+h+1
\]
strictly decreases on support deletions and on every accepted pair-block fusion staying within $C$, even if $h$ increases to $B$. Empty domain is a terminal. With outer base credit $q$ from S23 and $M=(B+1)C+1$, $W=M(q-1)+\psi$ contracts on same-$q$ moves as above; if $\sum_i q_i\le q-1$, then $\sum_i W_i\le M(q-1)<W$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
$1\le\psi<M$ since $m\le C$ and $h\le B$. A merge lowers $m$ by one and increases $h$ by at most $B$, so lowers $\psi$ by at least one; a deletion lowers $h$. Each trial enumerates at most $C^2$ pairs, and comparing all their bit-vector neighborhoods costs $O(C^5)$ bit operations, plus polynomial graph rebuilding, closure, guard/source verification and provenance. There are at most $C^2$ owner pairs per complete scan. Charge every failed/capped scan, old and new graph simultaneously, reconstruction lists, all accesses, and each actual outer occurrence. On the admitted phase this gives polynomial serial time and peak space on the same execution and $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$. The cap cannot be reset at fixed $q$; no other same-$q$ owner increase is covered. The outer inequality follows from $W_i\le Mq_i$. A decline is not a decision.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Explicit fusion-only obstruction]\label{lem:s24-fusion-barrier}
Even for satisfiable explicit binary selector registries of polynomial size with no forced bits, every sequence that completes by pair fusion of actual row tuples, exterior-support-preserving maximal-neighborhood deletion and support-preserving closure can require superpolynomially many live rows. More precisely, for the family below every complete binary merge tree has a block requiring $2^{\Omega(n)}$ rows.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Use one owner per edge of $K_n$, with all four assignments to its two endpoint bits; compatibility is equality on shared endpoints and unrestricted otherwise. All global words are legal, and initial arc closure changes nothing. A binary tree on $L=\binom n2$ edge owners contains a block of between $L/3$ and $2L/3$ leaves (descend through a child exceeding $2L/3$; then take the larger child). Let $D$ be vertices touched by both block and complement. Vertices exclusively inside and exclusively outside cannot coexist, because their connecting edge would violate one exclusivity. Thus one side has all its edges inside $D$, so $\binom{|D|}2\ge L/3$ and $|D|=\Omega(n)$. Inductively all assignments to bits occurring in at least two current blocks remain attainable: extend each new shared-bit assignment to old shared bits, take a premerge transversal, and retain its entire exterior selection using Lemma~\ref{lem:s24-fusion}. Every new shared bit occurs in some unchanged exterior block, so its value is preserved. Support-preserving closure cannot remove these transversals. At the balanced block every boundary-bit word occurs, and every actual row tuple fixes one such word. At least $2^{|D|}$ rows are necessary, even after dominance. Initial explicit input is polynomial in $n$. This refutes universal completion of this explicit fusion-only procedure under any fixed polynomial row cap, not arbitrary SAT, factored projections, or native tetravalent normalization; the constructed instances are trivially SAT.
\end{proof}
A separate nonincrease obstruction applies to raw unpinned linear signed NAE3 with minimum variable occurrence degree three: two owners have 18 compatible tuples if they share one bit, 36 otherwise. Every pair coordinate is seen by an exterior owner. That owner intersects the pair in at most two coordinates, and any consistent two pins extend to NAE. Distinct pair tuples differ on such a coordinate; their nonempty neighborhoods at the exterior owner are disjoint, so no containment is possible. The resulting domain has more than the original twelve rows. Thus row growth or another operation is necessary even at the initial raw stage; learned charts are not covered by this obstruction.

\section{DO19: Basis-invariant disjunctive factor discovery and arbitrary affine guards}\label{sec:do19}
The S24 explicit-fusion barrier motivates changing representation rather than growing row tuples. DO15's coordinate-support graph need not discover independent dual observation spaces in a dense basis. Here we prove a paid acquisition rule for a specified class, not U-PROGRESS.

\begin{lemma}[Basis-invariant full product acquisition]\label{lem:do19-atoms}
Suppose an explicit deduplicated nonempty registry consists of all Cartesian tuples of $s\ge2$ lists of nonempty positive-rank forbidden affine packets. The factor observation spans $U_j$ form a direct sum in the dual vector space. Each factor has at least two distinct packet row spaces, pairwise intersecting only in zero within that factor, with one affine packet per space. Then the factorization can be recovered in deterministic polynomial bit time in any invertible coordinate basis, without knowing the factors.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Form and deduplicate all nonzero pairwise intersections of parent packet row spaces, retaining the inclusion-minimal ones. Each intersection is the direct sum of the factor spaces on which the two tuples agree. Every individual factor space is attained alone by holding that factor fixed and changing all the others. Therefore the minimal nonzero intersections are precisely those spaces. Two different atoms occur together in a parent space iff they belong to different factors. Noncooccurrence, with equality, is the equivalence relation giving the groups. Verify the equivalence relation, the direct-sum ranks of the group spans, exactly one contained atom per group in each parent, and that the sum of the restricted equations including their affine right-hand sides reproduces the original canonical packet. A failed verification declines. Deduplicate the resulting labeled tuples and verify that their cardinality equals the product of their projected list cardinalities. As every tuple belongs to this product, equality proves full product coverage without enumerating more tuples than the input. The tests themselves are sound on arbitrary input; the stated promises guarantee discovery. There are quadratically many pair intersection candidates in the number of parent packets, with polynomial Gaussian elimination, containment/cooccurrence, dictionary and integer arithmetic costs. Reconstruction uses actual dual basis maps and Gaussian solution, not an assumed coordinate-disjoint representation. No complete semantic key is required. Missing tuples or overlapping atom spaces can cause decline.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Arbitrary affine guard on a disjunction]\label{lem:do19-guard}
Let $F=\bigvee_j F_j$ with each $F_j$ depending only on its observation space $U_j$. Let a consistent affine guard have rowspace $H$ and right-hand-side functional $g:H\to\mathbb F_2$. Then guarded decision is exactly the disjunction of local decisions with projected guards $g|_{H\cap U_j}$. Projecting each guard and lifting a winning local word costs polynomial Gaussian operations, independent of the numerical rank of the guard.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
A local word is a linear functional $f$ on $U_j$. It extends to the original guard iff $f=g$ on $H\cap U_j$. Necessity follows by restriction; sufficiency follows by defining the functional $h+u\mapsto g(h)+f(u)$ consistently on $H+U_j$ and extending it to the full dual space. Gaussian elimination computes both the intersection and a witness lift. In a disjunctive branch the other $F_i$ need not hold; the extension imposes no other regional constraints. The disjunction of the local guarded decisions is therefore exact. This argument does not permit independent guard projection for conjunctions or for the all-block sparse-hole terms of GD21. Indeed arbitrary 3-CNF is uniformly equivalent to independent single-clause blocks on fresh occurrence copies subject to an affine equality guard identifying copies of each original variable. Each block individually is trivial; joint guarded conjunction is NP-complete. Independent projected guard checks on conjunctive blocks need not compose.
\end{proof}

For Lemma~\ref{lem:do19-atoms}, the parent conjunction of tuple avoidances equals $\bigvee_j F_j$. Keeping the authenticated unabsorbed parent chart with actual guard, write $M$ for parent rank mass, $M_j$ and $m_j$ for factor mass and list size. Then
\[
 M=\sum_j M_j\prod_{h\ne j}m_h\ge2\sum_jM_j,\qquad
 \sum_j(1+M_j)\le M=(1+M)-1
\]
since every $m_j\ge2$ and $M_j\ge m_j$. This pays all children with $c=1$ on the stated chart domain; projected guards add no avoidance packets and substitution/closure cannot increase child avoidance rank mass. This inequality is not claimed relative to an already rank-reduced parent. Preserve exact guard and source maps, charge retaining/reconstructing the unabsorbed representation and all failed scans, and do not reset any outer credit. Run certified forced-information closure initially, after deductions and at stagnation; quotienting or other rewrites may leave the recognition domain, in which case an equivalent retained representation requires paid provenance. Under a fixed original-input polynomial size cap the admitted step costs polynomial bit time and peak space; $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$ on the same execution. Universal availability of such a step is OPEN.

\section{DA19: Exact neighborhood-code quotient and nonlinear residual rank}\label{sec:da19}
The target remains Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}. S24's actual tuple fusion may grow exponentially and DO19's factor recognition declines on the same five connected pair charts. RT24's component equations are necessary but not sufficient. Instead factor exact exterior behavior into shared labels without merging owner tuples. All actual guards must already be encoded in the explicit binary selector registry.
\begin{lemma}[Exact neighborhood-code quotient and paid projected enumeration]\label{lem:da19-code}
After certified arc closure, partition the rows of each owner $i$ for each other owner $j$ by equality of live neighborhoods in $j$. Compatibility is constant on every product of two classes. If the reduced bipartite class graph is a matching covering both sides (the original relation is a union of disjoint complete bipartite components), use common binary class-label bits for this pair, numbering matched classes identically. Complete relations need no bits. Otherwise use independent binary labels on each side and retain the explicit table of allowed class pairs. For each owner store the distinct concatenated incident class-label words and one actual row representative per word. The resulting owner and pair factors are exactly decision-equivalent to the original registry, with polynomial acquisition and reconstruction in explicit chart length.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every original transversal induces a compatible label word. Conversely each owner table supplies an actual row, and each shared label or class-pair factor guarantees compatibility for every representative in the indicated classes by the definition of neighborhood equality. Thus an actual transversal reconstructs, followed by earlier source lifts. This is exact on the projection to label words, not necessarily on internal representative values; DP19's guard-transport firewall applies. New restrictions on removed representatives require a separate proof.

For each deduplicated factor $T$ compute its affine hull from differences to an anchor. It is exact iff $|T|=2^{\dim\operatorname{aff}T}$. Collect all hull equations into $Ax=b$; inconsistency rejects. Let $J$ be the union of scopes of the factors that are not equal to their hulls. For a consistent system the residual observation rank is
\[
 r=\dim\pi_J(\ker A)=|J|-\operatorname{rank}A+\operatorname{rank} A_{\bar J}.
\]
Indeed the kernel of that projection is the nullspace of $A_{\bar J}$. Find a projected kernel basis with stored full preimages by Gaussian elimination. Enumerate the $2^r$ projected words of the affine solution set, one full lift per word, testing the nonaffine tables exactly. The affine factors hold automatically; the nonaffine tests depend only on $J$. A passing word lifts by the first part; exhausting the projected support rejects. Independently, a factor row outside the projection of $Ax=b$ onto its scope cannot occur in a legal solution and may be deleted with a Gaussian certificate and original class map. Reclose after accepted deletions and at stagnation; row/edge removals must be transported to actual row IDs before changing the active representation.

For $m$ owners and $R$ original live rows the number of label bits is $O(m^2\log(R+1))$, total owner rows at most $R$ and pair table entries at most $R^2$. Dense acquisition, deduplication, hulls, rank and projection checks are polynomial in explicit chart length $L$. The decision cost is $2^r\operatorname{poly}(L)$, hence polynomial in original $N$ only on a fixed polynomial chart cap and a fixed logarithmic bound on $r$. All discovery, unsuccessful checks, prior acquisition, guard and source maps, and witness verification are paid. On this admitted serial execution peak space is polynomial and $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$. Use the representation as scratch unless an independent aggregate credit check permits committing it: no reset of DR18 or S24 reserves. Strict certified deletions in the original row/edge registry pay repetitions; no universal strict deletion or logarithmic rank bound follows.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Label-independent nonaffinity and raw-rank obstruction]\label{lem:da19-barrier}
A nonrectangular binary relation cannot become affine under separate injective encodings of its two sides. Every raw unpinned signed linear 3-uniform NAE registry of minimum variable occurrence two has only rectangular pair relations but the minimal binary neighborhood-code construction has residual rank $r=n$ on its $n$ occurring variables.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Affine relations are closed under ternary XOR; three allowed corners of a rectangle imply the fourth. This implication is invariant under separate injective encodings. In the raw NAE chart each nontrivial pair shares precisely one coordinate and its class label is that bit, possibly complemented. Each owner observes all its three bits through its incident classes, so its code has six distinct words, not a power of two, and is nonaffine even under other injective encodings. The six raw NAE words have full affine hull on the three bits; the hull of the repeated binary labels thus imposes precisely agreement (with possible complements) between their copies. Global hull equations identify exactly all labels observing the same actual variable, since the owners observing a variable form a clique of pair links. All variables remain free in that hull, and every label is in a nonlinear owner scope. Thus $r=n$. Growing registries defeat a universal logarithmic residual-rank theorem for this adapter, irrespective of all pairs being rectangular; other representations, nonlinear deductions, factored algorithms and unrestricted decision are not excluded. Rectangularity and affine tractability are standard in CSP theory; compare Bulatov--Dalmau, \href{https://doi.org/10.1137/050628957}{A Simple Algorithm for Mal'tsev Constraints} (2006). Pair rectangularity alone supplies no common polymorphism for all owner tables.
\end{proof}

\section{M25: Conflict-clique Hall certificates and a universal relaxation obstruction}\label{sec:m25}
The target is Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}, not another assumption of universal coverage. DA19's exact neighborhood labels, RT24's selector hulls and BH18's guarded pair exclusions can feed a different primal/dual matching relaxation on the original row IDs without fusing tuple charts. Work in a fixed explicit binary row/pair chart with actual guards already applied. Higher-arity constraints may be omitted only for a necessary relaxation, not for positive decision.
\begin{lemma}[Certified Hall projection]\label{lem:m25-hall}
Let the live selector rows be partitioned into buckets, each containing pairwise incompatible rows, where different rows of the same owner count as incompatible. Form a bipartite graph from owners to buckets incident to their rows. Every legal transversal induces a matching saturating the owners. A Hall deficiency certifies UNSAT; a deficiency after restricting an owner to a single incident bucket certifies deletion of every row of that owner in that bucket. The converse need not hold. A supplied or deterministically greedily acquired partition is polynomially verifiable, including all pair conflicts and the Hall neighbor set. No maximum clique oracle is used.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
A transversal uses one row per owner and cannot use two rows in a bucket. Thus it maps injectively into buckets. A deficient set $X$ with $|N(X)|<|X|$ precludes any such map. Restricting an owner to a bucket covers every candidate row of that owner in the bucket and yields the stated guarded certificate; a contradiction under that guard entails the corresponding unconditional deletion in the current chart. Failed augmenting-path search supplies the reachable owners and buckets as a Hall witness. Positive matching solutions are only relaxation witnesses; actual row pair checks and source lift remain mandatory. This is the classical all-different matching filter of Regin (AAAI 1994) applied to authenticated conflict buckets rather than a predeclared value domain.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[All conflict-clique partitions stall on raw linear NAE]\label{lem:m25-barrier}
For every unpinned signed linear 3-uniform NAE registry with three distinct variables per owner and no additional pair exclusions, assign weight $1/6$ to each of its six rows. Every conflict clique has total weight at most one. Consequently every partition into conflict cliques has an owner-saturating fractional matching with strictly positive flow on every incident owner-bucket edge. Bipartite matching integrality implies every such edge extends to a saturating matching. No root Hall contradiction or single-row Hall deletion is possible in any of these partitions, on SAT or UNSAT instances, even if a partition is acquired by an unlimited search. More generally the complete system of clique capacity inequalities and owner one-hot equalities admits this strictly positive vector.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
If a clique meets only one owner it has at most six rows. If it meets $k\ge2$ owners, every pair of such owners must intersect, and all clique rows from one owner must disagree on the shared coordinate with all rows from the other. Thus each such coordinate is constant within an owner's clique rows. Three of these owners cannot share one coordinate because three binary values cannot be pairwise different. Linearity implies that an owner meets its $k-1$ other clique owners in distinct coordinates; hence $k\le4$. For $k=2$, at most three NAE rows per owner have a specified coordinate value. For $k=3$, at most two rows per owner have two specified bits; for $k=4$ at most one row per owner has three specified bits. The clique size is therefore at most six in every case (respectively $6,6,4$). Signs do not change these bounds. Send the weight of each row to its bucket; every owner has sum one and every bucket sum at most one. The integral bipartite matching polytope decomposes this fractional vector into saturating matchings, so every positive edge appears in at least one. This proves the obstruction for arbitrary partitions and all clique inequalities, not for arbitrary guarded probes, additional pair exclusions, nonlinear constraints or changed representations. In particular it is not a complexity lower bound on unrestricted SAT.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Charged integration.}
For $R$ rows and $m$ owners, verify partitions in $O(R^2)$ pair checks; the two deterministic greedy orders use polynomial scans and bitset work. At most $R+1$ matching queries per partition, each using at most $m$ augmenting searches over at most $R$ distinct edges. Hall certificates carry the exact current row IDs, bucket partition, pin and neighbor set. Reclose AC before initial acquisition, after each accepted deletion batch and after imported deltas; no semantic oracle. A strict row deletion spends existing fixed-span DR18/BD18 credit, never resets it. Under a fixed original-input polynomial chart cap, at most $R$ strict batches and polynomial scratch/certificate costs; all failed probes and prior acquisition paid, peak space polynomial and $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$ on the same serial run. No guaranteed strict decrease; decline is UNKNOWN. Pair-pin and higher-arity consumers not implemented here.

\section{GD25: Guarded bijunctive block contraction and the two-sided pin firewall}\label{sec:gd25}
Target Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} and S24's explicit fusion-only barrier, using the actual BD18/MS24/BH18 guarded selector states. A block can be removed without materializing its entire exterior support if the exterior demands are literal pins on a bijunctive internal core.
\begin{lemma}[Exact arbitrary-size bijunctive block projection]\label{lem:gd25-block}
In an authenticated explicit binary owner-selector chart with all actual guards enforced, choose a nonempty block $H$ of owners. Supply injective Boolean codes for its rows, of polynomial total bit length. Suppose each internal domain and each internal allowed-pair relation is exactly definable by 2-CNF on the corresponding disjoint code bits. For each exterior row $r$ and internal owner, its compatible internal rows must be exactly the domain restricted by a conjunction of code literals (or empty). Let $T$ be the conjunction of internal formulas, and $U(r)$ the union of pins required by $r$. If $T$ is inconsistent the chart is UNSAT. Otherwise remove $H$, reject $r$ when its required support is empty or $T\land U(r)$ is inconsistent, and reject any remaining exterior pair $r,s$ when $T\land U(r)\land U(s)$ is inconsistent. The resulting binary chart is the exact existential projection onto exterior owners. A witness lifts by solving 2-SAT under the actual exterior pins, decoding and checking the original rows, then applying authenticated upstream lifts.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every original transversal survives these necessary tests. Models of a 2-CNF are closed under coordinatewise majority: if the majority falsified a clause of at most two literals, one of the three models would falsify both. Over satisfiable $T$, an inconsistent unit set has a minimal inconsistent subset of size at most two. Otherwise choose three models of $T$ omitting three distinct literals respectively from that minimal subset; their majority satisfies every literal, contradiction. Now every single and pair of exterior assumption sets is consistent, so any contradictory one- or two-literal subset of their union is impossible. The entire union extends in $T$; exact internal coding and cross pin checks give the desired lift. This also covers empty exterior, where $T$ alone decides. No internal counts or later guards on eliminated representatives are preserved without separate replay.
\end{proof}
Recognition on a supplied code is polynomial: collect all absent unary and binary bit words of every explicit table, form the induced 2-CNF, and compare its complete model set to the supplied rows using exact pin-feasibility prefix search, stopping at the first non-table word. With $R$ distinct rows on $w$ bits, at most $R+1$ feasible leaves and $O(w(R+1))$ queried prefixes including failed siblings are needed. Exact feasibility uses the implication graph (Aspvall--Plass--Tarjan, 1979, \href{https://doi.org/10.1016/0020-0190(79)90002-4}{DOI}). Cross-pin recognition takes all fixed coordinates among the compatible rows and verifies equality with their restriction of the domain; any valid pin description is a subset of those coordinates. A deterministic candidate heuristic starts with all recognized domains, removes an offending owner upon a failed internal-pair or exterior-pin test, and repeats at most $m+1$ times; no completeness over choices or alternative codes. On a fixed original-input polynomial chart/code cap, all recognition, failed scans, pair tests, graph construction, replay, decoding, access and source lifts are paid. The move deletes at least one owner and never adds exterior rows or edges, hence strictly decreases S24's same-span reserve without reset. Polynomial same-execution $T,S$ and $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$ for this admitted phase, not the whole solver. Closure initially, after imported and accepted deductions, and at stagnation. For the S24 $K_n$ all-four-row edge-owner example, code the actual endpoint bits; internal equality is 2-CNF, exterior rows pin actual shared bits, and existing exterior consistency already enforces all projected conditions. Any block can be removed without exponential explicit fusion. This is an exact bypass of that representation obstruction, not a universal progress proof.

\begin{lemma}[Code-independent two-sided pin obstruction]\label{lem:gd25-pin}
Let $D$ be a nonempty bijunctive Boolean code domain, with an arbitrary decoder onto an actual Boolean relation $R$. If, for each actual coordinate, both value fibers on $D$ are definable by conjunctions of code literals, then $R$ is bijunctive (in particular majority closed). This holds even with arbitrarily many auxiliary code bits. Thus no code with these properties can represent signed NAE on three actual exposed bits.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For a nonconstant decoded bit the two pin conjunctions $U,V$ are individually feasible on $D$ but jointly infeasible. The two-pin property in the previous lemma implies that some $u\in U,v\in V$ cannot hold together on $D$. Every first-fiber word satisfies $u$, every second-fiber word falsifies it. Since the two fibers partition $D$, this actual bit is exactly a code literal (up to polarity) on $D$. Constant bits are harmless. Taking the majority of three code witnesses therefore commutes with decoding every actual coordinate, proving closure of $R$. Ordinary NAE excludes the majority $000$ of its three single-one words; signed NAE follows by coordinate complementation. In a raw linear signed NAE registry of minimum occurrence degree two, each coordinate of a single owner is exposed separately by another owner allowing both values, so its two exterior fibers must be representable by pins. Thus every singleton fails regardless of code. More generally an all-exposed block with non-majority-closed actual accepted projection cannot meet the two-sided pin property. This does not exclude other guard languages, larger private-coordinate contractions, or unrestricted SAT.
\end{proof}

\section{Guarded ordered-row implication hull and structural wheel escape (BW19)}\label{sec:bw19}
\begin{lemma}[Paid ordered-row binary hull and guarded SCC closure]\label{lem:bw19-hull}
Fix an actual guarded explicit pair chart with $M$ owners and $R$ registered rows, one live row selected per owner and symmetric compatibility masks. After certified semijoin closure, order each live domain of size $d_i$ deterministically. Its row index $a_i\in\{0,\ldots,d_i-1\}$ is uniquely encoded by the chain bits $z_{it}=[a_i\ge t]$, $1\le t<d_i$, with implications $z_{i,t+1}\Rightarrow z_{it}$. For each threshold literal $\ell$ on owner $i$ and each distinct owner $j$, let $U$ be the union of actual $j$-neighbors of all live rows of $i$ satisfying $\ell$. It is nonempty by semijoin closure. Put $l=\min U$, $h=\max U$ in $j$'s order and add
\[
\ell\Rightarrow [a_j\ge l],\qquad \ell\Rightarrow [a_j\le h]
\]
when nontrivial, with contrapositives. This is exactly the conjunction of all binary threshold exclusions implied separately by the actual pair relations, together with the row chains. Every legal transversal satisfies it. A contradictory implication SCC certifies guarded UNSAT. A satisfying SCC model decodes to an actual row at each owner; accept SAT only after all original pair masks and the necessary source lifts are verified. If local hulls equal their actual pair relations, this is an exact terminal; all domains of size at most two are a special case.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Each threshold literal describes a prefix or suffix of its row order. Its allowed target indices are precisely $U$; a target threshold half has empty intersection with $U$ exactly when it lies strictly outside the appropriate extremum. Thus the two strongest bounds imply all such binary exclusions, in both orientations, and are necessary. Chain monotonicity gives a bijection with row indices. Contradiction is sound; a verified tuple is sufficient for chart feasibility, with authenticated reverse map required for source feasibility. Testing all local row pairs against their local hull clauses certifies exactness without semantic global equivalence. For two-row lists each forbidden pair of choices is itself one binary clause; singleton lists have already been propagated by semijoin closure.

Compute each row's minimum and maximum neighbor in each other domain, followed by prefix/suffix extrema. There are $O(R^2)$ pair entries to inspect and $O(MR)$ implication insertions (plus chain edges); all actual indices and bit masks have polynomial bit size in the explicit chart. Standard SCC computation decides the resulting 2-CNF. Recompute after each accepted deduction, and before a row probe reclose the chart to a fixed point. A probe pins an actual row, applies semijoin closure and reconstructs its ordered hull. A contradictory SCC or empty domain rejects that row in the parent chart only, retaining its actual outer guard; it does not imply an unconditional source fact outside that guard. A satisfying relaxed tuple that fails verification is OPEN. Testing every row of one chosen hub costs at most $R$ probes; $q$ pinned owners cost at most $R^q$ assignments for fixed $q$, not for unrestricted $q$. A fixed polynomial probe cap and strict deletion of a registered live row pay DR18/BD18 same-span secondary reserve without reset. Charge all failed probes, graph construction, replayable SCC paths, row maps, guard checks, prior acquisition and source lifts; serial polynomial peak space implies $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$ on the same realization. There is no universal guarantee of strict progress.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Odd-wheel escape and all-orders raw linear NAE root obstruction]\label{lem:bw19-wheel}
On the explicit three-color disequality wheel, pinning the hub and reclosing gives two choices per rim vertex, so Lemma~\ref{lem:bw19-hull} decides that chart exactly. An odd rim is refuted under every hub color and an even rim is satisfiable. Raw pair path consistency does not detect the odd wheel. Conversely, for every raw linear signed NAE-3 chart on distinct variables with six rows per owner and pair relations given only by shared-coordinate equality, the unpinned root ordered hull is satisfiable for \emph{every} choice of local row orders, even on critical UNSAT sources.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
In a wheel, every compatible pair extends to any third owner because at most two of three colors are forbidden. After a hub pin, AC removes that color from each rim domain, but cannot detect the odd cycle of opposite-color requirements. The exact two-choice implication cycle rejects it; enumeration of the three hub rows is polynomial and covers all possibilities. This resolves the RT24 odd-wheel obstruction within the stated chart model, preserving the actual hub-row maps.

For the second claim, in each six-row domain choose a middle index (2 or 3, zero-based). Every threshold half containing it has size at least three. Each actual coordinate has three zero and three one rows, and distinct coordinate bipartitions differ even up to complementation because all two-coordinate patterns occur in signed NAE. Thus a homogeneous threshold half containing a middle row must have size exactly three, and there is at most one coordinate split into homogeneous first-three and last-three halves in that order. Choose the middle row in the zero half of that coordinate if such a split exists, otherwise choose either. Every selected threshold half then admits value zero on every coordinate. Two owners sharing one coordinate have a compatible pair between any such two halves (choose zero in both); disjoint owners have universal pairs. Consequently every selected threshold pair satisfies the necessary exclusions. This yields a root hull model, not necessarily an actual transversal, and falsifies universal unguarded hull refutation. No bound against guarded probes, alternative feature maps, native nonlocal normalization or unrestricted algorithms follows.
\end{proof}

\section{Horn projection and coupled-consumer obstruction (DR19)}\label{sec:dr19}
The missing step in Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} is not just elimination of an owner block, but the cost of consuming its exact exterior relation. GD25's binary inconsistent-assumption theorem uses a specifically bijunctive hypothesis; it cannot be generalized to all polynomial-time internal decision languages.

\begin{lemma}[Paid Horn block projection]\label{lem:dr19-horn}
Let a guarded block be exactly compiled to a Horn CNF $T$ on $v$ internal bits, with total literal occurrences $L$. Each exterior row $a$ supplies an authenticated set of internal literal pins $U(a)$. Given an actual exterior transversal, define the positive and negative pin flags as the union of these demands. There is a uniformly constructible monotone rejection circuit in these flags of size $O((v+1)(L+v+1))$, not counting the polynomial cost of collecting row flags, which accepts rejection exactly when $T$ plus all pins is inconsistent. A nonrejecting transversal lifts in polynomial time. This is an exact factored consumer, not in general an explicit unary/pair projection.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Write every Horn clause as a rule $B\to h$ or $B\to\bot$, with $B$ a conjunction of positive variables. Start the forward state with the positive pin flags; repeatedly add all heads whose bodies are true. After at most $v$ rounds it is the least model of the definite rules. A goal body true in this model or a negative pin intersecting the model certifies contradiction; otherwise the least model satisfies the complete system. Unroll $v$ rounds as AND/OR gates, keeping the old bits and collecting rule bodies, plus the final goal/negative-pin tests. Gate indices and pin maps require polynomial bits and all accesses are paid. Recompute or retain the least model for the actual witness lift and verify the original relations, including upstream lifts and the actual outer guard. This assumes the stated exact compilation, not mere Horn relaxation. The projected constraint preserves exterior support only; additional pins on forgotten internal bits require replay. A factored consumer must remain in the state and its storage, calls, guard versions and reverse maps must be included in a new reserve or the per-occurrence bound; it cannot be discarded or counted as an already solved child.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Exponential explicit fill and NP-complete composition]\label{lem:dr19-fill}
For every $k\ge1$ there is a linear-size Horn 3-CNF block (in variables/occurrences, with polynomial bit encoding) with $2k$ Boolean exterior positive-pin flags whose rejection relation is $\bigwedge_{i=1}^k(a_i\lor b_i)$. Its minimal inconsistent positive-pin sets number $2^k$. Any exact CNF over those flags alone needs at least $2^k$ clauses. Furthermore, deciding whether some exterior transversal is accepted by a negative Horn 3-CNF pin consumer is NP-complete even when all exterior owners are independent two-row choices, each supplying a single positive pin.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Use $a_i\to c_i$ and $b_i\to c_i$ (flags seed the corresponding internal variables), then a binary conjunction chain deriving a final variable from all $c_i$, and forbid that final variable. The least model rejects exactly when every pair is hit. Minimal rejected flags select exactly one per pair. Two distinct such words have an accepted coordinatewise meet. The falsifying assignments of a single non-tautological clause are closed under meet, so a clause valid on every accepted word cannot reject two distinct minimal rejected words. Each must be rejected by some clause, yielding the lower bound. It concerns an explicit exterior CNF or enumeration of all minimal inconsistent pin sets, not arbitrary factored circuits or affine packets.

For the second assertion, take an arbitrary 3-CNF $F$. For variable $x_i$, create internal rails $p_{i,0},p_{i,1}$ and one independent exterior owner choosing which rail to pin true. Include the Horn goal $p_{i,0}p_{i,1}\to\bot$. For each source clause, include a goal whose body consists of the rails for its falsifying literals. A full exterior choice forces exactly its selected rails in the least model; it is rejected precisely when a source clause is false. Thus compilation is uniform polynomial, and source assignments are recovered from exterior choices, with both decision directions exact. Membership in NP follows by guessing the choices and running the paid Horn check. The Horn block without pins has the zero model, and the independent binary owners alone are trivial; the joint problem is the original SAT instance. This is a noncircular reduction, not a separation or a claim that all solvers must use this representation. It refutes the proposed inference from separately tractable modules and a compact exact consumer to a jointly polynomial terminal without a new structural hypothesis.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Exact polarity-renaming test and raw obstruction]\label{lem:dr19-rename}
For an explicit binary row chart with nonempty live owner domains, use Boolean selection variables $y_a$, one positive coverage clause per owner, and a negative binary clause for every cross-owner incompatible pair. At-most-one clauses within an owner may be omitted: any satisfying selection can be reduced to one row per owner, preserving all cross compatibility. This encoding is renamable Horn precisely when there are polarity flags $f_a$ satisfying $(f_a\lor f_b)$ for every distinct same-owner pair and $(\neg f_a\lor\neg f_b)$ for every cross-owner conflict. Recognition and solution are polynomial via 2-SAT followed by Horn forward closure. A conflict $K_{2,2}$ on two rows of each of two owners refutes every such polarity renaming; in particular any intersecting pair of raw linear signed NAE-3 owners has this obstruction.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
After flipping variable $y_a$ when $f_a=1$, every coverage clause must have at most one positive literal, and no negative conflict clause may have two positive literals; these are exactly the two displayed constraint types. A $K_{2,2}$ has an edge between the flipped rows, since at least one of the two rows on each side must flip, contradicting the second constraint type. Raw shared-coordinate equality has a $K_{3,3}$ across opposite coordinate fibers. After ordinary semijoin closure, any successful renaming even gives a simple witness: choose a flipped row from every domain of size at least two; these have no cross conflict, and singleton rows are compatible with all other live rows. Thus this is not a general UNSAT refuter after AC. Decline is not a decision; extra constraints beyond the pair chart must still be checked, and no source witness is accepted without the authenticated lift.
\end{proof}

\section{BD19: Factored forest guard projection and the joint-consumer obstruction}\label{sec:bd19}
S24's explicit tuple fusion barrier and GD25/BW19's fixed-code eligibility failures motivate retaining exact factored exterior predicates instead of materializing exterior tuples. The source remains the authenticated binary owner-row chart, with actual guards encoded exactly. This is not universal progress.

\begin{lemma}[Exact factored projection of an induced forest]\label{lem:bd19-forest}
Form the owner graph with an edge iff a pair of live rows of the owners is forbidden. Let $B$ induce a forest, with each component rooted. For every exterior row $s$ use a Boolean selection input $z_s$. Define, for internal row $r$ of owner $i$,
\[
 A_i(r)=\bigwedge_{\substack{s\text{ exterior}\\(r,s)\text{ forbidden}}}\neg z_s,\qquad
 D_i(r)=A_i(r)\land\bigwedge_{j\text{ child of }i}
       \bigvee_{t\in R_j:\,(r,t)\text{ allowed}}D_j(t).
\]
The output $\bigwedge_{i\text{ root}}\bigvee_{r\in R_i}D_i(r)$ is exactly the feasibility of the block under the indicated exterior pins. Under a full legal exterior transversal it is exactly the existential projection of the block. Exterior exact-one constraints and exterior compatibility constraints must be retained.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Induction in postorder proves that $D_i(r)$ means that row $r$ admits a compatible subtree assignment under all indicated exterior vetoes. Every distinct child subtree has complete cross-subtree compatibility, because an extra constrained edge would violate the forest promise. Thus their witnesses glue. The same argument joins roots. For a true output choose a true root row in each component and a true compatible child row at each step, then verify against actual masks, exterior pins and the retained source maps. For a partial set of pins, setting the other selection inputs to zero tests only block extension under those pins, not the feasibility of unselected exterior owners. A false result certifies a necessary nogood within this exact chart; a true result is not a global SAT certificate. A representative-only deletion from DP19 is not a source nogood.
For $R$ total live explicit rows, the veto lists, compatibility lists and postorder recurrence use $O(R^2)$ gates and wires including binary fan-in expansion and constants, with polynomial bit indexing, discovery, verification, and reverse lift. Across disjoint blocks with no internal cross-block constraints this one-pass bound still holds by charging original row pairs and actual consumers. Graph construction and greedy induced-forest recognition are polynomial; maximum forest optimization is not assumed. A fixed polynomial explicit original-size chart cap makes each such attempt polynomial. Charge failed attempts, all probes and source verification. A necessary row/pair deletion pays the DR18/BD18 fixed-span reserve; no deletion gives no new free attempt. Projecting owners away does not remove the new factored constraints or their consumers, and subsequent projection through these circuits requires a separate theorem. On the admitted serial operations, peak storage is polynomial and $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$. No universal bound for the remaining exterior decision follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Exponential explicit positive-pin nogoods despite a linear guard circuit]\label{lem:bd19-nogoods}
For each $k\ge2$ use one internal owner with rows $r_1,\ldots,r_k$ and $2k$ binary exterior owners $a_i,b_i$. Only the active row $a_i=1$ or $b_i=1$ vetoes $r_i$. All exterior pairs are compatible. Its exact projection is $\bigvee_i(\neg a_i\land\neg b_i)$. There are precisely $2^k$ minimal inconsistent positive-pin sets, one choice of $a_i=1$ or $b_i=1$ per pair; all proper subsets extend. Yet the circuit has $O(k)$ size. Initial arc closure is stagnant. This is a lower bound on listing all these nogoods, not on arbitrary representations or decision.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
An internal row survives iff neither corresponding active pin is present. All rows are blocked iff each pair contributes at least one active pin; inclusion minimality is exactly one per pair. The displayed circuit is the direct recurrence. With $k\ge2$, each exterior row supports an internal row and each internal row supports some row of every exterior owner.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Joint consumer decision remains NP-complete after singleton projection]\label{lem:bd19-consumer}
Polynomial-size local factored projection and an edgeless remaining binary owner graph do not imply a polynomial decision terminal. Joint composition of the projected predicates is NP-complete even when each eliminated block is one owner with three rows and each exterior owner has two rows.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Reduce arbitrary 3-SAT with three distinct variables per clause. Use one binary exterior owner per variable, and one independent three-row internal owner per clause, whose rows name its three literals. A literal row is incompatible only with the exterior row falsifying that literal. No pair constraints between internal owners or between exterior owners. This exact polynomial compiler preserves both labels and witnesses: a satisfying assignment chooses a true literal in every clause, and any legal transversal has all chosen literals true. Arc closure is initially stagnant: each literal has a compatible variable value, and each exterior row has a compatible literal choice in every clause since each clause has distinct variables. Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:bd19-forest} to every internal singleton. The remaining exterior pair graph is edgeless, but its factored constraints are exactly the original clauses expressed via the one-hot exterior selections. Checking a candidate exterior transversal is polynomial, so joint decision is NP-complete. Antitonicity in selected-row inputs is not monotonicity in the actual free Boolean variables because exact-one couples the two inputs. Therefore a decreasing owner-count potential or bounded local circuit size, without a separately established joint-consumer solver or aggregate bound, cannot discharge Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}. This is not an unrestricted time lower bound.
\end{proof}

\section{I25: Gauge-stable joint occupancy and conditional phase acquisition}\label{sec:i25}
Target Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}, not free acquisition of a compact consumer. DA19's neighborhood labels, M25's Hall relaxation, GD25/BW19's bijunctive blocks and BD19/DR19's forest/Horn consumer barriers motivate checking whether actual chart gauge and peer deductions can cooperate. Use the explicit guarded owner-row registry, including all supplied factor constraints.
\begin{lemma}[Paid elementary-abelian stabilizer and representative contraction]\label{lem:i25-gauge}
For each owner whose live rows admit a supplied or explicitly verified fixed-point-free involution, assign one flip bit; otherwise fix it to zero. With explicit factors of maximum fixed arity $k$, the subgroup $K\le\mathbb F_2^m$ of these owner flips preserving every factor can be found in polynomial bit time. If $r=\dim K$, choose $r$ owners whose coordinate projection on $K$ is bijective. Restrict each such owner to the canonical orientation of each of its two-row orbits. This preserves decision exactly and leaves one representative per $K$-orbit of solutions, each of size $2^r$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Enumerate the at most $2^k$ flip masks on each factor scope $I$ and verify relation invariance (for a sparse forbidden list, test invariance of the list under the bijection). Its stabilizer $H_I$ is a subgroup of $\mathbb F_2^I$. Embed its annihilator equations in the global owner-flip coordinates, also setting ineligible owner bits to zero. The kernel is precisely the intersection of inverse projections of these stabilizers, not the entire semantic automorphism group. Gaussian elimination finds a basis and free coordinate columns giving a bijective projection. For any solution, the unique gauge vector with prescribed values on these columns changes its orientations to the canonical ones. Nonzero gauge vectors cannot fix a row transversal, because each eligible involution is fixed-point-free. The resulting solution is still a solution of the original explicit chart; the archived action and source map allow witness recovery. Reclose after the representative restriction. This is an equisatisfiable restriction, \emph{not} an unconditional forced row deletion or a certificate preserving all original models. Further source constraints must be checked for invariance before using this as an exact source transformation.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Orbit completion of entailed peer exclusions]\label{lem:i25-orbit}
Let $K$ be a certified symmetry group of the unanchored chart under its actual fixed guard. Every exclusion of a tuple $\tau$ on scope $I$ that is entailed by that chart has all its translates under $\pi_I(K)$ entailed as well. Replacing a batch of such exclusions by its orbit closure retains the stabilizer $K$; the monotone arc/unit-closure fixed point retains it too. For fixed arity $k$ each exclusion requires at most $2^k$ images, regardless of global gauge rank.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
A counterexample to a translated exclusion maps under the inverse symmetry to a counterexample to the original. Project a Gaussian basis onto $I$, enumerate only that projected span, and translate actual row IDs. The full orbit of a forbidden tuple is invariant. Arc support and unit nogood deletion are equivariant; the greatest fixed point of these monotone domain reductions is invariant. The same argument does not apply to a branch restriction or to deductions made only in a chosen representative slice: a conditional fact transports both guard and conclusion. An image under a non-stabilizing guard change cannot be used as an unconditional exclusion. A hidden constraint must be included or proved invariant. Do not assume an upstream certificate merely because a peer reports a numerical deletion.
\end{proof}
An asymmetric but entailed cut can destroy the syntactic stabilizer without changing the semantic solution set. The two lemmas permit complementary acquisition before anchoring. Under a fixed original-input polynomial chart cap, all scans, rejected symmetry probes, projected masks, Gaussian equations, closure, guard checks, maps and source verification are charged. At most $R$ strict anchor steps for $R$ initial rows; original row/pair exclusions spend existing credit. New explicit arity-$k$ exclusions require a fixed $O(R^k)$ tuple reserve on the same original row IDs (deduplicate and never reset on scope changes), or charged scratch followed by a verified outer descent. The row/edge-only reserve does not pay arbitrary new factors. Time and peak space on this admitted serial run are polynomial, and $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$ at step boundaries. Universal nonzero gauge rank is false: genuine pins can destroy it, and a connected raw linear NAE registry with one-bit overlaps has only simultaneous complement in this action. Rank one does not imply logarithmic residual width.
\begin{lemma}[Conditional XOR consumer and selection barrier]\label{lem:i25-phase}
In a binary owner-row chart invariant under simultaneous complement with two-row orbits, fixing an orbit index at each owner leaves a polynomial exact phase problem. But selecting a compatible orbit word is NP-complete even if every projected pair relation is full, each owner has at most three orbits, and the sole phase constraints are conditional binary XOR equalities. This holds after fixing a reference phase to zero.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For any orbit pair the four phase pairs are partitioned into the two XOR fibers by simultaneous flip. An invariant nonempty relation is one fiber or both. Thus fixed orbit indices give a signed graph solved by Gaussian elimination or parity union-find, and actual rows reconstruct. If the graph of all potentially forced edges is a forest, any projected word lifts; in general the selected cycle syndromes must be jointly consistent.

For hardness, take an explicit 3-CNF with three distinct variables in each clause. Make one reference owner and one owner per source variable, each with one two-row orbit. Each clause owner has three two-row orbits indexed by its literal selection. Require equality of reference and clause phases. For a clause orbit selecting literal $x_i$ (respectively $\neg x_i$), impose $p_i+p_{\rm clause}=1$ (respectively $0$) on its pair with variable owner $i$; impose no restriction on other variable pairs. All remaining pairs are free. Each projected pair is full, and all phase relations are simultaneously complement invariant. A legal transversal gives a satisfying source assignment $x_i=p_i+p_{\rm ref}$ because the selected literal of every clause is true. Conversely a source model selects one true literal per clause and extends to phases with $p_{\rm ref}=0$. Tables, verification, and lifts are polynomial; membership in NP follows from actual row selection. This is a barrier to the proposed automatic joint phase consumer, not an unrestricted lower bound and not a strict native-port compiler. Even an empty projected binary graph and individually exact XOR consumers do not discharge U-PROGRESS.
\end{proof}
