\section{Exact attainable veto signatures and their universal obstruction (DS19)}\label{sec:ds19}
\begin{lemma}[Paid full-transversal signature composition]\label{lem:ds19-veto}
In an authenticated explicit binary owner-row chart, let $A$ be processed owners and $P$ a valid partial transversal of $A$ (one live row per owner, all internal pairs allowed). Its signature $V_A(P)$ is the union of its rows' conflict neighborhoods restricted to the exterior live rows. Partial transversals of the same $A$ with identical signatures have identical compatible exterior transversals. An exact table with one representative per signature can be extended by owner $j$: for each signature $V$ and live row $r$ of $j$ not in $V$, retain a representative for
\[
 (V\cup N(r))\cap\{\text{live rows outside }A\cup\{j\}\}.
\]
An empty completed table proves UNSAT; a final representative proves SAT of the binary chart. Alternatively, join two child tables on disjoint owner blocks by testing representative compatibility and restricting the union to the new exterior. The latter compatibility is invariant under replacement by either child's signature-equivalent representative.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Across the cut the only remaining tests are whether an exterior selected row is in the signature. Internal feasibility is already verified. For the one-owner step this proves both directions by induction. For a two-child join, compatibility with a fixed opposite representative is a signature test, and replacing the opposite representative in turn is also a signature test. Union of signatures determines the new exterior veto. No representative removal is a necessary row deletion.
\end{proof}
Fix original input length $N$, a fixed polynomial chart-size cap, and $K=(N+2)^c$ for fixed $c$. Stop each attempted table acquisition at $K+1$ distinct signatures, discarding the partial table and returning DECLINE for that attempt. A deterministic adaptive ordering can test each remaining owner and retain the smallest completed next table, with fixed tie-breaking. If all attempts overflow, decline, never infer UNSAT. For $m$ owners and $R$ registered rows there are at most $m(m+1)/2$ attempts and at most $KR$ row trials per attempt; three simultaneous tables of at most $K+1$ entries and their polynomial-size representatives suffice. Even naive exact mask comparison, discovery, initial and repeated certified closure, failed attempts, and source verification/lift are polynomial on an admitted chart. A supplied binary decomposition similarly costs at most $K^2$ pair trials per node. This is a paid terminal when it completes, not a universal strict child contraction; do not reset credit at representation switches or repeat failed identical attempts for free. On the same serial realization, $T,S$ are polynomial for the capped attempt and $CM\le(T+1)S$.
If the cross-conflict matrix has binary rank $r$, the union of supports of chosen rows equals the union of supports of any basis of their span. Thus the number of attainable signatures is at most the number of subspaces, bounded by $(r+1)2^{r^2}$ (count ordered generating lists of length at most $r$). A supplied decomposition with $r=O(\sqrt{\log N})$ across every cut suffices for polynomial tables, not for uncharged discovery. This is a specialization of neighborhood-union/Boolean-width DP (Bui-Xuan, Telle and Vatshelle; reference below).
\begin{lemma}[Paid adapter for factored consumers]\label{lem:ds19-gate}
The polynomial-size Boolean guard circuits of BD19 and DR19 can be combined with a binary exterior owner chart by introducing Boolean flag owners and constant-size gate truth-table owners. Each flag is linked to the corresponding exterior row-selection indicator; equality constraints link all occurrences of actual wire bits; output bits are pinned. The new chart is equisatisfiable with the exact joint consumers and supports polynomial gate and source-lift verification, provided the original circuits and maps are polynomial-size. Charge all flag, gate, pair, guard-version and lift objects against the fixed original-size cap; this does not establish a universal table-size bound.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
An exterior transversal determines the selection flags, and evaluating all gates gives a legal extension exactly when all required output pins hold. Conversely the equality constraints and gate tables force actual circuit evaluation on those same flags. Thus every accepted extension restricts to a valid exterior tuple. Acyclic evaluation and the previously proved consumer reconstruction maps suffice for lifting. The number of gate rows is constant per gate and explicit pair compatibility construction is polynomial in the expanded chart. Without compilation or equivalent exact treatment, pair-only signatures cannot justify merging in a higher-arity chart.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Universal attainable-key cap is false]\label{lem:ds19-expander}
There are polynomial-size binary owner charts for which every owner order and every binary owner decomposition has a cut with exponentially many attainable veto signatures, even after complete semantic singleton/pair closure.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Take a bounded-degree edge-expander $G$ on $n$ vertices, with one Boolean owner per vertex and forbid only pairs of adjacent ones. Every row and every allowed pair extends by setting all other bits to zero, so complete pair closure is stagnant. Every balanced cut $A|B$ has $\Omega(n)$ crossing edges. Greedy induced matching selects a crossing edge and discards every crossing edge incident to either endpoint or their neighbors, at most $2(D+1)D$ edges for degree bound $D$. Hence there is an induced matching of size $\Omega(n)$. Choose any subset of its $A$ endpoints as ones and all other $A$ vertices zero. This is internally feasible, and the corresponding $B$ endpoint's one-row is vetoed precisely when its matched $A$ endpoint was chosen. The resulting $2^{\Omega(n)}$ signatures are distinct. Every order has a balanced prefix, and every binary owner tree has a cut with both sides of size at least $n/3$. The explicit chart bit length is polynomial in $n$. This excludes a fixed polynomial cap for full exact signature tables on these unchanged registries, not other representations or solvers: all zeros is an immediate SAT witness and the constraints are 2-CNF.
\end{proof}

\section{MS25: Component parity closure in unary feature space}\label{sec:ms25}
Attack Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} on the same BD18/MS24/BH18 charts and I25 representative anchors. DA19's class quotient and I24's source-coordinate moments motivate retaining all additive unary Boolean features without committing a larger active registry.
\begin{lemma}[Complete additive pair-hull relaxation and paid projection]\label{lem:ms25-component}
For each live row $a$ introduce a formal binary coordinate $z_a$. Every legal transversal obeys $\sum_{a\in R_i}z_a=1$ for each owner $i$. For the bipartite graph of allowed row pairs between owners $i,j$, impose for every connected component $C$
\[
\sum_{a\in C\cap R_i}z_a=\sum_{b\in C\cap R_j}z_b .
\]
These equations, with the owner equations, describe exactly the affine hull of each pair table in one-hot coordinates. Their global conjunction is a sound relaxation. Its inconsistency rejects; an exact one-hot row or pair outside the corresponding affine projection can be deleted. All discovery, projection and replay are polynomial in an explicit polynomially capped chart, with strict deletions paid by DR18's fixed reserve. Consistency does not certify SAT.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
A pair edge contributes its two endpoint unit vectors. In each connected component their linear span is the even-weight subspace: path sums generate every pair of vertices. The affine hull consists of odd sums of edge vectors; the parity on either owner equals the number of edges used modulo two, so the displayed equations plus an odd owner sum are necessary and sufficient for the pair hull. Isolated rows vanish under the component equation; empty relations reject. Every actual transversal belongs to every such hull and to the combined system. Gaussian elimination finds the combined rowspace, tests inconsistency, and computes its affine projections by intersecting the augmented equation space with each owner or pair coordinate subspace. The projected one-hot tests therefore preserve all actual guarded words and source maps. These are all linear constraints obtainable by summing arbitrary unary features of allowed pairs, not all nonlinear compatibility constraints.
For $R$ live rows and $m$ owners, graph acquisition scans at most $O(R^2)$ pairs and generates at most $O(R^2+m)$ equation rows; dense bit Gaussian elimination and $O(m^2)$ projections have polynomial cost. At most $R+\binom R2$ strict deletions occur; reclose certified unconditional constraints initially, after each accepted deduction batch and at stagnation. Extra explicit factors remain charged; ignoring ternary factors except for unit closure is a safe weakening, not deletion of their consumers. One-hot coordinates are scratch, not an active chart expansion or reserve reset. All guards, previous source compilation, accesses, failed tests, provenance, prior and later consumers, old/new storage and reconstruction are charged. The admitted serial execution has polynomial time and peak storage, hence $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$. No guarantee of a strict move follows.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Cooperative gain and a universal-progress counterexample]\label{lem:ms25-stall}
There exist binary pair charts on private three-bit rows where BD18 path consistency and MS24 source-coordinate conditional affine closure both stagnate but Lemma~\ref{lem:ms25-component} rejects. Conversely, the latter rule alone stagnates on every raw unpinned linear signed NAE-3 registry.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Use four owners on $K_4$. In each owner list its eight private three-bit words in order $(0,1,2,4,3,6,5,7)$. The index $t$ encodes two feature bits $u=\lfloor t/4\rfloor$, $v=\lfloor t/2\rfloor\bmod2$ and a nuisance bit. Give the three incident edges the features $(u,v,u+v)$, complementing the last feature at owner 3 only. Require feature equality along each edge. All single-feature fibers have four affinely independent source words (the XOR of the four is nonzero), and every pair of feature values occurs. Thus a pivot imposes only its own pins in MS24, and any two compatible rows extend to a row at each third owner in BD18. But the pair component equations enforce each feature equality on the formal unary moments, while the sum of the three feature functions at each owner is its fixed parity times the odd owner sum. Summing yields $0=1$. The all-even neighbor has $2^3$ compatible edge words and $2^4$ nuisance choices, hence 128 actual models.
For raw linear signed NAE, a pair is complete or shares exactly one source bit, so its component equations are precisely the corresponding bit agreement (in addition to odd owner sums). Each six-word owner has full affine hull on its three bits; every source-bit word has a formal odd combination of its local rows realizing those bit moments. In particular any locally compatible row pair extends to a global relaxed word by choosing a source-bit word agreeing with those two rows and odd combinations elsewhere. Thus every live row and pair survives, even on raw UNSAT charts. This falsifies universal progress of this relaxation, not unrestricted decision. I25's XOR phase consumer still requires actual compatible orbit selection; a parity vector is not a witness.
\end{proof}

\section{BA19: Integer component hull, modular forcing and its raw obstruction}\label{sec:ba19}
Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} remains open. Extend MS25's component parity relaxation to signed integer masses on the same actual row IDs, including I25 representative guards. This is not nonnegative integral occupancy and not an unrestricted SAT decision terminal.
\begin{lemma}[Exact pair-table integer affine hull and paid modular rejection]\label{lem:ba19-lattice}
For an explicit binary owner-row chart, with live domains $R_i$, every legal transversal has one-hot coordinates $z_a$ satisfying
\[
 \sum_{a\in R_i}z_a=1,\qquad
 \sum_{a\in C\cap R_i}z_a-\sum_{b\in C\cap R_j}z_b=0
\]
for each connected component $C$ of the actual bipartite allowed-pair graph on $R_i,R_j$. For each individual pair table these equations, restricted to its two owners, describe exactly the integer affine lattice of its one-hot edge vectors. The analogous statement holds over every field and every commutative ring with identity. Global signed-integer feasibility, including any specified one-hot row or pair pin, is a polynomial-bit-time necessary test. A failed test permits rejection under its actual guard; passing it does not certify SAT.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Orient the bipartite edges from left to right. Marginals of an affine combination of edge vectors with coefficient sum one satisfy the displayed equalities. Conversely in each connected component use a spanning tree and eliminate leaves, assigning the signed edge coefficient required by the corresponding marginal and subtracting it from the neighbor's remaining demand. The final root demand vanishes by component balance. This works over the integers without division (also over the stated rings); the coefficient sum is total left mass one. Isolated vertices require zero. Coefficients need not be nonnegative. Stack the component equations globally as $Az=b$; append exact one-hot pins when testing a row or pair. Polynomial-bit-complexity Smith/Hermite normal form is available by Kannan and Bachem, \href{https://doi.org/10.1137/0208040}{Polynomial Algorithms for Computing the Smith and Hermite Normal Forms of an Integer Matrix} (1979). For unimodular $U,V$ with $UAV=D$, divisibility of $(Ub)_i$ by nonzero $D_{ii}$ and vanishing of the remaining entries is necessary and sufficient for signed integer feasibility. Reduction mod a fixed prime and Gaussian elimination are cheaper sound rejection tests. No factorization of unbounded moduli, nonnegative integrality or full semantic closure is assumed.
\end{proof}
For $R$ live rows the explicit pair graph occupies $O(R^2)$ bits up to indexing overhead and generates $O(R^2+m)$ component/owner equations. At most $O(R^2)$ one-/two-owner pins per sweep; normal form and certificate replay polynomial in explicit input. Under a fixed original-$N$ polynomial chart cap, each strict deletion spends one original row/edge credit, with at most $R+\binom R2$ strict deletions for the fixed initial registry; no reset on reencoding. Charge all unsuccessful probes and rebuilds, exact guard/source authentication, storage, reconstruction maps and consumer calls. Reclose certified AC and available guarded unit nogoods after each accepted deduction batch, initially and at stagnation. Scratch mass variables do not enlarge the active chart. Polynomial serial $T,S$ on this admitted domain imply $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$ on that same realization. This is not a global potential for arbitrary scope-changing charts or branches.
\begin{lemma}[Characteristic-three gain beyond all binary component projections]\label{lem:ba19-fano}
Take the Fano lines $\{u,v,u+v\}$ on nonzero vectors of $\mathbb F_2^3$, but let each owner accept exactly-one rather than NAE. Every compatible row and pair survives MS25's complete GF(2) component projections; the GF(3) global relaxation rejects at the root. All seven single-line-deleted sources are SAT.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Pair components identify the formal moment $x_v$ of each shared coordinate. Each owner imposes $\sum_{v\in e}x_v=1$. Sum the seven line equations to obtain $3\sum_v x_v=7$, impossible modulo three or over the integers. Over GF(2), choose $x_v=1+\ell(v)$ for a linear functional $\ell$. An actual one-hot line word prescribes a linear functional on its two-dimensional span, since its complement has even parity. Any compatible pair prescribes functionals agreeing on the intersection, so they extend to a common functional on the ambient space. The local mass of each row is the corresponding coordinate moment. Thus all compatible pins survive even at the binary component fixed point. Deleting one line yields the actual witness selecting exactly its three vertices, since each other line meets it once. No claim that other portfolio methods stall on the root.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Raw linear signed NAE survives the entire signed-integer pair hull]\label{lem:ba19-barrier}
For every unguarded linear signed NAE-3 registry, every actual row and compatible actual row pair survives the signed-integer component feasibility tests in Lemma~\ref{lem:ba19-lattice}, and hence their reductions modulo every integer. This falsifies universal raw progress for this rule, including on DO01's critical high-girth families.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The six positive NAE rows contain $100,010,001,110$; subtract the first from the other three to obtain a determinant of absolute value one. Their integer affine span is $\mathbb Z^3$, and sign switching is affine unimodular. Fix a compatible actual row pair, or a single row. Choose any global Boolean word agreeing with those pins, with no requirement to satisfy the other constraints. Give the pinned owners their actual one-hot masses, and lift the word's three coordinate moments to signed integer masses summing to one independently at every other owner. Each raw pair is complete or identifies one actual shared bit, so component balances require exactly the equality of its bit-class masses (the owner sums are one). These hold by construction. Thus all pins survive. This concerns the unchanged raw representation, not arbitrary ternary moments, nonlinear normalization, or unrestricted computational lower bounds. Separate fractional and signed-integer feasible systems need not have a common nonnegative integral solution.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Executed controls and collaboration.}

\section{MS26: Conditional nonlinear component closure}\label{sec:ms26}
Attack Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} by combining actual BD18/MS24/BH18 pair and ternary cuts, I25 representative anchors, MS25 unary feature parity, and BA19 signed-integer component balance. The universal singleton progress conjecture is false; the rule below is a paid scoped normalization, not a proof of universal acquisition.
\begin{lemma}[Rebuilt conditional component hull and covered fusion]\label{lem:ms26-probe}
For an explicit authenticated owner-row chart under guard $G$, fix a live row $a$ of one owner and perform certified local closure under that assumption. Recompute the pair components on the remaining domains and compatibility tables, and form the MS25 affine relaxation $H_a$ in one-hot coordinates (or BA19's signed-integer relaxation). Inconsistency eliminates $a$; an actual one-hot row $b$ outside the corresponding projected relaxation eliminates $(a,b)$. All conclusions remain under $G$. For all live rows of one owner, the affine hull of the union of the nonempty binary $H_a$, embedded in the original coordinates with absent rows zero, supplies necessary unconditional equations under $G$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every actual solution selecting $a$ survives sound conditional closure and induces the corresponding one-hot word, satisfying the rebuilt owner sums and component balances. Thus the two exclusions follow by contraposition. Every actual solution chooses exactly one row of the split owner; the union of the relaxations covers all solutions, and affine-hull union via a representative and difference basis preserves every common affine equation. This does not treat abstract affine solutions as actual models. Rebuilding the components after deletions can strengthen the relaxation beyond substitution into a previous equation matrix.
For $R$ explicit rows, at most $R$ single-row probes per sweep, polynomial graph acquisition, Gaussian projection (or polynomial-bit integer normal forms), and polynomial chart storage per probe suffice. There are at most $R+\binom R2$ strict original-chart row/edge deletions. Exhaustion of the stated rule, with repeated sweeps and a final unsuccessful sweep, is polynomial in the explicit chart length, provided all certified closure operations used are charged and polynomial. Retain exact guard/provenance; charge failed probes, copies, Gaussian work, verification and consumer calls. The rule uses scratch variables and does not reset DR18's original-size reserve. This serial bound implies $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$ on the same realization. No such bound follows for unbounded nesting or arbitrary scope changes. Covered affine fusion is symbolic, not executed here.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Strict conditional gain, but raw singleton stagnation]\label{lem:ms26-stall}
A pair chart can pass arc consistency, pair path consistency and the root component hull, yet conditional component reconstruction forces a gate. Conversely, every raw unpinned linear signed NAE-3 registry with pair compatibility given by shared-bit equality survives every single-row rebuilt component projection, even over the integers and hence every modulus.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Take the hidden-parity four-owner $K_4$ of MS25, with eight base rows encoding two independent feature bits and a nuisance bit. Add a joker row per owner compatible with all rows of other $K_4$ owners. A two-row gate permits jokers only at gate 1. At the root the pair graphs are connected by jokers or the gate-1 row, hence the pair component constraints add nothing beyond owner sums. Arc and path consistency hold: any two incident features at a third $K_4$ owner can be prescribed independently, and a pair involving a joker can extend with another joker except under gate 0, where the joker is absent. Under gate 0, rebuilt components force equality of edge features. Complementing one owner's last feature gives the impossible global sum $0=1$. Hence gate 1 is forced; it has an actual all-joker extension. The even neighbor has $2^3$ compatible edge words and $2^4$ nuisance choices, hence 128 gate-0 models.

For the raw obstruction, fix one owner row $a$. Every other owner meets its scope in at most one bit. A signed NAE local table with zero fixed bits has full integer affine lattice by BA19; with one fixed bit its three permitted words in the two remaining coordinates form a unimodular triangle. Both values of every remaining free bit occur. Arc closure makes no further deletion beyond the shared pins. Pair components enforce only consistency of shared bit moments or redundant equations. For any remaining row $b$ compatible with $a$, choose an arbitrary source-bit word agreeing with $a,b$; give those owners actual one-hot masses and independently lift the other bit moments to signed integer masses of total one using the relative unimodular simplices. All pair balances hold. Thus no row or pair is eliminated by single-row rebuilt component projections, including their finite-field versions. This does not exclude PSD, stronger higher-order joint inference, alternative scopes or unrestricted algorithms.
\end{proof}

\section{RT25: Double-pinned full-support LP and signed-lattice obstruction}\label{sec:rt25}
This targets Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} and the proposed combination of BA19's integer pair hull with MS26's rebuilt conditional domains. Separate fractional and integer feasibility are not enough for exact joint occupancy; even requiring the integer solution to be supported on the relative-interior LP support does not ensure raw progress.
\begin{lemma}[Full support after two actual owner pins]\label{lem:rt25-double}
Let $H$ be a 3-uniform hypergraph of Berge girth at least eight, with arbitrary literal signs on NAE triples. Use raw six-row owners and binary compatibility precisely equal to agreement on common actual source bits. For every compatible choice of zero, one or two owner rows, certified coordinate forced-bit closure does not reject. On the remaining domains there exist both a rational marginal solution positive on every live owner row and compatible pair, and signed integer row and pair marginals on that same live support. Both obey normalization to one and all shared-bit and pair-to-row consistency equations. Consequently the pair-marginal LP with full positive-support refinement followed by the integer affine test cannot reject any such pin. Alternating these tests with the specified coordinate closure cannot delete any unguarded row or compatible pair. This is a fixed-representation, bounded-pin statement.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The fixed vertices initially belong to the pinned triples. If the two pinned triples intersect, or there is just one, the fixed incidence subtree has at most two owner nodes. A different triple touching two fixed vertices would close a Berge cycle of length at most three. For two disjoint pinned triples, a different triple touching two fixed vertices must bridge the components, meeting one vertex from each; two distinct bridges would close a cycle of length at most four. The sole bridge, if present, forces its third bit precisely when its two signed fixed bits coincide. Then include it in the fixed incidence tree, which now has at most three owners. No new triple can touch two fixed vertices of that tree without a cycle of length at most four. If the bridge does not force, its third bit is unrestricted. Thus forced-bit closure terminates without rejection, and all free bits in surviving local words have both values.

Form the graph on free variables whose edges are the two free variables of every one-fixed-bit owner. Label an edge by the fixed incidence component it touches. Two incident edges with the same label would give a Berge cycle via the fixed tree of length at most five. Therefore degree is at most two. A simple three-edge path would repeat a label on its first and third edges, yielding a Berge cycle of length at most six; a triangle also has incident edges of the same label. Thus components are paths of length at most two. For each free variable choose marginal $1/2+d_v/600$. On each such path start with $d=0$, then choose the next signed bias of magnitude $|d_{\rm prev}|+1$ in the direction making the sum of the two signed free marginals strictly greater than one for a fixed signed zero, or strictly less than one for a fixed signed one. Signs change coefficients only by $\pm1$. All $|d_v|\le2$. The three allowed free words of every one-fixed owner therefore admit strictly positive barycentric weights. For a zero-fixed owner start with uniform weights on all six signed NAE words; perturb using the unimodular simplex $100,010,001,110$. With denominator 600 and biases bounded by two, the largest absolute adjustment is at most six, whereas each baseline numerator is 100. Two-fixed owners with a free bit admit both words and positive Bernoulli weights; all-fixed owners admit their singleton. Fixed bits have exact point marginals. This constructs rational row marginals with full support. Disjoint pairs admit product coupling. For a shared bit take the product within each bit class and divide by that class's positive mass (skip empty classes). This yields positive weights on all live compatible pairs with the required marginals.

For the integer certificate choose any Boolean word extending the fixed bits, not necessarily a satisfying assignment. Lift its local integer coordinate moments using the unimodular four-row simplex at each zero-fixed owner, the unimodular triangle at each one-fixed owner, and the binary simplex or singleton in the other cases. These signed integer masses have sum one. Pair components are precisely shared-bit classes, or one component for disjoint owners. Equal component masses allow signed integer edge coefficients by BA19's tree transport (Lemma~\ref{lem:ba19-lattice}). Their support is contained in the positive LP support. Thus both relaxations are feasible after rebuilding under each actual pin. No joint nonnegative integer solution is inferred.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Infinite critical opposite-label controls]\label{lem:rt25-neighbors}
There are unbounded minimally UNSAT monotone NAE-3 registries of arbitrarily prescribed Berge girth and SAT single-sign neighbors on the same underlying triples, all satisfying Lemma~\ref{lem:rt25-double}.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The classical Erd\H{o}s--Hajnal high-girth/high-chromatic hypergraph theorem supplies a 3-uniform hypergraph of chromatic number at least three and arbitrarily large Berge girth (see Axenovich and Karrer, \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.06600}{High girth hypergraphs with unavoidable monochromatic or rainbow edges}). Take an inclusion-minimal non-2-colorable subhypergraph. Deletion of any owner admits a coloring violating exactly that removed triple in the root. Changing a single literal sign in that triple accepts the deletion witness, preserving all other constraints. Girth is unchanged by sign changes and cannot decrease under deletion. Increasing the girth yields unbounded size. This is an existential family, not a proved efficient generator in requested size.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Charged scope.}
For a fixed explicit registry of $R$ rows, all at most $O(R^2)$ root pin probes, iterative certified coordinate scans, polynomial-bit LP and positive-support discovery, polynomial-bit integer feasibility and certificate verification, and scratch storage are paid. A fixed-scope outer loop can charge strict deletions against $R+\binom R2$ original row/pair IDs, plus a final unsuccessful sweep; no reserve reset or free semantic closure. On the exhibited families every root probe passes. The same serial execution has $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$; the original-input polynomial chart cap is separate. Neither arbitrary higher-order marginals, arbitrary affine guards, recursively nested probes, PSD, imported veto masks, native physical compilation nor unrestricted algorithms are obstructed. This specifically rules out a proposed support-refined pair closure as universal progress, not all collective normalization. Compare Brakensiek et al., \href{https://doi.org/10.1137/20M1312745}{BLP+AIP for promise CSPs}; Lichter--Pago, \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.09097}{limitations of affine relaxations}.

\section{DP20: Orbit-cover export and phase-guarded aggregate credit}\label{sec:dp20}
This section addresses Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}, DP19's representative firewall, I25's exact gauge, and MS25/MS26's actual anchored deductions. It does not establish universal strict progress.
\begin{lemma}[Necessary orbit-cover export]\label{lem:dp20-cover}
Fix an authenticated owner-row chart $F$ under its actual guard $G$, with a certified elementary-abelian owner-flip group $K$ preserving all factors and the guard. Let $A$ select a representative of each solution orbit and let $H$ be a sound relaxation of $F\land A$. For any scope $I$ of at most fixed $k$ owners and any acquired superset $T_I$ of the projected $H$-model tuples, every root model projects to
\[
 \bigcup_{v\in\pi_I(K)}v\cdot T_I.
\]
A missing tuple is a necessary exclusion under $G$. At most $2^k$ masks need be enumerated, regardless of the rank of $K$. If $H$ is proved empty, $F$ is UNSAT.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every root solution has a representative in $F\land A$, hence in $H$. Its tuple is a translate of the representative tuple by a mask in the projected group. Gaussian projection of the certified basis onto the scope suffices. For unary and binary scopes, the surviving row domains and allowed pairs of $H$ are valid supersets; larger fixed scopes may enumerate the explicit tuple universe and check local necessary factors, not exact semantic support for free. A witness of the actual representative chart lifts by its source map; arbitrary relaxation membership does not certify SAT.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Phase-guarded transport of anchored facts]\label{lem:dp20-phase}
Choose anchor coordinates $J$ with $K\to\mathbb F_2^J$ bijective as in I25. Write $e_J(w)$ for the anchor-orbit orientation vector of a root transversal $w$, and $h(w)$ for the unique group element projecting to $e_J(w)$. An anchored entailed exclusion of tuple $\tau$ on scope $I$ implies, in the root under $G$,
\[
 \pi_I h(w)=v\quad\Longrightarrow\quad w_I\ne v\cdot\tau
 \qquad(v\in\pi_I K).
\]
There are at most $2^k$ guarded implications, with phase conditions of at most $k$ linear equations on the anchor orientation bits. For global rank one and canonical anchor rows $S$, opposite rows $C$, a pair exclusion $(a,b)$ on the representative chart gives root tuple exclusions $(a,b,c)$ for $c\in S$, and $(\bar a,\bar b,c)$ for $c\in C$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
By construction $h(w)\cdot w$ is the canonical representative of $w$ and remains a solution of the actual guarded chart. Its tuple cannot equal $\tau$. Involutions are their own inverses, giving the implication. Orientation predicates and the linear inverse of the anchor map are computed and charged; no semantic oracle is used to transport an already authenticated deduction. For rank one the two orientation conditions are just membership in $S,C$. Discard tuples containing incompatible choices of the same owner or already impossible pairs; repeated identical rows reduce arity. The resulting necessary exclusion is under the actual guard, not an unguarded pair exclusion. All factors, including higher ones, must admit the certified symmetry.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Fixed-scope tuple reserve, and failure of universal binary export]\label{lem:dp20-credit}
Fix a polynomially bounded original row universe of size $R$, fixed $k$, and one actual guard. Let $\mathcal U$ contain the possible tuples of arity at most $k$, and $D\subseteq\mathcal U$ the deduplicated recorded necessary exclusions. The potential
\[
 W=1+|\mathcal U\setminus D|
\]
strictly decreases under every genuinely new recorded exclusion. Under a fixed finite list of polynomially capped attempts per version and a final failed sweep, the aggregate cost is polynomial; rank-one pair transport uses $k=3$. There is no universal strict unary/pair export from representative progress.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
There are at most $\sum_{i=1}^k R^i$ exclusions, each recorded once. Reclose after accepted deductions, with all failed scans, guard checks, symmetry verification, scratch copies, canonicalization, consumers, source-map storage and witness lifts paid. Anchor scratch does not acquire a new reserve. General-rank compact implications may use a fixed anchor-map and tuple/mask reserve; changing the map or guard requires a separately proved bound or outer descent, not an automatic reset. On this admitted serial run, $T,S$ are polynomial and $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$. For the failure claim take positive NAE on three Boolean owners, invariant under global complement. All original pairs extend to a model. Anchoring $x=0$ excludes $(y,z)=(0,0)$, but its translated fact is under $x=1$ and excludes $(1,1)$. No unguarded pair exclusion results. This easy family is not an unrestricted lower bound. Nor does a finite tuple reserve ensure a strict new deduction at every residual.
\end{proof}

\section{BH19: Native NAE forest veto gates and direct-first source replay}\label{sec:bh19}
The target is Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}, in particular the proposed universal fixed-arity fill after an exact tractable block elimination. This section extends DR19's Horn obstruction to the actual NAE language and gives a paid constructive alternative, not a universal success theorem.
\begin{lemma}[Exact monotone forest pin consumer]\label{lem:bh19-gate}
Let a signed NAE-3 region have a forest as its variable--owner incidence graph, and authenticate its explicit exterior row-to-pin map. Each selected flag requires specified actual Boolean values on one or more vertices; no other uncompiled constraints may be hidden in the region. Local rejection is computed by a monotone AND/OR circuit of size linear in the forest and pin-map occurrence count, with polynomial-time construction, evaluation and witness lift.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Root each tree at a variable. Write $P_v(b)$ for the OR of the flags that prohibit value $b$ at $v$. The variable rejection message $R_{v\to e}(b)$ is the OR of $P_v(b)$ and the rejection messages at $b$ from all child owners. The owner rejection message $R_{e\to v}(b)$ is the AND over legal child tuples $(a,c)$ for parent value $b$ of $R_{u\to e}(a)\lor R_{w\to e}(c)$, where $u,w$ are its two child variables. Each owner has constant arity. At a root the AND of its two value rejection messages is the component rejection, and the OR of component rejections is the regional rejection. The empty AND and OR have their usual meanings. Induction on the rooted incidence tree proves exactness because conditioned child subtrees share no other variables. Reverse descent chooses an accepting value and a legal child tuple, independently reconstructing every child. The two messages per rooted incidence and explicit pin flags give the asserted bound. Actual source variables, signs, flags and all guards are retained.
\end{proof}
If a partial exterior choice gives masks $L\subseteq A\subseteq U$ for certainly active, actual active and possibly active flags, monotonicity proves rejection whenever the gate rejects $L$, and local extendability for every remaining exterior choice whenever it accepts $U$. The latter is not global SAT. A consumer retains the exact gate and its reverse lift unless its irrelevance is established on the actual guard. Each call, construction, identity check and lift is paid; a fixed chart of $R$ rows and a fixed polynomial cap on gate sizes can charge strict unary/pair deletions to original row/pair IDs and a final failed scan. This does not bound new scopes, branch aggregation, or joint gate selection universally.
\begin{lemma}[Exponential exterior-only fill on a native NAE tree]\label{lem:bh19-fill}
For every $h\ge0$ there is a positive NAE-3 incidence tree with $L=3\cdot2^h$ leaves, $2L-3$ variables and $L-2$ owners, variable degree at most two, and two independent exterior Boolean pin flags $a_i,b_i$ per leaf, such that its exact rejection function is
\[
\bigwedge_{i=1}^L(a_i\lor b_i).
\]
Any exact CNF for acceptance on the exterior flags alone requires at least $2^L$ clauses, including clauses of width at least $L$. The exact monotone gate of Lemma~\ref{lem:bh19-gate} has linear size in the tree and map.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Take three disjoint full binary trees of height $h$, one variable per node, and an NAE owner on every parent and its two children. Join the three top variables with one central NAE. Either flag at a leaf pins it to zero. If every leaf is pinned, the internal values alternate by level; the three top values coincide, so the central owner rejects. If a leaf is unpinned, set all other leaves to zero, flip that leaf and flip each ancestor on its path from the alternating assignment. Each owner on the path has unequal children, and the central owner becomes nonconstant. This constructs an extension. For each minimal rejected flag word (one selected flag per leaf), some acceptance CNF clause must be false. Changing any of its selected flags to zero yields acceptance, so the false clause must contain the negative literal for every selected flag. This clause cannot be false at a different minimal rejected flag word. There are $2^L$ such words, giving the clause and width lower bounds. This excludes only explicit exterior CNF without auxiliaries, not compact circuits, arbitrary normalization, or unrestricted SAT algorithms.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Executed cooperative comparison.}
Use the same immutable BD18 charts, MS24/BH18 actual pair and ternary cuts, I25 representative masks and MS25/MS26 BW17 anchor-local cuts, with GD24 and BS17 reverse lifts and original source predicates. The deterministic smallest-domain, maximum-support-row search caps each job at 128 nodes, runs arc closure before branching and after deductions, and in joint mode consumes actual ternary vetoes (three selected reject, two delete the third, one deletes a remaining pair under that guard). Reaching the cap declines. All five baseline charts, five pair-import charts, five joint charts, and three representative charts return SAT. \section{Coherent small-scope forest closure and joint local obstruction (S25)}\label{sec:s25}
We attack Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} using RT25's high-girth opposite-label construction, BH19's exact forest consumer, and DP20's bounded-scope export. The five common BD18 charts already have verified SAT source witnesses (BH19), so closure stagnation on those charts is not a hard decision obstruction.
\begin{lemma}[Coherent forest-closure support]\label{lem:s25-coherent}
Fix $k\ge6$. For any raw signed NAE-3 registry with three distinct variables per owner and Berge girth greater than $k$, there exists a nonempty family of supports $P(S)$ on every actual variable set $S$, $|S|\le k$, such that for $S\subseteq T$, $|T|\le k$, projection of $P(T)$ is exactly $P(S)$. All registered raw owner rows, compatible owner-row pairs, and all unary and binary words belong to their respective supports. Moreover every exact projection of an incidence-forest subregistry onto such a scope accepts all of $P(S)$, regardless of the size of the forest. For an actual coordinate guard whose word belongs to its support, the same property holds with guard variables included in the total scope budget.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Starting with $S$, repeatedly include any as-yet unprocessed triple with at least two present vertices, adding its missing vertices. Include all-present triples as well. Initially there are $|S|$ isolated components. Inductively an included edge cannot meet two present vertices in the same component: the old forest path and the new edge would form a Berge cycle of length at most $|S|\le k$, since at most $|S|-1$ edges have previously been included. Thus each included edge joins at least two previous components and adds at most one vertex. The process terminates with at most $|S|-1$ edges and at most $2|S|-1$ vertices for nonempty $S$, and the induced incidence graph is a forest. The least fixed-point vertex set $C(S)$ is monotone in $S$; $C(\varnothing)=\varnothing$. Define $P(S)$ as the projections to $S$ of legal colorings of the induced forest on $C(S)$. A forest can be colored from its roots, so $P(S)$ is nonempty.
For extension from $S$ to $T$, fix any legal coloring of $C(S)$. Every additional edge in the forest induced on $C(T)$ meets at most one fixed vertex, by closure. Remove fixed vertices from the incidence graph; every remaining owner has at least two free neighbors. Root each free tree at a variable, and traverse downwards, choosing child bits satisfying signed NAE with the parent bit and any fixed bit. Each owner has at least one free child and the other child, if fixed, has its specified value. This always succeeds. Restriction follows from monotonicity. For a single owner no further edge can enter its connected component. For two compatible pinned owners, first include their edges; if they are disjoint, any further included edge must bridge the two components and add a free third vertex (linearity); at most one bridge is possible. Thus every compatible pair extends. A pair of individual variables either has no added owner or adds one owner with a free third vertex.
For an arbitrary incidence-forest subregistry $H$, fix the coloring on its intersection with $C(S)$, using any isolated pinned variables as needed. Already fully fixed owners are satisfied and all other owners meet at most one fixed vertex. The identical free-forest traversal extends to all of $H$. Hence its exact projected relation accepts $P(S)$. A guard is handled by taking the fiber of these supports over its actual pinned variables; exact projection and extension preserve that fiber when the total scope remains within $k$.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Fixed actual-scope collaborative closure is not universally decisive]\label{lem:s25-barrier}
Initialize all explicit tables on actual variable subsets of size at most fixed $k$ by their induced raw constraints. Allow repeated support deletions across inclusion maps, and exact constraints obtained by projecting any incidence-forest subregistry onto such scopes, with actual coordinate guard variables charged to the scope. Every table continues to contain the coherent supports of Lemma~\ref{lem:s25-coherent}. This procedure cannot refute the raw high-girth instances and cannot delete any root raw row or compatible raw pair. Some higher-order tuples may be deleted.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Induct on accepted deletions and added factors using exact projection and forest extension. The family is nonempty on every scope, including the empty scope. For every fixed $k$, Erd\H{o}s--Hajnal's existence theorem (as stated in Axenovich--Karrer, \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.06600}{arXiv:1607.06600}) supplies a non-2-colorable 3-uniform hypergraph of girth $>k$. Take an inclusion-minimal UNSAT subhypergraph and flip one literal in a critical owner: its deletion witness becomes a satisfying word of the signed neighbor. Both labels pass the stated closure. This is existential, not an efficient generator or an asserted four-perfect-partition compiler.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Scope and accounting.}
For fixed $k$, the explicit table universe has at most $\sum_{j\le k}\binom nj2^j$ entries; each strict deletion is charged once, including a final unsuccessful scan. Computing $C(S)$ and enumerating at most $2^{2k-1}$ colorings per nonempty scope is paid. Each forest acquisition, gate construction, consumer, guard version and source lift needs its own charge; arbitrary forest discovery is not free. This is a barrier to a specified inference family, not all normalization, LP/AIP/PSD, arbitrary affine guards, transformed row tables, or unbounded-source-scope gates. In particular DP20 orbit exports are covered only when independently proved to preserve these supports; globally entailed arbitrary cuts need not preserve them. Growing $k$ with $N$ does not make the explicit $n^k$ table bound uniformly polynomial. Universal SEM/CLOSE, unconditional COST and U-PROGRESS remain open; a fixed cap decline is not UNSAT. Same serial execution $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$; no unrestricted lower bound or configuration-counting transfer.

\section{DO20: Bounded-pin forest saturation and a consistent local adversary}\label{sec:do20}
This addresses Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}, BH19's forest gates (Lemma~\ref{lem:bh19-gate}) and RT25's bounded-pin obstruction. In the raw signed NAE-3 language on actual variables, even the union of all acyclic regional pin consumers can be redundant. The scope is not arbitrary transformed charts or affine guards. The independently developed small-closure and coherent-support argument overlaps the concurrent S25 (Lemmas~\ref{lem:s25-coherent}--\ref{lem:s25-barrier}); the additional results here are equality with the raw two-fixed-bit propagation test, the outside-closure two-value extension, and the restricted tree-cap bound. In this section coordinate closure means only the signed NAE two-equal-fixed-bits forcing rule and the all-fixed violation check, iterated to a fixed point.

\begin{lemma}[Small seed closure is a forest]\label{lem:do20-closure}
Let the 3-uniform owner hypergraph have Berge girth $g>k$. For a seed set $S$ of at most $k$ actual variables, start with isolated seeds and repeatedly add any not-yet-added owner meeting the current variable set in at least two vertices, including all its vertices. Denote the resulting variable and owner sets by $V_S,E_S$. They are independent of the order, form an incidence forest, and for nonempty $S$ satisfy $|E_S|\le |S|-1$, $|V_S|\le2|S|-1$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The monotone finite closure is the least fixed point. Before an addition, each existing component is a tree. If two touched vertices are in the same component, the new owner closes a Berge cycle of length at most the number of previously added owners plus one. Otherwise the addition merges at least two components and creates at most one new variable. Inductively, before any addition there are at most $|S|-1$ previously added owners, so the cycle case contradicts $g>k$. Each addition decreases the number of components at least once, hence the bounds. Empty seeds give empty closure. Track owners even when an addition introduces no new variable.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Exact saturation of arbitrary forest pin consumers]\label{lem:do20-forest}
For any actual pin word on $S$, $|S|\le k<g$, the following are equivalent: (i) the word extends to a solution on $E_S$; (ii) exhaustive certified coordinate forced-bit closure on the original raw registry does not reject; (iii) every acyclic subregion of the original registry admits an extension of the word. Subregions may have unbounded size; no enumeration of them is required.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every owner outside $E_S$ touches at most one variable in $V_S$. Given a satisfying assignment on $V_S$, fix it, discard already satisfied owners of any forest subregion, and remove fixed vertices from the remaining incidence graph. Every remaining owner has at least two free variables, and the graph is still a forest. Root each component at a free variable, choose its bit, then descend: each owner has a free child, which can be chosen to prevent all three signed bits from agreeing. This extends the word throughout the subregion. Conversely the closure itself is an acyclic subregion. For (ii), a forced-bit step requires two equal signed fixed bits in an owner, and every such step stays inside $V_S$ by its definition. A contradictory all-fixed owner is also inside $E_S$. On the closure forest, at a nonrejecting fixed point all remaining unsatisfied owners have at least two free variables, so the same rooted construction yields a solution. Thus coordinate closure decides the closure query exactly. This is not a claim of global extendability. An actual pin word may be supplied by flags, but all pins and owners must be authenticated raw coordinates, not an unproved adapter.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Simultaneously stable bounded-view family]\label{lem:do20-views}
Let $P_S$ be the projection onto $S$ of the solutions on $E_S$. For $S\subseteq T$, $|T|\le k$, one has $\pi_S P_T=P_S$. Every $P_S$ is nonempty. If $x\notin V_S$ and $|S|<k$, both values of $x$ extend each word in $P_S$ to $P_{S\cup\{x\}}$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Closure is monotone, so restriction is sound. Choose a witness on $V_S$ for any word in $P_S$. The larger closure is a forest, and every new owner touches at most one old variable. The preceding rooted construction extends the entire old witness; when a specific new free variable is requested, root its free component there and choose either value. Starting with empty seeds proves nonemptiness. This family satisfies every raw owner whose three variables lie in the view, since such an owner belongs to the closure. Every forest projection of a view contains its $P_S$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:do20-forest}.
\end{proof}
Consequently, arbitrary repetition of bounded-view relational semijoins, restrictions and projection consistency on at most $k$ actual variables, even seeded by all forest-gate projections on those views, cannot reject these raw registries. The $P_S$ give a common nonempty invariant under all such operations. For owner-row scopes of at most $r$ owners use $k\ge3r$ and transport by the actual variable-to-row map; do not infer that every compatible tuple survives. Nor do these sets supply consistent fractional, integer or PSD higher moments: that requires another proof.

\begin{lemma}[Restricted direct-search cap obstruction]\label{lem:do20-cap}
On an UNSAT raw registry of girth $g>k$, a finite binary actual-bit decision tree whose rejecting leaves are certified only by acyclic subregion infeasibility under the branch pins must contain at least $2^k$ distinct nodes. This remains true with forced-bit propagation used as a rejection test.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Maintain an adversary witness on the closure of a seed set. At a query inside that closure follow the value of its witness; no new seed is needed. At a query outside, retain both branches and extend the witness separately by Lemma~\ref{lem:do20-views}, adding that query to the seeds. Until $k$ external choices have been made, every queried bit agrees with the witness and no forest consumer can reject: the extension argument applies to the whole witnessed closure, hence also to any subset of its pins. A finite sound UNSAT tree must therefore reach $k$ external choices on each retained path. There are $2^k$ distinct retained nodes at the $k$th external choice. This is a tree bound; sharing, general learning, arbitrary affine queries and nonlocal terminals are outside it.
\end{proof}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:rt25-neighbors}, for every fixed $k$ there are minimally UNSAT positive registries of girth greater than $k$ and single-sign SAT neighbors on the same triples. All survive the bounded-view invariant, including every local owner row for $k\ge3$. For a fixed direct cap $B$, choosing $k$ with $2^k>B$ excludes the specified tree method. This does not prove that the actual complete portfolio fails or even that BH19's transformed chart search fails. It is not an explicit efficient generator or an unrestricted time lower bound. In particular $k=O(\log n)$ yields only a polynomial tree bound.

\paragraph{Charged constructive consequence.}
On the eligible raw domain, use a single coordinate-closure query instead of enumerating, acquiring and evaluating forest consumers for bounded actual-pin tests. This preserves their exact collective rejection power; it does not remove a forest gate's global symbolic role under other guards or many pins. Source parsing, girth eligibility (BFS in the incidence graph with cycle length measured in owners), closure membership and forced-bit scans, conditional pin identity, witness reconstruction for a requested forest and every consumer access are polynomial. For fixed $k$, explicit bounded-view tables cost at most $O(n^k2^k)$ entries and their acquisition and all tuple accesses are paid. The forest closure uses at most $2k-1$ variables; enumeration is unnecessary for a single pin decision. For growing $k$, table storage is not uniformly polynomial. No reset of original input credit, no universal aggregate contraction. Serial fixed-scope implementation has polynomial $T,S$ and $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$ on the same execution.

\paragraph{Executed controls and shared benchmark.}
Three signed loose cycles with 5, 6 and 7 owners, $k=3$: 945 scopes, 6515 pin words, 41234 maximal-forest projection queries, 9292 extension checks and 9076 two-value checks, 115552 assertions with no failures; exhaustive reference assignments and all maximal forests obtained by one owner deletion. Fano root and seven single-sign neighbors have 0 and 10 models respectively, all root coordinate closure OPEN; low-girth negative controls, not high-girth UNSAT execution. On the SAME immutable BH19 source/guard jobs, independently checked all 18 supplied source words, 800 original owner evaluations and six actual guard bits against DR17/BW17/M23 source predicates. No new search, upstream GD24/BS17 lift replay, representative-anchor replay, high-girth critical generator, LP/SNF, native replay, full portfolio, kernel or physical CM. Source field \texttt{p} in those registries is provenance, not a sign mask; a first attempted replay using it as a sign mask failed and was corrected from the BH19 authoritative source checker. See \href{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/4c9d2b1fb60160129eb68404fde503ad6ab836fd}{checker} and \href{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/bdbf7f65e3edcc253f1a8490eda0f439418f1cc9}{results}.

\paragraph{Parallel stagnation.}
All five existing charts are positive controls, not unresolved source obstructions. Request a common high-girth critical UNSAT/single-sign SAT registry with deletion witnesses and actual source map, and a nonlocal reduction that bypasses the bounded-view invariant rather than increasing a fixed scope. Keep existing immutable BD18/MS24/BH18/I25/MS25/MS26/DP20 guards and maps for positive controls; representative cuts stay guarded. Requests only, no peer completion assumed. \section{BS19: Width-independent signed NAE resolution and a raw cap obstruction}\label{sec:bs19}
We address Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} by avoiding the truth-table boundary cost of BS17, consistent with the compact-consumer lesson of BH19. This is a specialized NAE-resolution/Davis--Putnam projection, not a claim of novelty or universal tractability.
\begin{lemma}[Exact wide-owner projection with paid aggregate reserve]\label{lem:bs19-nae}
Consider a chart consisting solely of explicit signed NAE lists, with no uncompiled guard or other consumer incident on an eliminated variable. Canonicalize each list by deduplication and whole-list complement, delete lists containing complementary literals and reject empty or singleton lists. A binary owner enforces a relative XOR; substitute it exactly throughout the chart and retain the lift. For a variable $v$ occurring in $d$ remaining owners, complement entire lists as needed so all these owners have the form $\operatorname{NAE}(v,L_i)$. Then exact existential projection of $v$ replaces these $d$ owners by
\[
 \bigwedge_{1\le i<j\le d}\operatorname{NAE}(L_i,\overline{L_j}).
\]
All unaffected constraints remain. There is a deterministic paid polynomial partial algorithm for every fixed original-input polynomial cutoff $D(N)$ on $d$, irrespective of boundary width. Repeatedly apply certified binary closure, choose a minimum-occurrence pivot with deterministic ties, project when $d\le D(N)$, and reclose after deductions and at stagnation. A cap failure returns OPEN with an exact residual, not UNSAT. If all variables are eliminated or a contradiction is acquired, it decides exactly with a polynomial-cost witness lift.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For a fixed exterior word, owner $i$ leaves $v$ free unless $L_i$ is monochromatic with bit $b$, in which case it forces $v=1-b$. There is a common bit iff no two forced bits conflict, which is exactly the displayed conjunction. Reverse reconstruction chooses the common required bit, or either bit if none. Each substitution or projection removes a variable, so credit $1+n_{\rm remaining}$ strictly contracts on the single child. After at most $n$ steps the owner count is at most $m+nD(N)^2$ and each canonical list has at most $n$ literals. Thus discovery, canonicalization, every pair candidate, closure, source maps and reverse logs, failed final scan, bit operations and original-source witness verification are polynomial in original $N$ on this realization; polynomial peak space and $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$ follow. The source can include actual coordinate pins via a common reference bit and signed binary parity owners; decode after the lift by a global complement fixing the reference to zero. This relies on complement symmetry and does not apply to arbitrary affine guards or non-NAE consumers without an exact paid adapter. A shorter literal list (or its complement) contained in a longer list implies that longer NAE owner; paid subsumption can be included without growing the registry. No claim of model-count preservation or universal cap success.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Raw degree-four elimination cap can stall under every order]\label{lem:bs19-cap}
On any nonempty simple linear 4-regular 3-uniform signed NAE registry of Berge girth greater than four, the rule of Lemma~\ref{lem:bs19-nae} with $D=4$, canonicalization and binary closure cannot eliminate every variable, regardless of pivot ordering.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Inductively the eliminated variables form an independent set in the primal graph. Each removed variable replaces its four incident original owners by six distinct signed 4-variable owners, because the four exterior pairs are disjoint. Different eliminated variables have no common original owner. If two generated scopes were identical, their pivots would have at least two common primal neighbors, giving a Berge cycle of length at most four (or violating linearity if both common neighbors are in the same owner at both pivots). Thus no cross-pivot duplicate drops; all generated lists have distinct variables, so no tautological or binary owners. Any surviving variable in a touched original owner loses that owner and gains three distinct resolvents, hence its degree increases by two per touched original owner. Untouched vertices retain degree four. The next eligible pivot is consequently nonadjacent to the eliminated set, establishing the induction. A maximal independent set cannot contain every vertex of an original triple; surviving vertices adjacent to it have degree at least six. No contradiction or binary owner is produced by these steps. This is a raw rule obstruction, not an unrestricted lower bound, nor a claim that larger caps or nonlocal transformations fail.
\end{proof}

\section{GD26: Factored wide-NAE pivot and a resolution firewall}\label{sec:gd26}
We strengthen BS19 (Lemma~\ref{lem:bs19-nae}) and address Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}, distinguishing a compact projected relation from a universally cheap consumer.
\begin{lemma}[Exact linear-volume factored pivot]\label{lem:gd26-gate}
In a normalized signed NAE pivot bucket $\operatorname{NAE}(v,L_i)$, $1\le i\le d$, with nonempty tails and no other pivot consumer, write $Z_i=\bigwedge_{\ell\in L_i}\neg\ell$ and $O_i=\bigwedge_{\ell\in L_i}\ell$. The exact rejecting predicate after existentially eliminating $v$ is
\[
  \left(\bigvee_i Z_i\right)\land\left(\bigvee_i O_i\right).
\]
It has circuit size and acquisition/evaluation/lift cost linear in the bucket literal volume in a unit-index model, polynomial in the encoded input. All unaffected owners and guards remain. If a $Z$ flag holds, $v=1$ is required; if an $O$ flag holds, $v=0$ is required; otherwise either works. The original pivot extends exactly when the two flag types do not both hold. Under partial actual-coordinate pins a certified rule is that a known true flag of either type forbids every flag of the other type; this is ordinary clause propagation. Retain guard provenance and reclose after deductions. No claim that subsequent elimination of arbitrary such gates preserves this size bound.
\end{lemma}
\begin{lemma}[All fixed polynomial raw NAE resolution caps are insufficient]\label{lem:gd26-res}
There is an infinite family of signed NAE-3 registries on which no fixed original-input polynomial occurrence cap in the BS19 raw projection, binary substitution, canonicalization and subsumption algorithm suffices for complete elimination or contradiction, under any pivot ordering. The claim excludes additional rules without polynomial-size ordinary resolution derivations, including arbitrary affine inference and non-resolution terminals.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Expand $\operatorname{NAE}(L)$ into clauses $\bigvee L$ and $\bigvee\overline L$. Each BS19 pair resolvent is derived by two ordinary resolutions on the pivot. A binary substitution is obtained using its two implication clauses, one resolution per affected expanded clause. Canonicalization, tautology deletion, complement and subsumption do not require new derived clauses; a singleton NAE yields an empty resolvent. For original $n$ variables, $m$ owners and a fixed polynomial cap $D(N)$, every chart has at most $m+nD^2$ owners, there are at most $n$ eliminations/substitutions, and an UNSAT completion produces a polynomial-length ordinary general resolution refutation, including identical-clause DAG sharing. This simulation also covers additional explicit clause deductions only when supplied with polynomial-size ordinary resolution derivations.
 
Take an infinite family of connected cubic expanders $G$ on $h$ vertices and odd-sum vertex charges, with one bit per edge. Encode each vertex parity equation by its four ordinary 3-clauses. For each clause $(a\lor b\lor c)$ use $\operatorname{NAE}(r,a,b,c)$ with common reference $r$, and split it into $\operatorname{NAE}(r,a,t)\land\operatorname{NAE}(\neg t,b,c)$ with private fresh $t$. For each exterior assignment the split extends iff the four literals are not all equal: equal first and last pairs impose conflicting values of $t$ exactly when their common bits agree. Fixing $r=0$ recovers the parity CNF under existential elimination of private bits. Global complement preserves all NAE owners, so odd total charge gives UNSAT without a reference pin. Flipping one vertex charge gives SAT by solving the even syndrome and lifting local gadgets. The source has $O(h)$ variables and owners, encoded length $O(h\log h)$.
 
For a resolution refutation restrict $r=0$ and group the resulting clauses by original graph vertex. Group $u$ is existentially its vertex parity, and private variables are disjoint across groups. Every proper subset of groups is consistent: each induced component has a boundary edge in the connected graph, and one such free edge together with a spanning tree solves its equations; then lift private variables. Define support of a clause as the minimum number of groups implying it. Axioms have support at most one, the empty clause has support $h$, resolution is subadditive in parent supports, and weakening cannot increase support. Backtracking from the empty clause to a parent of support at least $h/3$ while current support exceeds $2h/3$ yields a clause $C$ with support in $[h/3,2h/3]$. Let $S$ be a minimum witnessing group set.
 
For any edge $e$ crossing from $u\in S$ to outside, either $C$ mentions $e$ or it mentions a private variable of $u$. Otherwise minimum support gives a model of $S\setminus\{u\}$ falsifying $C$. Set $e$ to satisfy $u$'s parity and choose its private variables to satisfy its group. No other group in $S$ uses $e$ and $C$ is unchanged, a contradiction. Each clause variable thus covers at most three boundary edges, so $\operatorname{width}(C)\ge|\partial S|/3=\Omega(h)$. Initial width is at most three, with $O(h)$ variables. The general resolution size-width theorem (Ben-Sasson--Wigderson, 2001, Corollary 3.6) gives refutation size $\exp(\Omega(h))$. Restricting a resolution proof cannot increase size (allow weakening, which can be eliminated by replacing lines by subclauses), hence the unpinned NAE source also has this bound. This contradicts polynomial raw completion for every fixed cap on sufficiently large family members.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Constructive escape and scope.}
With the authenticated vertex-group map, enumerate each constant-size local existential relation, verify its parity equation, perform Gaussian elimination and lift private bits. This solves both labels in polynomial time on the same source, avoiding the restricted proof-size bound. If the map is not supplied, acquisition is charged. Neither this family nor the bound implies unrestricted SAT hardness. Compact gates can be outside the simulation, but a universal paid gate-consumer theorem is still missing. Source pins, general affine guards and physical E4/B4 replay are not covered by the raw obstruction.
 
\paragraph{Executed matched controls.}
Same immutable BW17/K16 data from \href{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/ff92a1c3d44e4b48dc9a7bf215825075396cae5a}{BS19}, blob cda85d10e150d823501fe6102408455d4fe2a, guard empty. \section{DA20: All-polynomial-cap obstruction to explicit wide NAE projection}\label{sec:da20}
This strengthens BS19 (Lemma~\ref{lem:bs19-cap}) from a fixed cap of four to every fixed polynomial occurrence cap, on a different raw positive ternary family. It also provides a factored algebraic certificate for each exact projection. No claim about the entire portfolio or arbitrary native tetravalent charts.

\begin{lemma}[Factored resultant and resolution simulation]\label{lem:da20-sim}
For an oriented bucket $\operatorname{NAE}(v,L_i)$ let $A_i=\prod_{\ell\in L_i}(1+\ell)$, $B_i=\prod_{\ell\in L_i}\ell$ in the Boolean ring, and $q_i=(1+v)A_i+vB_i$. The violation polynomial of the BS19 pair resolvent is
\[
r_{ij}=A_iB_j+B_iA_j=q_i(A_j+B_j)+q_j(A_i+B_i).
\]
Its factored identity can be recorded and syntactically verified with polynomial work in the two explicit parent scopes. On the paired-CNF encoding $E(\operatorname{NAE}(L))=(\bigvee L)\land(\bigvee\bar L)$, every pair resolvent has a derivation of two ordinary resolution lines, one per complementary clause. Deduplication, tautology deletion and signed subsumption require no new proof lines; exact binary parity substitution costs at most one resolution per affected clause, using the corresponding implication from the binary owner. Singleton/empty owner rejection yields the empty clause. Thus any UNSAT execution of BS19 with these rules yields a resolution DAG of size polynomial in the paid number and bit length of explicit operations. The same applies to ordinary coordinate unit propagation and resolution-derived learned clauses when all discharged proofs are paid. Arbitrary affine guards, extension axioms, semantic keys, nonresolution terminals and implicit factored coverage are not included.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Expand the two products in the Boolean ring and cancel repeated terms. The two CNF resolvents follow by resolving $v\vee\bigvee L_i$ against $\neg v\vee\bigvee\bar L_j$ and the complementary pair. Both are tautological or neither is. A binary owner $E(\operatorname{NAE}(x,\ell))$ gives $x\vee\ell$ and $\neg x\vee\neg\ell$, so substitution of $x$ by $\neg\ell$ follows by resolving with the appropriate clause. Maintain immutable clause IDs and parent IDs despite physical deletions, charging each consumer and all proof lines, not the unfolded tree. The resultant does not promise that repeated circuit elimination or its coverage test is cheap.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Expanding critical ternary NAE family]\label{lem:da20-exp}
There is an absolute $\delta>0$ and arbitrarily large raw positive NAE-3 UNSAT registries with $n$ available variables, at most $4n$ owners, and every subregistry of $t\le \lfloor\delta n\rfloor$ owners having more than $7t/4$ incident variables. Their inclusion-minimal UNSAT subregistries retain this property and have single-sign SAT neighbors on identical triples. Every ordinary resolution refutation of their paired 3-CNF encodings has size $2^{\Omega(n)}$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Choose $4n$ independent uniformly random distinct-vertex triples (sampling triples with replacement). For any Boolean word, the fraction of monochromatic triples is at least $1/4-O(1/n)$, by minimizing $\binom a3+\binom{n-a}3$. Hence the expected number of satisfying words is at most $2^n(3/4+O(1/n))^{4n}=o(1)$. For $t$ chosen owners and $u=\lfloor7t/4\rfloor$ vertices, the chance that all their triples lie there is at most $(u/n)^{3t}$. A union bound is
\[
\binom{4n}{t}\binom{n}{u}(u/n)^{3t}
\le [C(t/n)^{1/4}]^t
\]
for an absolute $C$, using the standard binomial bound (the case $u<3$ has probability zero). Sum over $1\le t\le\delta n$, choosing $C\delta^{1/4}<1/2$. Split at $\sqrt n$: the first sum tends to zero geometrically with ratio $Cn^{-1/8}$, the second is bounded by a geometric tail with ratio $1/2$. Thus both properties coexist. For any such small subregistry the number of variables occurring exactly once is at least twice the union size minus $3t$, hence greater than $t/2$. Every such subregistry is satisfiable: recursively remove an owner having a unique variable and extend by choosing that variable to satisfy NAE. Minimal UNSAT extraction preserves expansion, and flipping one literal of a deleted owner makes its deletion witness satisfy the original modified registry. This is existential extraction, not a polynomial acquisition algorithm.

Let $\nu(C)$ be the minimum number of original owners jointly implying a clause $C$ (including both CNF clauses of an owner). Axioms have measure at most one, tautologies zero, and resolution is subadditive. The empty clause has measure greater than $s=\lfloor\delta n\rfloor$. In any topologically ordered refutation there is a first line with measure greater than $s/2$, whose measure is at most $s$ by subadditivity. For a minimum supporting owner set of that size $t$, every unique variable must occur in $C$: otherwise removing its owner gives a word falsifying $C$ and satisfying the other owners, and changing that unique variable repairs the removed owner without changing $C$, a contradiction. Therefore the line has width greater than $t/2>s/4$. Initial width is three. Ben-Sasson--Wigderson, \emph{Short proofs are narrow}, Theorem 3.5 / Corollary 3.6 (author PDF \url{https://www.math.ias.edu/~avi/PUBLICATIONS/MYPAPERS/B-SW99/final.pdf}, pp. 8--9), converts this linear minimum width to size $2^{\Omega(n)}$, for general DAG resolution, not merely tree resolution. Renumbering occurring variables cannot increase the variable count; input bit length is $O(n\log n)$. No assertion of bounded occurrence, four-partition, logarithmic girth or explicit efficient generator for this family.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[No universal polynomial BS19 cap]\label{lem:da20-cap}
For every fixed polynomial cap $D(N)$, there are arbitrarily large raw ternary inputs on which the explicit BS19 projection-only procedure cannot finish with a correct decision under that cap, irrespective of pivot order. This remains true with paid resolution-compatible binary substitution, subsumption and polynomially many resolution derivations. In particular no aggregate polynomial potential can certify universal completion of this restricted dispatch.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
BS19 has at most $n$ elimination steps, at most $O(nD(N)^2)$ generated pair candidates, and polynomial work for its prescribed closure and representation. If it decided an UNSAT instance of Lemma~\ref{lem:da20-exp}, Lemma~\ref{lem:da20-sim} would give polynomial-size general resolution, contradicting the exponential size lower bound. It must decline or violate the charged cap. Neither a stronger proof system nor a compact gate whose evaluator is not resolution-simulable is excluded. In particular this is not an unrestricted runtime lower bound or simultaneous obstruction against the full cooperative portfolio.
\end{proof}

\section{M26: Compact gate-to-matching compilation and structural dual-rail limits}\label{sec:m26}
We address Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}, combining BS19/GD26/DA20's exact pivot semantics with M24's explicit relation selectors. This removes a degree obstruction, not the universal compatibility problem.
\begin{lemma}[Subcubic parsimonious tagged matching compiler]\label{lem:m26-selector}
Every nonempty explicit relation of $r$ rows admits an ordinary matching selector of maximum degree three with $4r-2$ vertices and exactly one perfect matching per row. Every finite acyclic Boolean circuit with fan-in at most two AND/OR/NOT gates, free inputs and pinned outputs compiles uniformly into disjoint constant-size such selectors with binary equality tags, preserving its accepted input words bijectively. Sparse occurrence-path tags have at most six bits set per edge and constant support per syndrome row. This tagged matching class is NP-complete for decision, and the compiler does not supply a universal exact polynomial compatibility algorithm.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Take two paths of $2r-1$ vertices and join corresponding odd positions by cross edges. Every perfect matching uses at least one cross edge by parity. If two consecutive selected cross positions existed, the intervening path segment would be odd and without any selected cross edge, impossible. The single selected edge leaves even paths with unique matchings. Label each cross edge by the chosen row's contribution; path edges are untagged. For the circuit use gate truth tables (at most three variables and four rows), free-input owners and unary output pins. Link all occurrences of each wire by a spanning path of XOR equalities, one syndrome coordinate per link, and target zero. A cross edge has at most six nonzero coordinates since at most three occurrences each meet at most two links; each link uses at most eight cross edges. Local matchings and their rows are bijective, and the syndrome is zero exactly when all copies agree. Topological functionality gives uniqueness given free inputs. Empty relations reject. Acquisition, verification, dictionary, topological reconstruction and dense tag storage are polynomial in explicit circuit volume, with linear sparse volume. Applying the compiler to arbitrary circuit SAT proves hardness and a matching with verified syndrome proves membership in NP. No claim of strict physical E4/B4 compilation.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Pure dual-rail matching firewall and syndrome switch rank]\label{lem:m26-rail}
Let a graph have distinct terminal pairs $(i0,i1)$. A boundary set $S$ is feasible when deleting precisely $S$ leaves a perfect matching. Suppose every untagged feasible boundary set deletes exactly one terminal per pair (structural one-hot, without an external filter). Then its nonempty boundary-word relation is a Cartesian product of unary sets. If edges additionally have $q$-bit XOR labels and feasibility requires one target syndrome, two target-feasible words at Hamming distance $d$ imply at least $2^{\max(0,d-q)}$ distinct target-feasible words obtained by independent-path switches. Thus a structurally one-hot pure matching gadget cannot represent nonproduct NAE or GD26's nonproduct gate; with tags an exact all-equal $d$-copy boundary relation requires $q\ge d-1$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Lift two boundary words to matchings leaving precisely their deleted terminals unmatched. Their symmetric difference is a disjoint union of alternating cycles and paths, with path endpoints the symmetric difference of the boundary sets. Switching any single path preserves untagged matching feasibility. Its two endpoints must be mates, since switching otherwise breaks structural one-hot. Consequently each differing bit can be flipped independently. Recombining coordinate values from arbitrary feasible words gives the full unary product. With tags, for two target-feasible words retain the $d$ disjoint paths and let the columns of a $q$ by $d$ binary matrix be their XOR label differences. Every vector in its kernel specifies a target-preserving switch and gives a distinct word. Rank-nullity yields the bound. Equality's two-word support forces the kernel dimension to be at most one, hence $q\ge d-1$. This bound is attained by independent one-bit path gadgets (three vertices, leaves as terminals), tagging their two edge alternatives to impose $d-1$ adjacent equalities. Equality is polynomial by Gaussian elimination. This is not a time lower bound and does not cover external one-hot filters, weighted optimum constraints, arbitrary decoders or nonmatching consumers.
\end{proof}
