\section{BS20: Gauge-normalized parametric 2-SAT and conflict-packet learning}\label{sec:bs20}
\paragraph{Status.} PROVED scoped, independent review pending; directly attacks Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}, not an unconditional closure. Integrates DS20 private-coordinate ideas, BA20 paid affine-flat consumers, and BS17 quadratic representation obstruction. A fixed exterior chart can use exact implication paths rather than enumerate internal assignments.
\begin{lemma}[Paid parametric implication consumer]\label{lem:bs20-param}
Consider an explicit affine-packet chart on private bits $z$ and exterior bits $y$, with actual guard already absorbed or involving only $y$. Suppose each packet observes at most two private coordinate bits, with independent columns for those bits. Gaussian elimination gives its forbidden event as $E_i y=h_i$ and $z_j=f_{ij}(y)$ for the observed private coordinates, where $f_{ij}$ is affine. For each private coordinate choose one incident affine function $g_j$, and set $u_j=z_j+g_j(y)$. Let $r$ be the rank of the exterior linear forms in all $E_i$ and $f_{ij}+g_j$ (include remaining exterior guard forms, or restrict to their consistent affine domain first). The complete chart is decidable and a witness is recoverable in $2^r\operatorname{poly}(N)$ bit work and polynomial serial space for polynomial-sized explicit charts and supplied partition. The exact feasible exterior projection has a polynomial-size Boolean circuit, even for large $r$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
On each attainable observation word, each owner is inactive or forbids one assignment of zero, one or two private bits. A zero-bit active owner rejects; others are unary/binary clauses. The actual private implication graph decides by mutually reachable complementary literals. For the compact circuit, encode each edge's presence as the conjunction of the owner's activation equations and normalized sign tests (OR over alternate owners), then compute reachability by the usual Boolean Floyd--Warshall recurrence and reject when complementary literals are mutually reachable or a zero-bit active owner exists. Its size is polynomial, and every edge predicate has its actual affine coefficients. Enumerate only a basis of the observation forms, lifting by Gaussian elimination to the actual $y$; each resulting 2-SAT witness lifts by $z_j=u_j+g_j(y)$ and the original source map. Charge rank computation, graph construction, reachability, failed jobs, basis and guard tests, consumer access and source verification. Polynomial-sized circuit alone does not imply inexpensive existential decision over $y$. Arbitrary guards coupling private bits are not covered by this statement.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Exact coordinate gauge rank and discovery]\label{lem:bs20-gauge}
For an unpinned signed NAE registry on distinct variables per owner, take exterior coordinates $Y$ meeting every owner so each owner has at most two private variables. Assume no additional predicates and remove unused variables. If the primal graph has $c$ connected components, the observation rank of the normalization in Lemma~\ref{lem:bs20-param} is exactly $|Y|-c$. For each owner choose an exterior anchor and use its signed value as the forbidden common value. For each private variable choose as gauge the value of one incident exterior anchor. All activation and normalized sign forms are differences of exterior coordinates. On a connected component an exterior set of size at most $h$ can be discovered or ruled out in $3^h\operatorname{poly}(N)$ bit work.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The difference graph on exterior coordinates has edges joining each owner's anchor to its other exterior coordinates, and joining a private variable's reference anchor to the anchors of all owners containing that variable. Every primal connected component maps onto exactly one connected exterior difference graph: each owner and each incidence through a shared private coordinate lies in one such component. Conversely every difference edge stays within its primal component. The binary edge difference rowspace of a connected graph on $t$ vertices has rank $t-1$; signs affect only constants. Fix one actual exterior coordinate to zero per primal component by independent global complement symmetry; this loses no SAT witness. For discovery, starting with empty $Y$, any owner with more than two private coordinates requires choosing at least one of any three of those coordinates. An owner of size at most two with no exterior also requires at least one of its coordinates. Branch on those at most three choices, stopping at budget $h$. Check all scopes at each node; the branching exhausts every eligible set of size at most $h$. Thus a logarithmic cap per independent component gives a uniform polynomial terminal including discovery. On any connected $d$-regular ternary registry, $|Y|\ge m/d=n/3$ by incidence counting, so every such coordinate partition has $r\ge n/3-1$. This falsifies a universal small raw gauge-rank shortcut, not general affine backdoors, nonlinear changes, or a runtime lower bound.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Conflict-path affine packet and exact coverage gate]\label{lem:bs20-learn}
For a failed exterior job in Lemma~\ref{lem:bs20-param}, retain two directed paths between a complementary literal pair, or the active zero-bit owner's equations. Collect the actual activation equations and normalized sign values of the owners supplying the path edges. Their conjunction is a consistent affine packet containing that job's exterior word and excluding no feasible exterior word. Such a packet is constructible and verifiable in polynomial time. A polynomial capped affine-flat complement consumer (BA20), with actual guard/version keys, may use these deductions to select an uncovered exterior word or certify that all words are excluded; the number of acquired certificates and complement pieces must both be separately capped and charged.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
On every word of the packet the same owner activations and private forbidden signs hold, so the same two paths or zero-bit contradiction hold. No global forced-information claim about private coordinates follows. The packet can be installed as an unconditional exterior exclusion within the chart guard. Reclose after each accepted deduction; rank-one forbidden packets give necessary opposite equations. The complement of an affine packet in a current affine flat is an explicit disjoint union of at most the number of independent new equations, by first violated equation, so exact subtraction and reconstruction are polynomial per bounded piece. A supplied piece cap and iteration cap give a polynomial decline-capable procedure only; neither complete coverage nor continued progress follows. Circuit reachability, exact packet verification and reconstruction do not require a semantic-equivalence oracle.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Opposite quadratic-chain obstruction to separate conflict coverage]\label{lem:bs20-chain}
For every $k\ge1$, an explicit $O(k)$-owner affine chart has two disjoint private implication components with common exterior $(x,y)\in\mathbb F_2^{2k}$. Each component's fixed-exterior feasibility is 2-SAT. Their conjunction is UNSAT, but every certificate consisting only of an explicit cover by affine packets each certified by one original component needs at least $2^k+1$ packets. A one-endpoint change gives a SAT neighbor. Joint quadratic cancellation decides this constructed family in polynomial time.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
In each component impose private endpoints $z_0=0,z_k=b$ and transitions $z_i+z_{i-1}=x_i y_i$. For each of the four exterior input pairs, activate the two binary forbidden assignments of consecutive private states that violate the transition. These are explicit affine packets of rank at most four; the endpoint packets are unary. The conditional implication graph is a chain of parity equalities or disequalities with endpoint pins. Thus the feasible exterior set is precisely $q(x,y)=b$ where $q=\sum_i x_i y_i$ over $\mathbb F_2$. Choose $b=0,1$ in the two components. For any exterior word exactly one component fails. A packet certified by only one component must lie in its failing quadratic level. By the BS17 polarization argument any affine flat contained in either level has dimension at most $k$: its direction is totally isotropic for the nondegenerate symplectic polar form. The levels have sizes $2^{2k-1}\pm2^{k-1}$, so their separate covers need at least $2^{k-1}+1$ and $2^{k-1}$ packets. This includes adaptive implication-path certificates, but not arbitrary cross-component certificate combinations. Changing one endpoint to make both target bits zero admits the all-zero witness. In contrast, sum the transition identities in each component over $\mathbb F_2$, cancel the internal state bits and then subtract the two common quadratic expressions to obtain $0=1$. All identities follow by checking each constant-size local relation; in the supplied chain registry this is linear many polynomial-size operations. This is a constructive nonresolution escape, not an unrestricted lower bound. General acquisition of cross-component quadratic cancellation or another polynomial joint consumer remains OPEN.
\end{proof}

These finite loops are reference executions, not evidence of polynomial covering. Checker filters learned forbidden packets, including rank-one opposite-parity requirements, rather than implementing full Gaussian/cooperative closure; plain and learned source comparisons have no rank-one packets. Large source packets are constructed from actual implication paths; independent exhaustive replay only on small controls. \section{DO21: Dense-affine local-support kernel and affine-rank width}\label{sec:do21}
Combine DS15 Lemma~\ref{lem:ds15-core} with RT26 Lemma~\ref{lem:rt26-eight} on the same raw critical family, extending BH20 Lemma~\ref{lem:bh20-width} beyond actual coordinate scopes. This is an attack on Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}, not a complete decision terminal.

\begin{lemma}[Small dense-guard kernel]\label{lem:do21-kernel}
Suppose the raw rank-two NAE owner planes $U_i$ satisfy $R(J)=\dim\sum_{i\in J}U_i\ge3|J|/2$ for every owner set of size at most $s_0\ge1$. Let $H$ be any affine guard rowspace of rank $r$, with consistent actual right-hand side, and put $k=\max(0,2r-2)$. If $2k\le s_0$, there is a single owner subset $K_H$, of size at most $k$, independent of the right-hand side, such that all subregistries of at most $s_0$ owners have a satisfying extension of the guard iff $K_H$ does. If $s_0/m$ is bounded below by a fixed positive constant, acquisition and exact feasibility take $2^{O(r)}\operatorname{poly}(N)$ bit work; for fixed $r\le C\log(N+2)$ this is polynomial on the certified domain.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Define $d_H(J)=|J|-\dim((H+\sum_{i\in J}U_i)/H)$. Supermodularity follows from submodularity of rank. For $|J|\le s_0$, $d_H(J)\le r-|J|/2$. A minimal positive-deficiency set $D$ has $d_H(D)=1$ (deletion cannot increase row rank), hence if small then $|D|\le k$. These sets are exactly circuits of the Rado matroid on owner indices, whose independent sets admit independent representative basis rows modulo $H$. Let $K_H$ be the union of all circuits of size at most $s_0$. Add such circuits in any order. When adding a circuit not contained in the current nonempty union, its intersection with the union is a proper subset of the circuit and has nonpositive deficiency. Supermodularity preserves positive deficiency. The new union has size at most $2k\le s_0$, so the rank-slack bound again limits its size to $k$. The first circuit has size at most $k$, and if there are none the union is empty.

For any $J$ of size at most $s_0$, the smallest maximizing subset $C_J$ of DS15 (in the quotient by $H$) is exactly the union of circuits inside $J$: deletion of an owner decreases the Rado matroid nullity iff it is not a coloop, equivalently belongs to some circuit. Thus $C_J\subseteq K_H$. A satisfying assignment of $K_H$ under the guard satisfies $C_J$ and lifts to a model of $J$ preserving $H$ and $C_J$ observations, by the independent-transversal construction in DS15. Rank-zero owners in the quotient may be retained as loops for this structural argument; a vacuous owner never obstructs a witness and a whole-fiber forbidden owner is detected by closure. Conversely $K_H$ is itself small.

For $k=0$ return the empty kernel. Otherwise partition the $m$ owner IDs into $B=\min(m,\lceil2mk/s_0\rceil)$ near-equal blocks (take $s_0\le m$ without loss). Enumerate unions of $\min(k,B)$ blocks. Each union has size at most $s_0$: singleton blocks suffice if $B=m$, otherwise $k\lceil m/B\rceil\le s_0/2+k\le s_0$. Every circuit of size at most $k$ is contained in some such union. Compute the DS15 core of each union by at most $|J|+1$ deterministic matroid intersections and take their union. The number of unions is at most $2^B=2^{O(k)}$ for fixed $s_0/m>0$. This discovers the kernel without enumerating all small owner sets. Enumerate at most $3k$ actual variables of the kernel, checking each word against the actual guard by Gaussian extension on remaining coordinates. This pays at most $2^{3k}\operatorname{poly}(N)$ additional operations. Any specified small regional witness lifts with polynomial work using DS15. All matrix acquisition, failed tests and temporary storage are charged. The rank-slack promise is not claimed efficiently recognizable; a verified subset contradiction is sound without it, but positive saturation is promised-domain only.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Coherent arbitrary affine-scope supports]\label{lem:do21-coherent}
Under Lemma~\ref{lem:do21-kernel}, let $P_H$ be the guard functionals on $H$ accepted by its kernel. For nested eligible rowspaces $H\subseteq H'$, restriction maps $P_{H'}$ onto $P_H$, and all these sets are nonempty. Thus bounded-rank affine-scope local consistency on the raw family can simultaneously retain nonempty coherent supports, even for dense observations.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every small owner set is SAT without a guard by Rado, so a model of $K_H$ supplies a member of $P_H$. Any $b'\in P_{H'}$ restricts to a locally feasible $b$. Conversely for $b\in P_H$, the small set $K_{H'}$ is satisfiable under $b$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:do21-kernel}; take the resulting assignment's observation word on $H'$. It belongs to $P_{H'}$. Acquisition is paid for each specified eligible rowspace, not for all rowspaces at once.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Dense affine-rank width obstruction]\label{lem:do21-width}
On the critical RT26 family, every semantic refutation using at most $q\ge2$ earlier relations per inference, with each relation an arbitrary Boolean function of declared affine observations (including all guard rows for implications), has a line of observation rank greater than $\lfloor s_0/q\rfloor/2$, for $s_0=\lfloor\delta n\rfloor$ and sufficiently large $n$. In particular a fixed-premise logarithmic-affine-rank derivation cannot refute the family. This does not bound the size of unrestricted circuits or proof systems.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The RT26 small-set expansion and sufficiently large incidence girth imply the raw rank-slack hypothesis. On each connected component with $t\ge4$ owners, raw rank is $|V|-1>7t/4-1\ge3t/2$, since the observation rows generate all pair differences on its variable component. For $t\le3$ the incidence graph is a forest and rank is $2t$. Sum over components. Also $s_0/m$ is bounded below.

For any relation $Q(Ax)$, let $J$ be a minimum supporting owner set and let $r=\operatorname{rank}(A)$. If $0<|J|\le s_0$, compute the DS15 structural core $C_J$ modulo $\operatorname{row}(A)$. Every word satisfying $C_J$ lifts to one satisfying $J$ preserving $Ax$, so $C_J$ entails $Q$ and minimality gives $C_J=J$. A nonempty smallest maximizer has positive deficiency. Thus $1\le d_{\operatorname{row}(A)}(J)\le r-|J|/2$. This argument does not require the kernel acquisition condition $2k\le s_0$. The supporting-owner measure is subadditive over sound inferences, initially at most one, and the final contradiction has measure greater than $s_0$ by unguarded Rado feasibility. For $s_0\ge q$ the first line of measure greater than $\lfloor s_0/q\rfloor$ has measure at most $q\lfloor s_0/q\rfloor\le s_0$. Its declared rank exceeds $\lfloor s_0/q\rfloor/2$. A compact high-rank function, unbounded-premise global inference or other nonlocal algorithm is not excluded.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Universal gap and collaboration.}

On RT26 the root kernel is empty despite global UNSAT. Thus even combining bounded affine observation scope and bounded-premise exact nonlinear inferences cannot universally establish contradiction. \section{GD28: Factored affine-guard coverage by observation interfaces}\label{sec:gd28}
\paragraph{Status.} PROVED scoped; independent review pending. Responds directly to BS20 conflict-packet learning and BA20 complement piece blowup, S26 activated dependencies. It does not assume semantic coverage free.
\begin{lemma}[Exact two-output rank-boundary consumer]\label{lem:gd28-rank}
Let a polynomial-size supplied binary Boolean formula tree have leaves testing affine packets $Ax=b$ or their complements on actual exterior coordinates. An actual affine guard is first absorbed by Gaussian parametrization (inconsistent guard rejects). For each subtree $t$, let $U_t$ be the span of all its observation rows, $V_t$ the span outside it, and $B_t=U_t\cap V_t$. Let $w=\max_t\dim B_t$. Both existence of a true word and existence of a false word, with actual witnesses, can be decided in $2^{O(w)}\operatorname{poly}(N)$ bit work and space, including acquisition of all bases, compatibility tests and reconstruction. In particular this is a paid polynomial consumer for a supplied polynomial-size tree with $w\le C\log_2(N+2)$ for fixed $C$. No bound on the individual leaf ranks is required.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For each $t$, tabulate attainable pairs $(\lambda,z)$ where $\lambda$ is a linear functional on $B_t$ and $z$ is the Boolean output. Retain one representative extension or sufficient Gaussian equations and child pointers per pair. At a leaf, under $\lambda$, packet truth is a consistent linear system with all packet rows; packet falsity exists iff at least one row can take its opposite value, each tested by Gaussian elimination. Complement swaps outputs. At an internal node with children of spans $U_1,U_2$ and outside span $V$, the child boundaries are $U_1\cap(U_2+V)$ and $U_2\cap(U_1+V)$. Their intersection includes $U_1\cap U_2$; moreover $(U_1+U_2)\cap V\subseteq B_1+B_2$: if $u_1+u_2\in V$, then $u_1\in U_2+V$ and $u_2\in U_1+V$. Thus agreeing child boundary functionals glue their representatives on $U_1\cap U_2$, and uniquely determine the parent boundary functional. They extend to the sum of spans and to the whole exterior space. Conversely any actual word yields the child pairs; replacing either representative by another with the same boundary and output cannot change compatibility or parent boundary. Apply the Boolean gate to the two outputs. At most $2^{2w+2}$ child pairs per node require polynomial Gaussian work. A root pair has empty boundary; recover a functional by gluing the stored representatives, then solve for actual exterior coordinates and verify the original formula and guard. All retained equations can be bounded by polynomial tree size per entry; failed pairs, basis discovery, and consumer accesses are paid. This is not an assertion that an arbitrary shared DAG can be unfolded cheaply; a Tseitin adapter requires separate charging and a new width check.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Small geometric guard graph does not imply cheap coverage]\label{lem:gd28-path}
For any 3-CNF $F(y)$, build one private equality path between two opposite pinned terminals per clause. Each path has one edge per literal, activated exactly when that literal is false. Paths share only terminals. The activated private equations are inconsistent iff some original clause is false: a complete path forces opposite pins equal, and if no path is complete the terminals belong to distinct connected components and each component admits a constant assignment. The graph is series-parallel with constant graph treewidth, each edge activation uses one literal, and size is linear. Thus existential exterior feasibility is NP-complete and universal rejection coNP-complete even here. These are reductions, not separations. A compact path graph, even without general private 2-SAT, is insufficient unless shared exterior guard information is controlled.
\end{lemma}

\section{DA21: Direct-sum indicator spans and alternating affine closure}\label{sec:da21}
\paragraph{Status.} PROVED scoped, independent review pending. This attacks BS20 joint high-degree cancellation and Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}. GD28 pays joint boundary width for Boolean composition; the following linear consumer instead pays the sum of individual packet widths, not the product. It is not a complete SAT decision procedure.
\begin{lemma}[Exact simultaneous indicator evaluation span]\label{lem:da21-span}
Let $P_j=\{x:A_jx=b_j\}$ be explicitly specified Boolean affine packets, $G$ an actual affine guard and $f_\ell$ supplied XOR sums of packet indicators (with the constant allowed). Fix a common order of the $n$ source bits. Intersect each packet with $G$, include $G$ and $G\cap\{x_i=1\}$, and discard inconsistent systems. For each resulting system $A_jx=b_j$, let $U_{jt},V_{jt}$ be the column spans before and after cut $t$; define $W=\max_t\sum_j2^{\dim(U_{jt}\cap V_{jt})}$. There is a deterministic algorithm with bit work and space polynomial in the explicit encoded length and $W$ that computes the exact linear span
\[
E=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F_2}\{(f_1(x),\ldots,f_m(x),1,x):x\in G\}.
\]
It stores actual representative words for a spanning set. For any fixed polynomial cap in the original input length on the individual-state sum, it discovers the required span or declines with polynomial charged work. It does not enumerate the Cartesian product of the packet states.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
After reading prefix $x_{\le t}$, each packet retains its residual syndrome $s=b_j+A_{j,\le t}x_{\le t}$ if $s\in V_{jt}$, otherwise enters a permanent rejecting sink represented by the zero vector. The live syndromes lie in $(b_j+U_{jt})\cap V_{jt}$, empty or a coset of $U_{jt}\cap V_{jt}$. Use a one-hot vector for a live syndrome. Each next bit acts by a linear map on these vectors: send the basis vector for $s$ to that for $s+a_{j,t+1}x_{t+1}$ if live, else to zero. Take the direct sum across packets. At each layer apply both maps only to an independent basis of reachable prefix vectors, then retain an independent subset of the results by Gaussian elimination. Inductively their span is the span of all actual prefix vectors, since the maps are linear. The basis can consist of actual prefix representatives by retaining the original candidate upon a successful pivot; keep its actual prefix. At the final layer the only live syndrome is zero, so the individual states are indicators. Apply the supplied linear map for the XOR sums, the guard indicator and coordinate indicators; outside the guard every output is zero. This proves the exact span identity, including a zero guard. Suffix-span membership, row normalization and all state labels use polynomial bit length in the input. An implementation generates at most twice the previous basis size in candidate vectors per layer; a live state coordinate not reached by those candidates could not occur in their span. Thus dynamic state discovery with a fixed cap, including failed probes, is sound. Gaussian elimination, bit vectors, prefix retention and state dictionaries cost at most a fixed polynomial in input size and cap, with no semantic equality oracle. Witnesses for a nonzero linear functional are obtained from actual representatives. This is elementary white-box linear-span computation related to read-once oblivious algebraic branching programs; no black-box PIT theorem is required.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Affine relaxation, feedback and paid reserve]\label{lem:da21-close}
For the equations $f_\ell(x)=0$ on $G$, compute $H=\{x:(0,\ldots,0,1,x)\in E\}$. If empty, UNSAT is certified. Otherwise $H$ is an affine space containing every feasible word. Its annihilator equations are unconditional necessary information within $G$. If an actual representative satisfies every equation, it is a checked witness. One may include the consequences $x_i f_\ell=0$ via intersecting each indicator packet in the expression with $x_i=1$, or any explicitly charged fixed list of such multipliers. For a fixed root registry and a fixed polynomial cap on every direct-sum phase, alternating this procedure and Gaussian rank-one forbidden-packet closure, adding only independent necessary affine equations, is polynomial in the original input length, or declines. The proof does not require a bounded polynomial degree of individual indicator expressions.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every feasible word contributes its evaluation vector, hence belongs to $H$. Row-reduce the evaluation span with the constraint coordinates first and constant next; this decides whether a row with zero constraints and constant one exists and supplies one affine base point and the remaining direction rows. Annihilator equations follow by ordinary elimination. Intersect new equations with the current guard, retaining original provenance. For a registry of individually forbidden packets, an empty packet after quotient is removed, a packet equal to the guard rejects, and a rank-one forbidden packet forces the opposite equation. Do not apply those singleton rules to individual summands of a general XOR equation. Reclose after each strict deduction, and at stagnation. Guard rank increases at most $n$ times; keep original equations plus at most $n$ independent new equations, rather than retaining all generated consequences across rounds. The one-coordinate multiplier list has at most $(n+1)(m+n)$ entries and polynomial explicit input length; intersections are charged. Thus at most $n+1$ polynomial capped rounds (and polynomially many local closure scans) give same-execution polynomial $T,S$, and $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$. In a recursive portfolio all invocations, including declines, still require the original aggregate reserve. The affine space $H$ need not equal actual support or its affine hull. In particular the Fano UNSAT control below has full $H$ even after the chosen multiplier pass, so universal progress does not follow.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Unbounded-degree BS20 chain extension]\label{lem:da21-chain}
For integers $k,d\ge2$, use $k$ disjoint exterior blocks of $d$ bits and transitions $z_i+z_{i-1}=\prod_{j=1}^d x_{ij}$. This has an explicit $O(kd)$-packet private two-bit representation: forbid both inconsistent private parity words when all exterior bits are one; for each exterior bit equal to zero forbid the two inconsistent private words for parity zero. Endpoints $z_0=0,z_k=b$ are pinned. Thus its projected equation is $q(x)=b$, $q=\sum_i\prod_j x_{ij}$, proved by summing authenticated transition equations and reconstructing all private states by prefix parity. Two copies with opposite endpoints are UNSAT; same endpoints zero have the zero witness. The projected equations are XORs of coordinate-cube indicators, each individual live width one in every coordinate order, and their joint contradiction is certified by Lemma~\ref{lem:da21-span} with polynomial work independent of $d$. Separate affine covers certified by one component still require at least $2^k+1$ pieces: restrict the last $d-2$ bits of every block to one, obtaining BS20's quadratic levels and its bound. This is an escape from separate coverage, not a universal algorithm for arbitrary parametric implication components.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The transition packets described in the statement enforce exactly the indicated parity: if every exterior bit is one only the all-one activation applies, otherwise at least one zero activation applies and all applicable zero activations agree. The sum telescopes to $z_k+z_0=q$. Prefix parity is a polynomial witness lift. Opposite equations sum to $1=0$; the span algorithm discovers this identity from the supplied indicator representations. Restriction of any affine flat is empty or affine, so the quadratic separate-cover lower bound transfers. No claim is made that arbitrary implication components admit a polynomial-size XOR-of-packets projection, or that a jointly feasible syndrome is determined by its affine span.
\end{proof}

\section{BW21: Exact affine boundary classification for pure balance and feedback quotient}\label{sec:bw21}
\paragraph{Status.} PROVED scoped, independent review pending. Addresses U-PROGRESS by distinguishing which actual affine guards can be absorbed into tag-free native balance geometry and by consuming DA21's actual RT26 cuts without branching. It neither asserts universal tag elimination nor complete semantic closure.
\begin{lemma}[Pair-switch generation of affine hull]\label{lem:bw21-hull}
Consider a finite signed B4 gadget with exactly two active ports per vertex, signed internal wires, optional fixed boundary ports, and $d$ remaining free boundary ports, each appearing once. Let $R$ be its exact nonempty boundary relation and $a\in R$. Then
\[
\operatorname{aff}(R)=a+\operatorname{span}\{e_i+e_j:a+e_i+e_j\in R,\ i<j\}.
\]
In particular the affine hull is specified by one parity equation per component of the graph on free ports whose edges are the displayed feasible pair switches (isolated vertices give fixed bits). The hull and witness lifts for its generators are deterministically obtainable using at most $1+\binom d2$ polynomial matching feasibility calls (up to a constant factor for the initial witness).
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Compare lifts of $a,b\in R$. At each B4 vertex the changed ports split equally into increases and decreases, so pair increases with decreases locally. Along each signed wire either both ends change or neither changes. The changed ports, local pairings and changed wires therefore decompose into paths between distinct free boundary ports and cycles. Fixed ports never change. Flipping exactly one path preserves all signed wires and integer balances even if the path visits one vertex twice: it flips one increase and one decrease for each local pairing traversed. Hence each path yields a feasible pair switch from $a$. The sum of their boundary differences is $a+b$. This proves both inclusions; weight-two generators along graph edges span exactly the even subspace in each connected component. For the algorithm, encode a B4 by four port nodes and two private nodes each adjacent to all four port nodes; a perfect matching leaves exactly two ports to be matched outside the gadget. An equal wire is an edge between its port nodes; an unequal wire is subdivided by one node, forcing exactly one end matched to the wire. A fixed active port is removed, and a fixed inactive port has no exterior edge. To allow unpinned boundary values, connect each free port to its own dummy and make the dummies a clique; optionally add one extra dummy. Try both choices, permitting either parity of the number of used exterior edges. Conversely any feasible lift extends in one of these two matching graphs. With all free boundary bits pinned, the same construction without dummies tests a word. Thus one can find a base and test all pair flips by ordinary deterministic perfect matching, retaining actual witnesses; size $O(d^2+|G|)$ in vertices/edges up to encoding overhead, all failed queries paid. Empty support is detected by the initial calls. The hull is not in general equal to nonlinear support.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Exact affine guard realizability on actual single ports]\label{lem:bw21-affine}
A nonempty affine relation $C=\{x:Ax=b\}$ on actual free ports has an exact pure signed B4 realization with optional fixed ports iff its direction space is the direct sum of even subspaces on disjoint coordinate blocks. Equivalently $C$ is a conjunction of one parity equation on each block of a partition (singletons allowed). This criterion is polynomially decidable from $A,b$. For a consistent system, partition columns of $A$ by equality; the space generated by weight-two kernel vectors has dimension $d-t$, where $t$ is the number of column classes. Acceptance is exactly $\dim\ker A=d-t$. A zero column implies rejection for nonempty coordinate scope. Realization and witness reconstruction use $O(d)$ B4 vertices and fixed ports.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Necessity follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:bw21-hull}. Since $A(e_i+e_j)=0$ iff columns coincide, the pair span is contained in the kernel and has dimension $d-t$; equality characterizes the requisite direction space. A zero column gives a weight-one kernel vector, which no such pair span contains. Conversely $K_4$ with one free port per vertex realizes the entire even four-bit parity relation: for zero exterior ones choose a four-cycle internally, for four choose a perfect matching, for two choose a spanning path with endpoints at the two active exterior ports; odd totals violate integer degree summation. Sign a boundary wire for odd parity. Use pins on spare ports for ternary and unary parity; concatenate ternary parity gates along a private accumulator for an arbitrary block, computing intermediate bits by prefix parity and lifting each gate by the explicit construction. Use disjoint blocks. No boundary bit needs duplication. This proves exactness in both directions, including lift cost. If the model forbids fixed ports entirely, complement invariance further requires even block sizes; even-size blocks can use four-port parity gates chained on private wires, with a two-port equality wire as the base. The pinned result must not be applied to a pin-free chart without a separately certified pin adapter. A parity checksum output can embed a general affine code in an even code, but does not force it into this class.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Same-source native quotient and reserve.} On signed NAE sources the actual pair equations $x_i+x_j=b$ are consumed by a signed disjoint-set quotient. Each owner with opposite literals on the same quotient bit is tautological; with two equal literal occurrences and a distinct quotient bit it forces a signed pair equation; with all three equal it is contradictory. Reclose after strict joins, preserving source IDs and xor offsets. These rules are pointwise equivalences under the authenticated cuts. In the I21 duplicated-B4 representation a surviving variable occurring $q\ge1$ times needs $2q$ physical boundary ports; BW20's equality chain uses exactly $q-1$ genuine E4 vertices (zero for $q=1$). Sum over live variables and use the tag-free wire replacement. The quotient can be compiled from scratch with linear-size native graph in the surviving occurrence count and reconstructs via saved DSU offsets, arbitrary choices for unconstrained components, and the native adapter. It never needs to impose the learned pair equations as extra E4 tags. A strict join or removed owner decreases the source-level potential $1+n_{\rm active}+m$ when charged to its actual source representation, with at most $n$ independent joins and polynomial scans, including a stagnation scan; physical tag count by itself need not decrease under every join. This pays one normalization pass, not arbitrary repeated growth, discovery of new cuts, or every recursive occurrence. No representative-only cut is asserted as a root consequence.
\paragraph{Executed collaborative controls.} Immutable RT26 85e959ac and DA21 6d991774 supply actual zero-based owners, forbidden sign words, and accepted pair cuts/RHS (hex masks). The empty guard is retained, and the first-sign SAT neighbor uses its own separate cuts. All 150249 assertions passed in a finite JS checker: exhaustive original-versus-quotient support comparisons, $K_4$ parity gate (3 lifts for 0000/1111, 2 for each weight-two word, 0 for odd), and affine pair-span classifications. For root $n=9,12,15$, native quotient alone is OPEN (9,9,16 owners; 18,18,34 genuine tags); importing DA21 cuts leaves 6 owners and 12 tags at $n=9$ and gives explicit local contradictions at $n=12,15$. All roots reference UNSAT. Neighbor supports 24/64/96 preserved exactly; remaining owners 1/0/8, tags 0/0/15 versus 18/18/34. These are symbolic native counts, not new physical graph or matching executions. In each root and neighbor, the separately tested parity-checksum extension of the accepted guard has kernel dimension exceeding the pair-span dimension by one, so it cannot be directly realized on those single boundary ports with pure B4 even with pins. The actual pair quotient bypasses that representational obstruction by identifying coordinates instead of constructing a separate guard gadget. No new DA21 cut acquisition was executed; the checker consumes authenticated peer results, replays exact local closure and verifies models exhaustively on these small cases. It did not execute the larger BW17/K16 native replay, full portfolio, physical memory or formal kernel verification. \href{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/c2643c9019b7bb45ced4a5e17deab666184506cf}{Checker}, \href{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/cbb0e2c61e3114ca9ba20a36f09018380724949d}{results}.
\paragraph{Remaining dependency and collaboration.} U-PROGRESS, universal SEM/CLOSE and unconditional COST remain OPEN. The affine classification is an exact boundary obstruction, not a lower bound against a solver allowed to change coordinate representations. It suggests an adaptive dispatch: quotient actual pair cuts first, absorb certified partition-parity guards directly, then pay matching or other consumers. What is missing is a uniform mechanism obtaining enough compatible deductions, or another exact contracting step, at arbitrary fixed points. Background: Kazda, Kolmogorov and Rol\'inek, Even Delta-Matroids and the Complexity of Planar Boolean CSPs, \href{https://doi.org/10.1145/3230649}{ACM TALG 2018}; the above specialized proof is direct and does not assume a general tagged-matching solver.


\section{M27: Exact positive-energy matching adapter and planar crossover obstruction}\label{sec:m27}
\paragraph{Status and target.} PROVED scoped, independent review pending. Attack Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} using the actual BS20 learned packets and GD28 coverage, S26 private projection and RT26 critical controls. The aim is to eliminate tags by ordinary planar weighted matching, not to treat compact coverage as decision. This attempt proves a conditional adapter and falsifies universal progress in its specified representation.
\begin{lemma}[Exact pair-energy criterion and paid reweighting]\label{lem:m27-fourier}
Let $A x=b$ be a consistent affine forbidden packet with independent rows over $\mathbb F_2$, rank $r$. Its violation indicator is a constant plus field-free pair interactions on the same coordinates iff its rowspace consists only of zero and weight-two vectors. Thus $r\le2$; rank one gives a pair and rank two a triangle. Given an explicit chart of such or higher-rank packets and a supplied planar allowed pair graph, let mandatory packets describe the actual source/guard and optional packets be authenticated consequences within that guard. If $L=\sum_i2^{r_i}$ is polynomial in original $N$, one can deterministically acquire, or reject the existence of, positive mandatory and nonnegative optional rational weights whose summed violation energy has only allowed pair terms and a constant, in polynomial bit time. When acquired, exact decision and witness lift are polynomial by ordinary planar dual matching. A rejection of reweighting is not an UNSAT decision.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Write $\chi_s(x)=(-1)^{s^Tx}$. The indicator is $2^{-r}\sum_{u\in\mathbb F_2^r}(-1)^{u^Tb}\chi_{A^Tu}(x)$. Every mask is distinct and every coefficient nonzero. Fourier uniqueness yields the iff. In a subspace of pair masks any distinct edges must intersect (otherwise their sum has weight four). Two such edges generate a triangle; no edge outside that triangle intersects all three. Thus the dimension is at most two. Inconsistent packets can be dropped, and a rank-zero forbidden packet either is empty or gives immediate contradiction.
Expand each packet after Gaussian preprocessing; solve a rational LP with mandatory weights at least one, optional weights nonnegative, and equations setting every disallowed coefficient to zero. Any positive mandatory weighting can be scaled to this normalization. The weighted sum is nonnegative and vanishes exactly on the original source solutions under the authenticated guard, since optional packets are necessary exclusions. On success scale rational denominators and rewrite each signed pair coefficient as a constant plus a nonnegative penalty for violating its preferred edge xor $p_e$. The actual edge xor vector $c$ is a cut iff its cycle sums vanish. In a planar embedding the face boundary vectors span the cycle space, so the defect $z=c+p$ is exactly a dual $T$-join with prescribed face parity. Nonnegative minimum-weight $T$-join is solved by shortest path distances on the dual and minimum-weight perfect matching of the odd vertices, taking path sums modulo two. Reconstruct actual spins by tree integration, checking all edges, the guard and original source, and compare the exact minimum energy with zero. Disconnected components are treated separately. Gaussian expansion, LP with polynomial bit complexity, embedding and path/matching certificates and source lift are charged. A different graph, basis or auxiliary representation requires its own acquisition and verification; no free discovery of the allowed graph or semantic closure. A mandatory unique high mask, or same-sign coefficients with at least one mandatory contributor, excludes quadratic reweighting.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Raw edge support and residual surface syndrome]\label{lem:m27-genus}
In a linear signed NAE3 registry, positive reweighting of original violation indicators cannot remove a primal edge. For a connected simple graph of $n$ vertices and $e$ edges its orientable genus $g$ satisfies $e\le3n-6+6g$ (for $n\ge3$). On any cellular orientable embedding, the face-cycle span has codimension $2g$ in the cycle space. Thus ordinary dual parity omits $2g$ independent cut-consistency equations, which must be retained by this particular dual representation.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Each ternary owner is a rank-two packet of pair differences and contributes three nonzero pair coefficients of magnitude $1/4$. Linearity means each pair has just one owner, hence no cancellation under positive weighting. The edge bound follows from Euler and the face-length bound for simple graphs (or triangulation). In a connected cellular embedding the face boundary rank is $f-1$ over $\mathbb F_2$ (dual connectedness), cycle rank $e-n+1$, and Euler $n-e+f=2-2g$ gives the difference $2g$. No requirement to enumerate all handle syndromes follows, and this is not a lower bound on arbitrary solvers or changed representations.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[No field-free planar crossing-equality ground-state gadget]\label{lem:m27-cross}
A planar graph embedded in a disk with distinct boundary terminals $t_1,t_2,t_3,t_4$ in cyclic order cannot realize precisely $\{0000,0101,1010,1111\}$ as the projection of the ground states of an arbitrary field-free pairwise xor energy, regardless of auxiliary size. The same holds for feasible assignments of complement-invariant hard local relations whose \emph{primal} graph is so embedded.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Suppose full ground states $a,b$ have boundary words $0000,0101$. For any two ground states, the induced subgraph on the disagreement set has components that can be switched independently from the first state. Edge-energy changes add because no edge joins distinct components, each change is nonnegative by optimality, and their sum is zero. For hard relations each owner touches at most one disagreement component, so each component switch also preserves feasibility. For $D=\{v:a_v\ne b_v\}$ the second and fourth terminals must lie in one component: switching a component containing only one would give a forbidden boundary word. Therefore there is a path connecting $t_2,t_4$ in $D$. Complement invariance makes $\bar b$ another ground state/feasible assignment. Its disagreement set with $a$ is the complement of $D$, and the same reasoning connects $t_1,t_3$ there. These are vertex-disjoint paths connecting alternating terminals, impossible in a disk. Signed ternary NAE incidence embeddings admit primal triangle expansion, but arbitrary four-ary incidence embeddings need not. The statement does not exclude fields, arbitrary higher-arity native E4/B4 relations, tags, nonplanar lifts or external decoding.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Executed joint comparison.} SAME BS19 BW17/K16 immutable source \texttt{ff92a1c3d44e4b48dc9a7bf215825075396cae5a}, BS20 \texttt{c736065bdc4742f72b2dd342bc6ba82c70eda701}, RT26 \texttt{85e959ac861572a2411b9858da0d58d7c72ac780}, actual empty guard and exterior IDs. Import the learned masks by restoring the actual gauge representative in odd masks (global complement invariance); check both coordinate supports initially and after import, no pins. Independent fixed-exterior implication replay on 2048 words per chart: raw 1412 covered, 99 feasible; K16 128 covered, 96 feasible; every covered word infeasible, so no new root deduction and no source support lost. Raw four rank-two learned packets are positive triangle penalties; all raw positive coefficients and those triangles have the same sign, and the interaction graph remains 24 vertices/96 edges, connected and simple, hence genus at least five and residual cycle dimension at least ten. The fifth rank-seven packet has degree eight and 99 unique high masks; assigning it positive weight cannot produce a pair energy. \section{DR21: Degree conservation under adaptive affine feedback}\label{sec:dr21}
\paragraph{Status.} PROVED scoped, independent review pending. This links DA21 (Lemmas~\ref{lem:da21-span}, \ref{lem:da21-close}), BW21 source quotient, DA16 degree transfer and DR16 guard weakening. It attacks U-PROGRESS rather than claiming that one more fixed-degree terminal gives universal coverage.
\begin{lemma}[Affine feedback does not reset proof degree]\label{lem:dr21-degree}
In a common original Boolean polynomial ring over $\mathbb F_2$, let source equations have reduced degree at most $d$, and start with actual consistent affine guard axioms. Fix $k\ge0$ and $D\ge\max(1,d+k)$. Allow any sequence of Gaussian affine parametrizations of the current guard, exact linear-span relaxations as in Lemma~\ref{lem:da21-close} using restricted source equations multiplied by polynomials of degree at most $k$, and addition of the resulting necessary affine equations. Previously proved degree-at-most-$d$ equations may also be used; every other accepted rule must have an independent degree-$D$ derivation from the current premises. Then all acquired affine equations and any final contradiction have BPC derivations of degree at most $D$ from the original source and the initial guard, regardless of the number of feedback rounds or accumulated rank. This does not cover nonlinear decoding or extension coordinates, independently supplied high-degree expressions, or semantic deductions without the stated degree lift.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For a pass let $p_j$ be the supplied products on the actual chart. The exact evaluation span $E$ includes their outputs, the constant and the chart coordinates. If its affine relaxation is empty, the constant functional vanishes on the kernel of projection to the $p_j$ coordinates of $E$. If the relaxation is nonempty and an affine form $L$ vanishes on it, choose an element of that kernel with constant coordinate one. Adding it to any element of the kernel with constant zero shows that the functional $L$ also vanishes there. Thus in either case the desired affine form (or constant one) factors linearly through the product outputs; there is an identity $L=\sum_j a_jp_j$ on the chart. This is linear algebra, not a semantic support oracle.

Write the current guard in Gaussian solved form $x_i=h_i(y)$ with free original coordinates $y$ and affine $h_i$. For any polynomial $p$ of reduced degree at most $D$, the difference between $p$ and its substitution normal form is a sum of $(x_i+h_i(y))$ times polynomials of degree at most $D-1$: replace pivots one at a time and telescope each monomial. All intermediate reduced degrees are at most $D$. Thus the difference is derivable from the current affine equations by additions and variable multiplications, with Boolean reductions. Any other affine chart is related to $y$ by affine maps, so its polynomial multiplier degrees do not increase when lifted. Multiply original equations by the lifted multipliers at degree at most $d+k$, combine, then use the telescoping identity for the difference from $L$. This yields a derivation in the original ring. The equality as functions on the free cube implies equality of their unique multilinear representatives. Induct on passes: previously acquired affine equations are derived lines, not free axioms. Singleton rank-one closure on the bounded-degree owner polynomials is included; inconsistent acquired affine equations yield $1$ by Gaussian elimination. This proves the bound even if the final guard rank is much larger than its initial rank.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Consequences and constructive dispatch.}
Conditional on independent review of the existing degree-hard family in Lemma~\ref{lem:da16-transfer}, fixed-degree multiplication of the raw signed NAE equations ($d=2$) and unrestricted affine feedback cannot refute every input. More strongly, a DR16 guard-weakening DAG using these leaf procedures with initial node guard rank at most $r$ has degree at most $D+r$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:dr16-dag}; hence on that family $D+r=\Omega(n)$. Learned guard equations do not need to be charged as additional free assumptions, precisely because their proofs are retained. No unrestricted SAT lower bound follows.

A constructive alternative within the fixed-cap domain is the complete degree-$D$ saturation from DA16, which absorbs nonlinear as well as affine derived equations. Maintain the span in the squarefree monomials of degree at most $D$; for each variable take the entire linear multiplication image, eliminate coordinates of degree exceeding $D$, and add the resulting intersection with the degree-$D$ space. Multiplying only individually low-degree basis rows need not suffice. Each strict insertion increases dimension; for fixed $D$ there are polynomially many monomials of degree at most $D+1$ (enumerate bounded-cardinality subsets), image computations and Gaussian operations, including explicit derivation provenance. Extract necessary affine rows, reclose after accepted deductions and at stagnation, and return UNSAT on deriving $1$; return SAT only with a verified source witness, otherwise decline. Under a fixed original-$N$ cap this is a paid polynomial job with polynomial peak space on the same serial realization and $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$, not a bound for the whole cooperative recursion. It does not replace DA21's factored high-degree path on the BS20 chain or supply a universal proof lift for matching, wheels or nonaffine transformations.

\section{I27: Exact character-energy defects and chart-invariant matching obstruction}\label{sec:i27}
\paragraph{Status.} PROVED scoped, independent review pending. Attacks Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} via M27's positive energy, DA21's feedback equations, BW21's native quotient, and the same RT26 controls. No universal normalization or unrestricted resource claim.
\begin{lemma}[Exact weighted defect domain and zero-offset certificate]\label{lem:i27-defect}
On an authenticated affine chart, expand mandatory violation indicators with positive rational weights and optional authenticated violations with nonnegative weights, subject to a fixed original-input polynomial expansion and bit-length cap. Merge identical character masks, absorb affine translations and constants, and write $E(y)=c+\sum_{j=1}^t a_j(-1)^{v_j^Ty}$ with distinct nonzero masks and nonzero coefficients. Put $A=[v_1,\ldots,v_t]$, $p_j=[a_j>0]$, $w_j=2|a_j|$, $B=c-\sum_j|a_j|$. For $H$ whose rows are a basis of $\ker A$, the exact minimum energy is
\[
 B+\min_{Hz=Hp}\sum_j w_j z_j.
\]
If $B>0$ the source is UNSAT. If $B=0$, the source is SAT iff $Hp=0$, with a Gaussian witness. This is a polynomial terminal regardless of syndrome rank.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The energy is nonnegative and zero exactly at source models in the authenticated chart. Set $z=A^Ty+p$. Each character term contributes $-|a_j|+w_jz_j$. Since $\ker H=\operatorname{im}A^T$, the displayed syndrome domain is exact in both directions, and any returned defect word lifts by solving $A^Ty=z+p$ and then applying the authenticated chart map. Strictly positive weights give the zero-offset criterion. The case $B<0$ requires an exact budget consumer and is not resolved by Gaussian elimination alone. All coefficient aggregation and arithmetic is charged to the explicit cap. No count-preservation claim.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Exact direct graph-parity criterion and affine invariance]\label{lem:i27-cographic}
A graph incidence matrix on the same defect coordinates can replace $H$ without loss or extra syndrome iff the column matroid of $H$ is graphic, equivalently the column matroid of $A$ is cographic. Recognition, realization and weighted T-join consumption are polynomial from the explicit matrix. This condition is invariant under any surjective affine reparameterization of the whole chart. In particular for a raw linear signed NAE3 registry with positive mandatory weights and no additional terms, this direct adapter is available iff its primal interaction graph is planar, even after arbitrary invertible affine coordinate changes or redundant surjective affine lifts.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The binary dual matroid is represented by $H$. Labelled binary representations of the same matroid have the same kernel (circuit indicators generate the binary kernel), hence the same rowspace. A graphic realization of the explicit binary matrix can be acquired by row-reducing to $[I\mid D]$ and applying Bixby--Wagner tree-path realization to $D$; add the corresponding non-tree edges and verify rowspace equality, with zero columns represented by loops. Components may be joined at a vertex without changing the cycle space. The exact syndrome becomes a weighted T-join with odd vertices given by incidence times $p$. Nonnegative weights permit shortest paths followed by minimum-weight perfect matching of the odd vertices, XORing their paths; solve for and verify the source witness. If recognition fails, the adapter declines, not UNSAT. This is the criterion for this direct fixed-coordinate graph parity representation, not for all graph reductions. Under a surjective affine map $y=u+Lx$, the pullback $L^T$ is injective and preserves all mask dependencies, while translations only change signs. On a raw linear NAE3 registry each primal pair occurs once, so all its nonzero Fourier pair masks survive positive weights. The resulting column matroid is precisely the primal graphic matroid. Whitney's planarity criterion gives the iff. Fano and its single-sign neighbors have primal $K_7$ and therefore fail this direct adapter in every such chart. Non-surjective certified quotients, additional coefficient cancellation, existential nonlinear lifts and other solvers are not excluded.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Same-residual joint certificate.} RT26 immutable registry \href{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/85e959ac861572a2411b9858da0d58d7c72ac780}{85e959ac}, DA21 actual feedback cuts \href{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/6d9917749c8438435d889b31e5c81ed0fc410e9a}{6d991774}, BW21 quotient \href{https://github.com/j15marti/pnp/commit/cbb0e2c61e3114ca9ba20a36f09018380724949d}{cbb0e2c6}. \section{DS21: Affine character minimum elimination and a dense-rank obstruction}\label{sec:ds21}
\paragraph{Status.} PROVED scoped, independent review pending. Integrates I27 signed character energy with DA21 actual affine feedback, BW21 reclosure and DR21 degree firewall. Attacks Obligation~\ref{obl:progress}; no universal claim.
\begin{lemma}[Exact minimum over one affine direction]\label{lem:ds21-min}
Let an authenticated chart have explicitly represented nonnegative rational energy $E(x)=\sum_a c_a\chi_a(x)$ whose zero set is its feasible set, with exact witness maps and actual guards absorbed. Choose a nonzero free direction $d$ and coordinate $p$ with $d_p=1$. On representatives $y_p=0$ write $E(y+td)=A(y)+(-1)^tB(y)$. If the set of present masks odd on $d$ is nonempty, let $r$ be the rank of its pair differences; otherwise set $r=0$. The exact projected energy is
\[
 E'(y)=\min_{t\in\{0,1\}}E(y+td)=A(y)-|B(y)|.
\]
It is nonnegative and its zeros lift by choosing $t=1$ iff $B(y)>0$. The new absolute-value term has at most $2^r$ Fourier coefficients (zero if $B=0$). For a fixed original-input polynomial support cap and supplied direction with $r\le C\log_2(N+2)$, this is a paid polynomial transformation. For each fixed integer $k$, complete discovery of an eligible odd-mask pattern with $r\le k$ is polynomial, including a polynomial support-count gate.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Choose an odd mask $a_0$. Then $B=\chi_{a_0}\sum_{a\ {\rm odd}}c_a\chi_{a+a_0}$; the first factor vanishes from the absolute value. Pair differences lie in $d^\perp$ and restriction to $y_p=0$ is injective on $d^\perp$. Row-reduce their span, evaluate the inner function on all $2^r$ independent observation words and Walsh transform its absolute values. Merge the resulting coefficients with the even terms, retaining exact signed rational coefficients; positivity of individual packets is no longer required. If no odd mask, the direction is invisible. Minimization and reverse reconstruction prove both SAT directions pointwise, not count preservation.
For fixed $k$, enumerate the affine hulls of at most $k+1$ present nonzero masks. For each hull $L$, solve the linear system prescribing $d^Ta=1$ for every present mask in $L$ and zero for the others. Every nonempty odd set of rank at most $k$ is the intersection of the present support with its affine hull, since every point of this hull is odd. Also test the common kernel for a nonzero invisible direction. Each feasible pattern determines the even masks and odd differences before coordinate restriction, all in $d^\perp$; their distinctness and coefficient cancellations after restriction are unchanged for every realizing direction. Thus one Gaussian solution per pattern suffices for the support-count gate. Failed trials are charged. This proves fixed-rank discovery, not complete logarithmic-rank dense discovery. For coordinate trials logarithmic rank suffices by direct enumeration of coordinates.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Aggregate ledger.}
Each accepted projection decreases the free dimension by one. In a stand-alone run with fixed original-$N$ support and observation-table caps, at most $n$ accepted steps and a polynomial number of trials per step are needed; retain minimizing maps and original source verification. A common rational denominator is initially of polynomial bit length; multiplying it by $2^r$ at each transform and bounding numerator growth by a factor polynomial in support and $2^r$ per step preserves polynomial bit length. Thus serial $T,S$ are polynomial on the same scoped run, and cumulative live storage is at most $(T+1)S$. Charge failed attempts and reverse maps; do not reset portfolio reserve when switching representations. Certified rank-zero/one packet closure before energy compilation and after imported cuts; once projected, old packet constraints are no longer free constraints on survivors. Reapply I27 offset test and other proved applicable energy deductions at each step and stagnation. A declined state is exact but OPEN, not a universal terminal.
\begin{lemma}[Complete-pair opposite-label obstruction]\label{lem:ds21-clique}
For an energy on $n$ Boolean coordinates whose nonconstant support is exactly all pair masks $e_i+e_j$, every direction other than zero or the all-one invisible direction has odd-mask affine rank $n-2$. The statement is invariant under invertible coordinate changes and removing the invisible gauge. There are unbounded SAT and UNSAT signed linear NAE3 registries with exactly this support and with negative I27 offset.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
A nontrivial direction splits coordinates into nonempty $A,B$. Its odd masks are exactly crossing edges. Differences of crossing edges sharing one endpoint generate the even parity subspace on each part, and every difference belongs to their direct sum, of dimension $|A|-1+|B|-1=n-2$. Invertible changes preserve the rank; gauge removal is injective on the span of visible masks. For $n=2^\ell-1$, $\ell\ge3$, take nonzero vectors in $\mathbb F_2^\ell$ and the distinct triples $\{a,b,a+b\}$. Every pair occurs once. All-positive NAE contains a Fano subsystem; satisfaction of seven Fano owners requires 14 crossing pairs in $K_7$, exceeding its maximum cut 12. With one negative literal per owner the all-zero word satisfies the entire registry. In both cases scaled energy $4E$ has constant $m$ and $3m$ pair coefficients of unit magnitude, hence offset $-2m$. No fixed-rank dense selection plus offset-only terminal covers these unchanged charts. Other algorithms, necessary non-surjective guards, new energy factors, and factored high-rank absolute values are not excluded; these labels themselves are easy.
\end{proof}

\section{BD21: Signed-character min-plus quotient and paid sparse-direction discovery}\label{sec:bd21}
\paragraph{Status.} PROVED scoped, independent review pending. Attacks Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} by combining I27 defect energy, M27 matching, DA21 guard feedback and multisign cancellation. It preserves minimum energy and a minimizing witness, not counts or full exterior support.
\begin{lemma}[Exact sparse and dominant affine-direction elimination]\label{lem:bd21-min}
On an authenticated free affine chart, let $E(y)=c+\sum_{j=1}^t a_j\chi_{v_j}(y)$ be a rational nonnegative energy with zero exactly at source models, with distinct nonzero masks and nonzero coefficients. For a nonzero direction $q$, put $J=\{j:v_j^Tq=1\}$, $k=|J|$, and choose a linear complement $U$ of $\langle q\rangle$. There is an exact quotient on $U$ with no increase in the number of nonconstant characters whenever $1\le k\le3$, or whenever some $i\in J$ satisfies $|a_i|\ge\sum_{j\in J\setminus\{i\}}|a_j|$. The quotient preserves minimum energy and has a polynomial-time minimizing-witness lift. A direction with $1\le k\le3$ is deterministically discoverable, or its absence certified, in polynomial work from the explicit masks.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Write $E(u+bq)=C(u)+(-1)^b L(u)$, where $L=\sum_{j\in J}a_j\chi_{v_j}$ and $C$ includes the unchanged terms and constant. Exact existential minimization gives $C-|L|$. For $k\le3$, factor out $\chi_{v_i}$ for any $i\in J$ and expand $|\ a_i+\sum_{j\ne i}a_j\chi_{v_j+v_i}\ |$ by its Walsh truth table in $k-1$ formal signs. There are at most $2^{k-1}-1\le k$ nonconstant terms, even when the relative masks are dependent. All relative masks annihilate $q$. In the dominant case, including ties, $|L|=|a_i|+\operatorname{sgn}(a_i)\sum_{j\in J\setminus\{i\}}a_j\chi_{v_j+v_i}$, with at most $k-1$ nonconstant terms. Restrict unchanged and relative masks to $U$, merge duplicates, and drop zero coefficients. For any minimizing exterior word, choose $b=1$ iff $L(u)>0$, with either choice allowed when zero. This is an existential lift, not an unconditional forced equation. Enumerate all nonempty supports $S$ of size at most three and solve the linear system $A^Tq=1_S$, where $A$ has the actual masks as columns; any solution is nonzero. There are $O(t^3)$ systems, and each solve and verification is polynomial. Kernel directions are redundant gauges, removable by Gaussian elimination. Arbitrary high-fanout dominance need not be discoverable universally: test only a fixed polynomial list of directions and charge all failures.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Polynomial serial quotient reserve and restricted obstruction]\label{lem:bd21-reserve}
With a fixed original-$N$ polynomial cap on the initial explicit energy and rational bit lengths, repeatedly executing Lemma~\ref{lem:bd21-min} and I27's $B\ge0$ terminal is a polynomial-time and polynomial-space exact partial solver. It may decline. The raw Fano NAE chart and every single-sign neighbor decline under this move family even allowing arbitrary affine coordinate changes. There are infinite connected examples of both labels with the same obstruction.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every accepted quotient reduces free dimension by one and never increases the nonconstant term count. A common denominator initially has polynomial bit length; each small Walsh step multiplies it by at most four. The rational coefficient norm can grow by at most a constant factor per small step and does not grow under dominance; thus all bit lengths and all lift logs are polynomial after at most $n$ moves. Discovery, all unsuccessful supports, energy aggregation, offset checks and witness verification are paid; same-realization CM is bounded by $(T+1)S$. \section{MS28: Collective syndrome-budget cancellation}\label{sec:ms28}

\begin{lemma}[Odd-check packing and zero-budget feedback]\label{lem:ms28-pack}
On an authenticated affine chart with nonnegative violation energy $E=B+\sum_j w_jz_j$, $w_j>0$, and $z_j=v_j^Ty+p_j$ over $\mathbb F_2$, let $\mathcal C$ consist of sets of distinct defect coordinates satisfying $\sum_{j\in C}v_j=0$, $\sum_{j\in C}p_j=1$ over $\mathbb F_2$. Any rational nonnegative packing with loads $l_j=\sum_{C\ni j}\lambda_C\le w_j$ certifies
\[
E\ge B+\sum_C\lambda_C.
\]
A positive lower bound certifies UNSAT. If it is zero, each actual source model obeys $z_j=0$ whenever $l_j<w_j$, and $\sum_{j\in C}z_j=1$ as an integer equation whenever $\lambda_C>0$. These deductions retain the actual chart guard; the former are authenticated affine cuts and the latter can be passed to the integer-lattice channel.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every odd check has at least one defect, so each term on the right of
\[
 E=B+\sum_C\lambda_C+\sum_C\lambda_C\left(\sum_{j\in C}z_j-1\right)+\sum_j(w_j-l_j)z_j
\]
after the constant is nonnegative. At zero energy and zero constant, every positively weighted summand must vanish. No converse is inferred from integer or fractional feasibility. For fixed maximum check size $k$, enumerate $O(t^k)$ sets of the $t$ explicit masks, check XOR conditions, and solve a rational packing LP. Polynomial-bit exact LP gives a uniform polynomial acquisition and exact verification bound under the original-input cap on masks and coefficient sizes. Integer equality consistency is polynomial by normal forms, or modular inconsistency suffices for rejection. If only independent affine equations are inserted into the same chart, at most $n$ productive feedback passes and one final unsuccessful pass are required; any new integer registry, consumers and nonlinear transformations must be separately capped and charged. Include failed discoveries, rational arithmetic, verification, guard transport, reconstruction, simultaneous old/new storage and provenance. Polynomial serial $T,S$ on this domain imply $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$. No aggregate bound for arbitrary scope changes or branching is inferred.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[All-redundant-check unary-marginal obstruction]\label{lem:ms28-allchecks}
Every raw linear signed NAE-3 registry with incidence girth at least eight passes the zero-budget relaxation consisting of the convex hull of each individual redundant parity check, identified on shared unary defect marginals. Even restricting each local check table to its maximal support on that zero-budget face and allowing signed integer masses does not give a root contradiction. The statement permits all redundant checks, not just bounded-length checks, but does not include joint higher-order marginal constraints between checks.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Each primal pair occurs only once and each primal triangle is an original owner: a triangle using three distinct owners would create a length-six incidence cycle, and two edges of one owner already determine the third pair. The raw scaled energy $4E$ has $3m$ distinct pair masks, weights two and offset $-2m$. A nonempty zero-XOR mask set has size at least three; those of size three are exactly owner triangles, with odd preferred parity since the three coefficient signs multiply to $+1$. Set each marginal $z_j=1/3$. Each owner triangle admits the uniform exactly-one distribution; every check of length $k\ge4$ has $k/3$ strictly between the minimum and maximum permitted Hamming weights for either parity. By mixing a sufficiently small positive uniform distribution over permitted words with a symmetric endpoint mixture one obtains positive mass on every permitted word at this marginal. Thus all checks are feasible at zero budget; the only local support restrictions are the one-hot triangles (their odd parity and mean sum one exclude weight three).

Take any actual source word, not necessarily satisfying, and its binary defect word $b$. Within each edge-disjoint owner triangle the sum is odd. When it is three, subtract two from one of its coordinates, yielding an integer vector $z'$ with every owner sum one and $z'\equiv b\bmod2$. For a parity table of length $k\ge3$, its integer affine hull is precisely the lattice coset of integer vectors of the specified total parity: differences generate $e_i-e_j$ and $e_i+e_j$ by choosing parity-correct words differing in those two coordinates, and these differences generate the even-total lattice. The one-hot triangle integer hull is exactly total sum one. Consequently $z'$ lifts independently into signed masses of total one on each maximal-support check table, sharing exactly the unary marginals $z'$. Its energy is zero. Thus neither this full local LP nor the signed-integer maximal-support refinement universally rejects raw high-girth UNSAT registries. This does not address arbitrary higher-order overlaps, PSD, conditioning, nonaffine transforms or unrestricted algorithms. The construction itself needs no assertion about the acquisition cost of an exponentially large all-check table.
\end{proof}

\section{BA21: Exact magnitude-spectrum min-plus normalization}\label{sec:ba21}
We address DS21/BD21's high-rank absolute-value acquisition gap in the same authenticated energy chart. The integer violation count of a 3-CNF has a sparse Walsh expansion with at most eight terms per clause before merging; its range is $[0,m]$. An affine guard parameterization and exact existential minimization retain the integer range. The NAE implementation uses four times the violation count.
\begin{lemma}[Bounded-magnitude exact quotient without rank restriction]\label{lem:ba21-moment}
Let $E$ be an explicitly represented sparse rational Walsh polynomial taking integer values in $[0,M]$, with $M$ bounded by a fixed polynomial in original input length $N$. In the section of any supplied nonzero affine direction write $E(y,z)=A(y)+(-1)^zB(y)$. For each fixed $K$, it is decidable in polynomial bit time whether $|2B|$ has at most $K$ distinct values. If so one can construct the exact sparse polynomial $\min_z E=A-|B|$ in polynomial time, regardless of the rank of the odd-mask differences. The output need not have nonincreasing support.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Let $X=(2B)^2$ and $m_j=\mathbb E_y X^j$ under the uniform section. Sparse XOR convolution constructs $X^i$ for $0\le i\le K$; by orthogonality $m_{i+j}$ is the dot product of the coefficient vectors of $X^i,X^j$. For $r=1,\ldots,K$, solve the rational Hankel system $(m_{i+j})_{0\le i,j<r}c=-(m_r,\ldots,m_{2r-1})^T$. This Gram matrix is positive definite when the number of distinct values of $X$ is at least $r$, since a nonzero polynomial of degree below $r$ cannot vanish at those distinct points. Test whether $P(X)=X^r+\sum_{i<r}c_iX^i$ has squared mean zero using these moments. Nonnegativity and full support of the finite uniform measure make this an exact identity test. The first successful $r$ equals the number of distinct values; if none succeeds by $K$, decline. The actual values of $|2B|=|E(y,0)-E(y,1)|$ are integers in $[0,M]$. Scan this polynomial range for the roots $j^2$ of $P$; exactly $r$ distinct roots are obtained. Interpolate the unique degree-at-most-$r-1$ rational polynomial $Q$ with $Q(j^2)=j$ at them. Then $Q(X)=|2B|$ pointwise and $A-Q(X)/2$ is the exact minimum. A minimizing bit is $z=1$ iff $B>0$, with either bit allowed at zero. This is a witness lift, not a necessary affine equation.

With $t$ input masks, powers through $K$ use at most $O((t+1)^{2K})$ terms before merging; intermediate coefficient bit lengths and fixed-size rational Gaussian solves are polynomial. The output has $O(t+(t+1)^{2K-2})$ terms. Canonical coefficients of any subsequent integer-valued energy on $d$ bits are multiples of $2^{-d}$ bounded in absolute value by $M$, so normalized bit sizes are bounded by $O(d+\log(M+1))$ throughout. An implementation using common integer denominator $D$ may instead take $X=(2B_{\rm num})^2$ and roots $(jD)^2$, with interpolation values $jD$. No exhaustive assignment acquisition is used by this argument.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Original-input reserve and strict rank-independent separation]\label{lem:ba21-reserve}
Under a fixed original-$N$ polynomial cap on all intermediate sparse maps, a polynomially enumerated candidate direction list (e.g. current coordinates) each round, and fixed $K$, the preceding quotient is a paid single-child contraction with $\mu=1+$ remaining dimension. It can handle high-fanout, nondominant odd masks of arbitrarily large affine difference rank.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Charge all candidate probes, failed capped convolutions, moment solves, discovery, canonicalization, guard transport and verification; stop before exceeding cap. A successful move eliminates one dimension and requires only polynomial reverse logs. On a nonnegative chart the offset lower bound and zero-offset preferred-parity Gaussian check (I27) may decide before a quotient; otherwise decline if no eligible move is found. Reclose certified unconditional information initially, after actual accepted necessary cuts and at stagnation; minimizing bits remain conditional on the future quotient word. The original source is verified on any reconstructed zero-energy word. Under the caps, at most $n$ successful moves and polynomially many attempts imply polynomial $T,S$ on the same serial realization, hence $\mathrm{CM}\le(T+1)S$. Universal eligibility is not established.

For a separation, let $a$ be $k$ address bits, $s=2^k$, and $d_i$ independent data bits. Put $B=s(-1)^{d_a}=\sum_{i,u\in\mathbb F_2^k}(-1)^{i\cdot u}\chi_{u(a)+d_i}$ (the notation $\chi$ denotes a character, the data and address masks are on disjoint coordinates). All $s^2$ coefficients have absolute value one and the affine difference rank is $s-1+k$. For $s\ge2$, no coefficient dominates. Nevertheless $|B|=s$ and the $z$-direction quotient of $E=s+\chi_zB$ is identically zero; adding one gives the opposite decision. This is a sparse-energy separation, not an asserted strict physical adapter. Sanyal's address-function sparsity/dimension result provides context (\href{https://theoryofcomputing.org/articles/v015a011/}{Theory of Computing 15(11), 2019}); classical elimination context: Dechter (\href{https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.3572}{arXiv:1302.3572}).
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Exact chosen-direction Walsh blowup]\label{lem:ba21-blowup}
For even $d\ge2$ and independent characters $\chi_i$, $B=\sum_{i=1}^d\chi_i$ has $d/2+1$ absolute magnitudes, and $|B|$ has exactly $2^{d-1}$ nonzero Walsh coefficients. Thus the exact $z$-quotient of $d+\chi_z B$ can have exponentially many explicit masks despite a sparse source.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Odd coefficients vanish under global complement; the constant is positive. For each even nonempty subset $S$ of size $\ell$, the integral identity $|v|=(2/\pi)\int_0^\infty(1-\cos(tv))t^{-2}\,dt$ and independent uniform signs give its coefficient as
\[
-\frac{2}{\pi}(-1)^{\ell/2}\int_0^\infty \sin^\ell(t)\cos^{d-\ell}(t)t^{-2}\,dt .
\]
Finite averaging commutes with the integral; the integrand is nonnegative, integrable and positive on an open interval, hence every such coefficient is nonzero. This counts all even subsets. This example is easy via I27's zero-offset terminal; it refutes universal cheap explicit elimination in a prescribed direction, not every direction, a factored consumer, the cooperative portfolio, or unrestricted polynomial decision.
\end{proof}

\section{DP22: Guarded integer-field frontier quotient and all-direction magnitude barrier}\label{sec:dp22}
\paragraph{Status.} PROVED scoped, independent review pending. Integrates I27 quadratic energy, DA21 actual affine cuts, DS21/BD21/BA21 min-plus normalization and DP18 aggregate credit. No universal claim.
\begin{lemma}[Exact field--syndrome quotient]\label{lem:dp22-field}
Let $E=C+\sum_i h_i s_i+\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}s_i s_j$, $s_i=(-1)^{x_i}$, be an authenticated nonnegative integer energy with zero set the source models under actual guard $Gx=b$. For a prefix $A$ of a supplied order, with suffix $B$, keep for each key $(f,p)=(J_{BA}s_A,G_Ax_A)$ one assignment of minimum internal energy and its witness. Discard $p$ unless $b+p\in\operatorname{im}G_B$. The resulting sequential min-plus recurrence preserves the exact guarded minimum and a minimizing witness. If $|J_{ij}|\le W$, the number of keys at a cut is at most
\[
(2nW+1)^{r}2^{g},\qquad
r=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}J_{BA},\quad
g=\dim_{\mathbb F_2}(\operatorname{im}G_A\cap\operatorname{im}G_B).
\]
The same key is sufficient on a supplied binary decomposition tree; two child tables can be joined using at most the product of their sizes.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For any suffix assignment the cross energy is $s_B^Tf$ and the guard requires $G_Bx_B=b+p$, so identical keys permit retaining the lower internal cost. On adding variable $i$, increment cost by $s_i(h_i+f_i)$, delete $f_i$, add $J_{B',i}s_i$ to the residual field, and add $G_i x_i$ to the syndrome. This gives exact induction and a source witness. For a binary tree, child internal costs add with the cross term computed on their stored witnesses; replacing either by an equal-key witness preserves cross energy with every assignment outside that child, hence the pair minimum and parent key are unaffected. Independent rows of the integer cut matrix determine all field entries, and each of their $r$ integer values lies in $[-nW,nW]$. The feasible syndromes lie in $\operatorname{im}G_A\cap(b+\operatorname{im}G_B)$, empty or an affine coset of the stated intersection. This proves the bound. No complete semantic merging or support acquisition is assumed.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Aggregate ledger.} With an original-$N$ polynomial cap $P$ on actual acquired keys per layer, a fixed order has at most $2nP$ transitions (stop immediately on exceeding the cap); use deterministic ordered maps, exact syndrome membership, polynomial-bit arithmetic and witness copies.
