Fixed $r$, polynomial numerical $W$ and $g=O(\log N)$ suffice; binary-encoded exponentially large weights do not satisfy the numerical bound but can still pass the actual key cap. \begin{lemma}[All-direction magnitude barrier with field bypass]\label{lem:dp22-magnitude}
On an unguarded complete-pair spin energy with every pair coefficient of magnitude one, every non-invisible affine direction has $\Omega(n)$ distinct absolute odd-part magnitudes. Thus no fixed BA21 magnitude cap, DS21 fixed affine rank cap, or BD21 sparse/dominance rule covers all such unchanged charts. Uniform complete-pair weights nevertheless have rational cut rank one for every order.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
A nontrivial direction toggles the crossing pairs of a cut $(A,B)$, $1\le |A|\le|B|$. For independent uniform spins on $A$, each field $f_j=\sum_{i\in A}J_{ji}s_i$ is nonzero with probability at least one half: odd sums cannot vanish; for positive even size the central binomial probability is at most one half. Some word has $t\ge |B|/2$ nonzero fields. Starting with anti-aligned suffix spins, flip these $t$ spins one at a time to get $t+1$ strictly increasing values of the odd-part sum, hence at least $\lceil(t+1)/2\rceil$ different magnitudes. Passing to any affine section preserves the set of absolute values because moving along the direction negates the odd part. DS21 supplies the rank $n-2$ and BD21 is excluded for sufficiently large $n$ by cut size and unit coefficients. The uniform matrix has constant entries, rank one. DS21's projective Steiner families furnish both source labels; the all-positive family has the rank-one bypass, while arbitrary signs need not. This excludes a move family, not all algorithms or non-surjective guard deductions.
\end{proof}

\section{RT27: All-direction magnitude and explicit Walsh obstruction}\label{sec:rt27}
\begin{lemma}[All-direction obstruction to fixed-spectrum normalization]\label{lem:rt27-spectrum}
For $n=2^k-1$, $k\ge3$, use the triples $\{a,b,a+b\}$ on nonzero vectors of $\mathbb F_2^k$, with arbitrary literal signs per owner. Each pair occurs once. The scaled violation count $Q=4E=m+\sum_{i<j}\sigma_{ij}s_i s_j$, $s_i=(-1)^{x_i}$, $|\sigma_{ij}|=1$, $m=n(n-1)/6$. In every nonglobal-complement nonzero affine direction the odd term $B$ has at least $\lceil n/8\rceil$ distinct absolute magnitudes. This is invariant under invertible affine recharts and global-complement gauge quotient.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The direction defines a nontrivial cut $(S,T)$, where $q=|T|\ge n/2$ after swapping sides. Its odd term is $B=\sum_{i\in S,j\in T}\sigma_{ij}s_i s_j$. Uniform spins on $S$ give each $w_j=\sum_{i\in S}\sigma_{ij}s_i$ a probability at least $1/2$ of being nonzero by conditioning on all but one spin. Some $S$ assignment has $t\ge\lceil q/2\rceil$ nonzero weights. Flipping the corresponding $T$ spins successively from all negative to all positive contributions gives $t+1$ strictly increasing sums. Absolute value identifies at most two, proving the bound. The absolute odd term is independent of the choice of representative of each direction orbit and is gauge invariant. Thus BA21's fixed-$K$ criterion fails for every nongauge direction when $n>8K$. BD21's crossing support is at least $n-1$, with equal absolute coefficients and no dominance. DS21's odd-mask affine-difference rank is $n-2$ (differences span the even subsets within each side). I27's offset is $-2m$. Raw singleton closure fixes nothing. No claim for nonsurjective guards or stronger prior cuts.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[All-direction explicit Walsh blowup]\label{lem:rt27-blowup}
For the unsigned subfamily every nongauge single-direction exact minimized energy has at least $2^{q-1}-1-\binom n2$ nonzero Walsh coefficients, where $q$ is the larger cut side size.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Here $B=(\sum_S s_i)(\sum_T s_j)$. In a section fixing one $S$ spin, restrict the remaining $S$ spins to $+1$. The absolute odd term reduces to $|S||\sum_T s_j|$. For even $q$, Lemma~\ref{lem:ba21-blowup} gives every even coefficient nonzero. For odd $q$, average the even-$q+1$ absolute sum over the extra spin: $\frac12(|v+1|+|v-1|)=|v|$ for odd integer $v$, retaining all even coefficients not using that spin. Restriction cannot increase support. Subtracting from the quadratic $A$ cancels at most $1+\binom n2$ coefficients. Affine bijections on the quotient preserve support size; the gauge invariant coefficients survive its exact quotient. Input length $O(n^2\log n)$, hence explicit materialization exceeds every fixed original-input polynomial cap. The factored expression remains compact, so this is not unrestricted hardness. Indeed $Q=m+((\sum s_i)^2-n)/2>0$ for unsigned $n\ge7$, a simple polynomial refutation.
\end{proof}
\paragraph{Opposite-label controls.} Keep the seven unsigned Fano owners on a 3-dimensional subspace. Flip one literal in one of them; a fixed satisfying Fano word extends to the larger registry by choosing the other owner signs to accept it. The unchanged Fano root is UNSAT and the single-sign neighbor SAT. Both obey Lemma~\ref{lem:rt27-spectrum}; no signed exponential Walsh claim or criticality of every owner. A Fano scan is a polynomial escape for these roots. \section{BH21: Collective count normalization beyond every fixed magnitude cap}\label{sec:bh21}
We attack the universal eligibility question in Obligation~\ref{obl:progress} for BA21 and BD21, and connect DP01/S06 count aggregation to MS28 and BW21 actual energy/guard feedback. All claims below are scoped, independent review pending.

\begin{lemma}[Every-direction magnitude obstruction]\label{lem:bh21-spectrum}
Let a field-free quadratic spin energy be $E=C+\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}s_is_j$ with $s_i\in\{-1,1\}$ and every $J_{ij}\ne0$. Modulo the global complement kernel, every nonzero affine flip direction splits the coordinates into two nonempty sets $A,B$, with $|B|\ge |A|$ after interchange. In the section of that direction, the number of distinct magnitudes of $E(x)-E(x+q)$ is at least
\[
\left\lceil\frac{\lceil |B|/2\rceil+1}{2}\right\rceil.
\]
Thus no fixed BA21 magnitude cap is universally eligible on these raw full-support charts, even with arbitrary invertible affine reparameterization.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The difference is twice the crossing bilinear sum $\sum_{j\in B}s_j\sum_{i\in A}J_{ij}s_i$; its absolute value is constant on each flip orbit. For uniform independent $s_i$ in $A$, each inner sum is zero with probability at most $1/2$ by conditioning on all but one nonzero term. Hence some fixed $A$ word leaves $r\ge\lceil |B|/2\rceil$ nonzero coefficients. Start the remaining $s_j$ opposite to their respective coefficient signs, then reverse those $r$ spins successively. The sum strictly increases at each step, giving $r+1$ distinct real values. Absolute value identifies at most two of them. The count is invariant under a change of basis since a direction still corresponds to an actual flip and a section contains one point per orbit. This is not a claim about charts after arbitrary guards or nonlinear transformations.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Baseline-subtracted component count consumer]\label{lem:bh21-count}
For an explicit integer quadratic spin energy $E=C+\sum_i h_i s_i+\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}s_is_j$, try a baseline $\beta$ from zero and the distinct pair coefficients (including implicit zeros). Form the residual graph with edges $J_{ij}\ne\beta$. Let its connected components be $G_\ell$. For each, acquire the exact minimum local residual energy $D_\ell(t)$ subject to $\sum_{i\in G_\ell}s_i=t$, with one attaining word. This acquisition is polynomial if every component either has constant residual pair coefficient on all distinct pairs or has size at most $C_0\log_2(N+2)$ for a fixed $C_0$, where $N$ is original encoded input length. Then the global minimum and a genuine minimizing word are deterministically computable in polynomial time, irrespective of the number of components or the product of their count ranges.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Subtract the uniform baseline, using the identity
\[
E=C+\frac{\beta}{2}\bigl((\sum_i s_i)^2-n\bigr)+\sum_\ell\bigl[\sum_{i\in G_\ell}h_i s_i+\sum_{i<j\in G_\ell}(J_{ij}-\beta)s_is_j\bigr].
\]
For uniform residual coefficient $a_\ell$, the pair term is $a_\ell(t^2-|G_\ell|)/2$. For fixed number of negative spins, sorting local fields gives the minimizing linear term (select the largest fields for negative spins). For capped small components enumerate their words and retain the minimum for each count. Pins can be substituted before recognition, adding fields and constants. For the union of the first $j$ components, store $M_j(T)=\min_t[M_{j-1}(T-t)+D_j(t)]$, with $M_0(0)=0$ and infeasible entries infinite. There are at most $2n+1$ counts at any stage. Minimize $C+\beta(T^2-n)/2+M_k(T)$, and follow attaining pointers and local words. Counts only compress the baseline coupling; local residual terms are never discarded. Discovery tries at most $O(n^2)$ baselines, builds and checks components by matrix scans, and declines before any oversized nonuniform local enumeration. For each admitted trial there are $O(n^3)$ DP transitions and at most $n(N+2)^{C_0}$ enumerated words, each with polynomial verification. Integer bit lengths are polynomial by the original coefficient bounds and sums. Store polynomial tables and reverse logs; all failed trials, authenticated coefficient compilation, closure, accesses and final source verification are charged. This is a paid terminal, not a universal contraction claim. For a supplied verified bounded-rank integer baseline feature map, the same proof works with vector counts when the number of coordinates is fixed and their summed absolute ranges are polynomial in original $N$; discovery of that more general map is not asserted.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Opposite-label all-direction family.}
For $d\ge3$ use the nonzero words of $\mathbb F_2^d$, $n=2^d-1$, and triples $\{x,y,x+y\}$. Every pair belongs to one triple. In scaled energy $4E$ for NAE violation count, each owner contributes one plus three signed pair products; the sign products on each triangle equal $+1$. The monotone chart has $J_{ij}=+1$ and $C=n(n-1)/6$, so its exact minimum is $C-(n-1)/2=(n-1)(n-3)/6>0$. For the SAT chart, partition words by highest nonzero bit. Every triple has two members in its highest-bit class and one in a lower class. Negate the minority-class literal of each owner; all-zero is a source witness. Its coefficients are $+1$ within each highest-bit class and $-1$ between classes, because every pair occurs once. The preceding lemma automatically recognizes baseline $-1$ and uniform residual cliques of sizes $1,2,\ldots,2^{d-1}$. The naive count-box product $\prod_{i=0}^{d-1}(2^i+1)$ is superpolynomial in the explicit source size (which is polynomial in $n$), while the aggregate-count DP remains polynomial. Both labels defeat every fixed BA21 magnitude cap for sufficiently large $d$, and BD21 small-fanout/dominance on the raw chart, yet both admit this nonlocal bypass. The raw owner-local affine closure is stagnant: each signed NAE has full affine hull and full pair projections. These are opposite-label same-scope controls, not single-sign neighbors, not high-girth or bounded-degree families, and not a simultaneous obstruction to all available terminals. In particular the complete-graph monotone cut bound also rejects the UNSAT family. This shows why universal progress cannot be deduced from a fixed magnitude cap alone, and why failed magnitude probes should feed global structural consumers rather than branch immediately.

\section{S27: Simultaneous all-cut field and all-direction magnitude obstruction}\label{sec:s27}
\begin{lemma}[Adjacent labels with uniformly high original-coordinate cut rank]\label{lem:s27-cut}
For all sufficiently large $n=2^k-1$, signed projective Steiner NAE charts exist with opposite labels differing by one literal sign modulo whole-owner complement, such that for every disjoint $A,B$ of size at least $n/4$ the pair-energy matrix has $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}J_{BA}>\lfloor n/100\rfloor$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Each pair occurs once among the $m=n(n-1)/6$ triples. Independently sample each of four forbidden complementary classes uniformly, and independently sample a planted registry from the three classes accepting zero. The first is UNSAT except with probability at most $2^n(3/4)^m$, by first moment; the second is SAT. Replace owners by their planted versions in a fixed order. At any stage, a specified single crossing sign has probability at most $2/3$, and two specified crossing signs from one triple have probability at most $1/3\le(2/3)^2$, since two pair products determine its class. At most two edges per triple cross disjoint sets $A,B$. Independence across owners gives probability at most $(2/3)^{ab}$ for any specific $a$-by-$b$ cross matrix. The number of sign matrices of rank $j$ is at most $\binom aj\binom bj2^{j(a+b-j)}$: choose basis rows and pivot columns, whose entries determine all others. Put $r=\lfloor n/100\rfloor$. Union bounding ranks at most $r$, at most $3^n$ disjoint pairs, and $m+1$ stages gives
\[
(m+1)3^n(r+1)2^{n+rn}(2/3)^{n^2/16}=o(1).
\]
Here $\log_2(3/2)/16>1/100$. Thus there is a path with the high-rank property at every stage and opposite endpoint labels; a consecutive pair has opposite labels and differs by one forbidden class, hence one sign modulo whole-owner complement. Existence is not efficient discovery.
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Actual field-key and baseline barrier]\label{lem:s27-keys}
At a cut of rational rank $h$ with a consistent affine guard of rank $g$, full DP22 field-key acquisition with affine feasibility and equal-key min merging retains at least $2^{h-g}$ distinct field keys. On the S27 pair, every original-coordinate order or binary leaf decomposition has a cut requiring $2^{\Omega(n)}$ such keys if at most $n/4$ coordinates are pinned and remaining guard rank is at most $n/200$. Further, if $J=L+D$ off-diagonal with $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}L\le\lfloor n/100\rfloor$, the symmetric deviation graph of $D$ has no separator of size at most $n/4$ whose remaining components all have size at most $n/2$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
At least $2^{a-g}$ prefix words extend to a guard word. Every fiber of the real field map on Boolean words has at most $2^{a-h}$ members: fixing nonpivot input coordinates uniquely determines pivot values. Min merging preserves each attained key, hence the bound. A binary leaf tree has a node with between one third and two thirds of all free leaves (follow a largest child until below two thirds); orders have a midpoint. After the stated pins both sides contain at least $n/4$ original coordinates, so Lemma~\ref{lem:s27-cut} applies. For the baseline claim, take the union $A$ of separator components with size between $n/4$ and $n/2$ (one sufficiently large component or greedy accumulation of smaller ones). The remaining $B$ has size at least $n/4$. Then $D_{BA}=0$ contradicts the rank bound. In particular low-rank baseline deviations cannot universally have bounded treewidth, by the centroid-bag balanced-separator argument.
\end{proof}
RT27 already proves all nongauge directions on these raw charts exceed the fixed BA21 magnitude cap for large $n$, also excluding BD21 sparse/dominant and DS21 fixed-rank moves. Every raw NAE owner has full affine hull. Thus the same opposite-label family obstructs the union of these raw exact-representation strategies, including the DP22 full field tables and BH21 small-component baseline escape; it is not an unrestricted lower bound, not a proof about arbitrary affine recharts after nonlocal cuts, and not a counterexample to every alternative terminal. Explicit input length is $O(n^2\log n)$. Stronger MS28/DA21/DR21 deductions, zero-specific pruning, direct witnesses, nonforest geometry and implicit consumers remain legal. U-PROGRESS (lines 28--30), universal SEM/CLOSE and unconditional COST remain OPEN; capped declines cannot be interpreted as UNSAT.
